subject: Fix NPE when accepting backup changes that add groups (#17165)
body:
* Do not touch the active tab when reviewing a backup

The library being reviewed has no tab yet, so the active tab is another
library's or absent; its lookup threw and the review ended in an NPE.

* Keep a library without groups groupless when accepting a metadata change

A backup that adds groups to a library without groups produces a metadata
change whose original group root is null; installing that root threw and
the review ended in an NPE.

* Link the pull request in the changelog

* Forget injected test services after each backup review test

---------

subject: Remove Reflection, show action descriptions as tooltips, fix tooltips not showing first time run (#17200)
body:
* Show action descriptions as tooltips in menus

Menu items now show the action's long text (description plus status
message) as tooltip, installed on the menu row via public JavaFX API
instead of reflecting into ContextMenuContent. Tooltips repeating the
label are skipped, and the redundant descriptions of "Open file(s)" and
"Open folder(s)" are removed.

Closes https://github.com/JabRef/jabref/issues/9615

* Drop opens of com.sun.javafx.scene.control

ActionFactory no longer reflects into ContextMenuContent; the package is
still exported for direct compile-time use.

* Add changelog entry for first-open menu tooltip fix

* Dispose menu tooltip setup when an item is reconfigured

GuiPushToApplicationCommand reconfigures the same menu item whenever the
push target changes; without disposal, listeners piled up and the
previous action's tooltip could stay installed.

* Document missing menu tooltips in the macOS system menu bar

subject: Add jabkit git merge-driver for semantic .bib merges (#16838)
body:
* Add jabkit git merge-driver for semantic .bib merges

Exposes JabRef's three-way semantic merge (SemanticMergeAnalyzer +
GitMergeApplier) as a Git merge driver: `jabkit git merge-driver
BASE CURRENT OTHER` writes current + (other - base) into CURRENT,
exits 0 on a clean merge and 1 when semantic conflicts remain.

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01UpFy4JVhKFAFugkbTemRoA

* Link PR in CHANGELOG

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01UpFy4JVhKFAFugkbTemRoA

* Reject merges that would silently drop content

The semantic merge plan only covers entries with a citation key, so entry
type changes, @String definitions, preamble, epilogue, metadata and keyless
entries from OTHER never reached CURRENT while the driver reported success.
Type changes are now applied; the rest makes the driver report a conflict.

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_014xQwRqLx2R27m7xFYPfAdK

* Merge entry types three-way, compare persisted metadata

Entry types were only propagated when CURRENT kept BASE's type, so
divergent type changes, a type change against a deletion, and additions of
the same key with different types passed as clean merges. They are now
reported as conflicts. Metadata is compared in its serialized form, since
MetaData.equals ignores unknown metadata items.

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_014xQwRqLx2R27m7xFYPfAdK

* Keep merging around conflicting entries, fix dependency scope

Entries with a type conflict are removed from the merge plan instead of
discarding it, so safe changes of the other entries still reach CURRENT.
GitFileWriter aborts the atomic write when the encoding cannot represent
the content, which otherwise replaced the file with lossy content. jabkit
requires org.jspecify directly, and the merge-driver smoke test now checks
that the driver stays silent.

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_014xQwRqLx2R27m7xFYPfAdK

* Register EventBus subscriber for the native image

Applying the merge plan sets fields on entries that belong to a database,
which dispatches a FieldChangedEvent to BibDatabase via Guava's EventBus.
Its subscriber is invoked reflectively and thus failed in the native image.

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_014xQwRqLx2R27m7xFYPfAdK

* Register KeyChangeListener subscribers for the native image

Same reflective EventBus dispatch as the previous commit: applying the
merge plan reaches the listener that keeps cross-references in sync.

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_014xQwRqLx2R27m7xFYPfAdK

* Move the merge driver setup to the user documentation

The developer documentation keeps the contract and the limits of the
driver and links to the user documentation for the Git configuration.

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_014xQwRqLx2R27m7xFYPfAdK

* Preserve custom entry types, refuse unparseable input

Rewriting CURRENT dropped its custom entry type definitions, because the
writer got a fresh BibEntryTypesManager; it now gets the types parsed from
CURRENT. A file the parser reported a warning for (a duplicate @String name,
for instance) cannot be written back without loss and is refused, and the
mergeability check covers custom entry types and the comments of @Strings.

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_014xQwRqLx2R27m7xFYPfAdK

* Link the section instead of the not-yet-published page

The user documentation page is still in review, so its deep link 404s.

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_014xQwRqLx2R27m7xFYPfAdK

* Escape the Git placeholders in the merge-driver help

picocli formats the help text, so %O %A %B made it warn about an unknown
conversion instead of printing the setup command.

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_014xQwRqLx2R27m7xFYPfAdK

* Merge entry comments, guard the file prolog

The comment written above an entry took part in neither the merge plan nor
the conflict detection, so a comment changed in OTHER alone was dropped
while the merge reported success; it is now merged like the entry type.
The shared database ID and the encoding are compared as well, and a comment
in front of an @Comment block makes the driver refuse the merge, because
JabRef's parser drops it.

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_014xQwRqLx2R27m7xFYPfAdK

* Harden the comment handling of the merge driver

A deletion on one side now conflicts with a comment change on the other,
the guard for comments an @Comment block swallows reads the file in its own
encoding instead of assuming UTF-8, and it matches the entry type the way
the parser does: case-insensitively, indentation allowed.

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_014xQwRqLx2R27m7xFYPfAdK

* Assert the conflict output, drop restating comments

The conflict tests compare the complete stderr output instead of looking
for a citation key somewhere in it.

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_014xQwRqLx2R27m7xFYPfAdK

* Trace the merge driver as a feature

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_014xQwRqLx2R27m7xFYPfAdK

* Return the clean merge at the end of the driver

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_014xQwRqLx2R27m7xFYPfAdK

* Refuse custom entry types no entry uses

The writer emits the definition of a custom entry type only for types an
entry uses, so a standalone definition disappeared on rewrite. The aborted
write on an encoding problem gets a regression test.

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_014xQwRqLx2R27m7xFYPfAdK

* Move the merge logic of the Git merge driver into jablib

The jabkit command now only maps Git's driver contract to exit codes and messages. BibFileMerger does the work and reports a sealed MergeOutcome, MergePreconditions names every reason a merge is refused, and EntryPropertyMerge applies the three-way rules to entry type and comment. Refuses two more lossy cases: an empty entry and a comment in front of @Preamble.

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01G5wUZVmQHA3aUjgNPTNaTG

* Keep only the implementation view in the code-howto

The user-visible merge behavior moves to the user documentation.

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01G5wUZVmQHA3aUjgNPTNaTG

* Declare jspecify as compile-time-only module dependency of jabkit

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01G5wUZVmQHA3aUjgNPTNaTG

the class is added to and removed from the new root while the old one
keeps a stale value. Restoring the previous root then restores the stale
font size.

Move the class along with the root instead.

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01KWW25B4KzBvBkBmkAzyixM

* Make the walkthrough pane a permanent part of its window

The walkthrough used to host its overlays by replacing the scene root of
every window it visited and restoring it afterwards. Three parties claim
that root: JavaFX's Dialog reassigns it on every show and swaps in a
placeholder on close, ControlsFX injects its decoration pane on the first
validation decoration, and the walkthrough wrapped it. Any two colliding
drop the third's contribution -- a decoration pane installed in a dialog
during a walkthrough was dropped, with its decorations, when the
walkthrough restored the root it remembered.

The pane is now a child of a parent the window already has, added where
the window is built and kept for its lifetime: a sibling of the info
center pane in the main window, a child of the dialog pane in dialogs,
and added to the scene root on first lookup for the popups a walkthrough
visits but JabRef does not build.

One rule covers all three hosts: the pane is unmanaged and sizes itself
to the scene. Its view order keeps it in front of siblings, which a
dialog pane needs because it appends its header, content and button bar
as they are first needed.

This also settles two defects that came with the root swapping. The
highlighter installed panes it never released, so a window that received
a highlight but no tooltip or panel kept a replaced root and an entry in
a static map for the rest of the session. And replacing the root of a
visible window invalidated the CSS of the whole scene graph twice per
visited window, on the interactive path, which is what
JabRefGUI#installControlsFxDecorationPane exists to avoid.

Spotlight's shape is now unmanaged like the other effects' nodes; it is
positioned in the pane's coordinates and only landed correctly because
its bounds happened to match the pane's.

* Document where walkthrough overlays are rendered

Records where the pane is added and why an overlay must not host itself
by replacing the scene root, so the next contributor does not reintroduce
the root swapping. Also notes on RecursiveChildrenListener which root
replacements remain, now that the walkthrough is not one of them.

Key bindings and the walkthrough pane both belong to the dialog pane and
are both reapplied when a dialog swaps in a new one, so they are applied
together instead of being written out twice -- once for the initial pane
and once in the listener, where the second copy reached back through
getDialogPane() for the pane it had already been handed.

A window re-enters Window#getWindows() every time it is shown again,
bringing the same scene, so each re-show stacked another root listener
on it. Record the registration in the scene's properties, keyed per

* Let clicks pass through the walkthrough pane

A Region picks on its bounds by default, and the walkthrough pane covers
the whole window in front of its content. As soon as it held a node --
a ping, a panel, the quit button -- it took every click, including the
ones a walkthrough step waits for through a spotlight's hole. Only the
overlay nodes themselves take input now, which also makes the
mouse-transparency binding for the empty pane unnecessary.

The "Download from URL" walkthrough steps into the TextInputDialog that

brings no walkthrough pane, so the step found none and reverted the

* Keep a popup's walkthrough pane from sizing its popup

menu's drop shadow offsets that content from the scene's origin. The

show the pane's scene listener and the popup's bounds listener recursed
until Parent#recomputeBounds overflowed the stack, and the menu stopped
rendering while its items still reacted to the mouse.

A popup's pane now takes no size of its own. The walkthrough only draws
effects there that position themselves, such as the ping.

Replaces the hand-rolled temp-file/atomic-move/permission/hard-link
handling in FileUtil with the existing AtomicFileOutputStream, which
already implements the same commit strategy for library saves. FileUtil
is untouched again; the PDF writers load the document into memory and
save through the atomic stream.

* Address review: abort atomic stream on failed save, load PDFs file-backed

A PDFBox serialization failure between stream writes left the atomic
stream unaware of the error, so closing it committed a partial file.
The writers now commit explicitly after the document is closed and
abort on every failure path. Loading is file-backed again instead of
reading the whole PDF into memory.

replaced the target. The deletion failure is now logged instead.

subject: Fix undo after adding an entry by DOI or URL (#17022)
body:
* Record an imported entry, wherever the import came from

Adding an entry by DOI or URL in the New Entry dialog inserted it and
recorded nothing: Ctrl+Z did nothing, and since the modified marker is
derived from the journal, the library did not even ask to be saved on
close. The paste and file-import paths were undoable only because their
callers each remembered to record the insert themselves.

importCleanedEntries now opens the step around its own insert, so every
caller gets it: LibraryTab#insertEntries and the background file import
drop the UndoableInsertEntries they built by hand, and the group
assignment the insert sets off still joins the same step.

Two tests had mocked the journal around an import, which now answers the
recording block without running it - they build a real one.

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_0194MmVeMweN5EKQEx5yNoC1

* Link the CHANGELOG entry to the issue it fixes

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_0194MmVeMweN5EKQEx5yNoC1

* Address the qodo review of #17022

Three of the four were real, and two of them were made worse by this
branch: before it, an unrecorded insert meant undo did nothing, which is
at least harmless.

- Replacing a duplicate removed the entry that was there without
  recording it, so undoing the import left the library with neither. The
  removal is recorded now, as its own step - the decision is asked
  asynchronously, well before the insert it makes room for.
- Moving entries between libraries removed them from the source
  unrecorded. Undo in the target would have removed the copy while the
  original stayed gone. The source library now records losing them, in

subject: Fix undo E - Undoable library properties, coalesced typing, honest modified marker (#16988)
body:
* Journal what the library properties dialog writes

Seven tabs write straight into one MetaData instance, so there is no
per-setting change to collect: the dialog records a snapshot pair around
the tabs, and what the tabs record themselves - the preamble, the string
constants, the entries the keyword separator migration rewrites - joins
the same step.

The keyword separator therefore no longer records a change of its own,
and the group separator migration stops building node-keyed records that
a later group operation would silently detach. That leaves
UndoableGroupChange and UndoableKeywordSeparatorChange without callers,
so both are gone.

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_0194MmVeMweN5EKQEx5yNoC1

* Add the CHANGELOG entry for the library properties step

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_0194MmVeMweN5EKQEx5yNoC1

* Retire the two keys the deleted records used

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_0194MmVeMweN5EKQEx5yNoC1

* Cover the properties dialog through its own view, and mark the import group

The dialog's undo step is now tested through the built dialog and its seven
real tabs, not only through the view model with stubs. That turned up what
an untouched dialog does: the tabs write back the defaults their controls
were filled with, so accepting it materialises an encoding the library did
not have - one step now, and one nobody could take back before.

AddGroupImportEntriesAction reports its write through
ParserResult#setChangedOnMigration. It runs before the tab is attached to
the library, so nothing was listening when it added the group, and a
library whose only change was that group could be closed without a prompt.

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_0194MmVeMweN5EKQEx5yNoC1

* Put the CHANGELOG placeholder back

No pull request is open for this branch, so the entry cannot link one.

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_0194MmVeMweN5EKQEx5yNoC1

* Give a metadata change a source, so the marker can tell recorded from not

The tab marked the library on every metadata event, whoever posted it, so
a change the journal had recorded was stamped through a path no undo can
clear: undoing a group edit or a settings change left the asterisk on
until the library was saved.

MetaDataChangedEvent now carries a MetaDataChangeSource, the way an entry
change carries an EntriesEventSource, and the tab marks only on LOCAL.
Every setter reports LOCAL, so a writer that says nothing is treated as
unrecorded - the safe default.

Saying it needed one door per recorded change rather than a parameter on
fifteen setters: setGroups for the group panel, overwriteWith for the
settings. The properties dialog reaches that door by having its tabs
write into a copy of the settings, which the step installs - so the
dialog writes the library once, and the record describes the change
instead of observing it afterwards.

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_0194MmVeMweN5EKQEx5yNoC1

* Let a properties tab read and write the settings it is handed

storeSettings took the settings to write to while setValues still read the
library's own, and the view models kept a MetaData field besides - three
sources for one thing, and nothing saying which one wins. A tab could
have been filled from one library and written to another without a word.

Both halves take the settings now, and no tab holds any: the dialog hands
the live ones to setValues and the working copy to storeSettings. The
fields that only existed to be written to are gone with the constructor
parameters that fed them, which is how SavingPropertiesViewModel came to
read the order the dialog opened with in setValues rather than in its
constructor.

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_0194MmVeMweN5EKQEx5yNoC1

* Make a run of keystrokes one undo step, and queue one refresh for a burst

A field editor records one change per keystroke, so Ctrl+Z took back a
letter rather than a word. CoalescingPolicy decides when a change
continues the step on top of the stack; the journal consults it on every
single-change push. Two field changes are one step when they describe the
same field of the same entry and the second starts where the first ended.

The merge is guarded four ways: a merged step takes a new position id,
the saved position is never merged into, a run that ends where it started
leaves no step at all, and a recorded block is never continued. The one
boundary the journal cannot see is a change of entry, which the editor
draws with endStep().

P20: the JavaFX refresh queues one update for a burst instead of one per
push, cleared before the stacks are read so an edit arriving mid-refresh
still queues a fresh one.

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_0194MmVeMweN5EKQEx5yNoC1

* Drop guard for event sources, and say where the merge rule lives

Formerly guarded a burst that was just removed: one push per keystroke was
the only realistic source, and a command pushes once however long it ran.
What was left was a flag and two paragraphs explaining where it is
cleared, for queue pressure that no longer happens. The item keeps its
place in the plan with the shape recorded, so it can come back if a burst
source does. The burst test stays, rephrased to pin what matters - the
properties end at the journal's last state.

The coalescing rule stays a policy the journal consults rather than a
mergeWith on the change: what counts as one user action is editing
policy, and the codebase already draws that line for user-facing text.
The condition reads forwards now instead of as two negations.

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_0194MmVeMweN5EKQEx5yNoC1

* Convert FieldChange to a record

Fifty-eight lines shorter: the 25-line equals, the hashCode and the four
getters are generated. Only toString survives, because it prints the
citation key rather than the entry.

The blast radius the plan feared did not exist - six files read the
accessors, not the hundreds the estimate assumed, because most of jablib
passes a FieldChange on rather than reading it.

Not collapsed into UndoableFieldChange: that one compares its entry by
identity, because a step on the stack has to describe that entry object,
while a FieldChange compares entries as BibEntry does. Merging them would
force one semantics on the other's callers. Both now say so.

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_0194MmVeMweN5EKQEx5yNoC1

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_0194MmVeMweN5EKQEx5yNoC1

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_0194MmVeMweN5EKQEx5yNoC1

* Formatter

* Address the qodo review of #16988

A command no longer joins the run the user was typing. The journal could
not tell a keystroke from a command - a field editor and
GenerateCitationKeySingleAction record the same UndoableFieldChange
against the same entry and field - so typing a citation key and then
generating one was a single step, and one undo removed both. The caller
says which it is now: applyEdit(change) is a user action of its own, and
only applyEdit(change, EditSource.TYPING), which the field editor uses,
may continue the step it lands on.

Also from the review: the CHANGELOG entry is 17 words rather than 23,
MetaDataChangedEvent and MetaDataChangeSource are @NullMarked, and
org.jabref.logic.undo has a package-info describing what the package
promises, including where a step begins and ends.

UndoableMetaDataChange now says why it applies unconditionally, which the
review read as a defect: verifying would refuse the undo outright
whenever an unrelated metadata write had happened.

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_0194MmVeMweN5EKQEx5yNoC1

* Address the review of #16988

Undoing a settings snapshot keeps the AI library id and the .blg paths the live metadata acquired since, so the stored chats stay reachable. Fixes the MADR heading level, drops a redundant redo-stack clear, and states honestly in the CHANGELOG what one undo takes back.

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_011uYTdptCBPh5Zw8Ak7F6ro

* End a run of typing at a word boundary

Undo took back everything typed into a field, so a typo at the end of an
abstract cost the whole abstract. Redo brought it back, but a user who
has just watched a paragraph vanish does not think of Ctrl+Y first, and
every other editor breaks a run at whitespace. A finished word now ends
the run, which is a change to what the requirement promises, so it moves
to revision 2.

The group tree test drove the view model from the test thread while the
refresh it triggers walked the same children on the JavaFX thread, which
failed on CI as an IndexOutOfBounds inside the list mapping. Both calls
run on the JavaFX thread now.

The two tests this branch adds still used TestFX, which main dropped in
#16850; they use JavaFxExtension like the rest.

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01QKmBCe59g42fuvb4jHMs1v

* Create the group for imported entries on import, not on open

The group was created when a library was opened, which wrote to a
library the user had only looked at. Marking that write, as this branch
did, brings back the modified marker #15610 set out to remove; not
marking it loses the group on close. Creating the group when entries are
actually imported removes the choice: nothing writes to a library nobody
imported into, and the write that happens belongs to an import the user
asked for.

The creation is announced, because the group is a change to the library
the user did not ask for by itself.

AddGroupImportEntriesAction is no longer a post-open action; it writes
the root back so that the group panel and the modified marker hear about
the change through the metadata, the way every other group operation
reports itself.

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01QKmBCe59g42fuvb4jHMs1v

* Say that a changed field value can be absent

`FieldChangedEvent` declared its two values non-null while every caller
passes `null` for a field that was not there yet or has just been removed,
which is what NullAway reported on the class. The values and the getters are
now `@Nullable`, and the two readers that dereferenced them are written so
an absent value is the empty string. `computeMajorCharacterChange` returns
what it returned before.

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01Qogp9Uq6PGZjhPohJacLqV

* Say how the two "is this still the same edit?" rules differ

`CoarseChangeFilter` and `CoalescingPolicy` decide the same thing for
different consumers, and each now points at the other. The filter says why it
keeps its own conservative rule: a filtered change is held back from the
shared database, so filtering too eagerly costs more than filtering too
little.

subject: Do not apply the JBang plugin (only use its task type) (#16975)
body:
Applying `dev.jbang` displays a kordamp banner that reads and increments
`<gradleUserHome>/caches/kordamp/jbang/<version>/marker.txt` at configuration
time. Gradle tracks that read as a configuration input and the plugin's own
write changes it, so the configuration cache was invalidated on every build -
costing ~2.5 minutes of re-configuration each time.

written.

Applying the plugin only prints the banner, applies `BasePlugin`, and registers
an unused `jbang` task, so `apply false` keeps everything we need: the

subject: Fix undo D - Undoable groups and citation keys, cleanups, quality and bugfixes (#16936)
body:
* Make generated citation keys undoable

GenerateCitationKeyAction overrode BackgroundTask#onSuccess(Consumer),
which is a setter the executor never calls - it reads the stored consumer
through getOnSuccess(). The override was therefore dead code: the collected
CompoundEdit was never pushed, so the keys were not undoable, and the
"Generated citation key for" notification never appeared.

Register the work with .onSuccess(...) instead of overriding the setter.
The same change makes the tab marking reachable, so mark the tab captured
when generation starts rather than whichever tab is in front when the task
finishes - the keys are recorded against the library the action started on.

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_0194MmVeMweN5EKQEx5yNoC1

* Keep a library's metadata instance when its contents are replaced (P26)

BibDatabaseContext#setMetaData replaced the object, while LibraryTab and
CoarseChangeFilter register listeners on the instance. After the one caller
that truly swapped it - UndoableMetaDataChange, installing the metadata
parsed from disk - both were subscribed to a discarded object, so later
metadata edits no longer marked the library modified and no longer reached
autosave and backup.

MetaData#setContentsFrom takes over another instance's contents, leaving
identity, and with it every subscriber, intact. UndoableMetaDataChange
applies that instead of swapping references, and copies both of its states,
since the library's live instance is typically the "before" state and
applying writes into it.

setMetaData is gone: its two remaining callers read the context's own
metadata, mutated it and set the same object back.

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_0194MmVeMweN5EKQEx5yNoC1

* Say what was undone in the notification

UndoAction notified with a bare "Undo" and RedoAction with "Redo", leaving
the user to work out what had just changed - hardest exactly when it matters,
after an import or cleanup that finished while they were elsewhere.

undo() and redo() now return what they took back, named for the user and read
inside the monitor, so the name describes the step that moved rather than
whichever step another thread has since pushed. Only the name leaves the
journal; nothing outside it reads the stacks.

A ChangeSet is named by the control the user activated, which no derived text
beats. A change recorded on its own has no such name, so BibChangeDescriber
derives one from what the change does. The text lives there rather than on the
records, which are model values carrying no user-facing text, and its switch
is exhaustive over the sealed interface: a new kind of change does not compile
until it has been given a description.

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_0194MmVeMweN5EKQEx5yNoC1

* Report the changes a set could not apply

ChangeSet#apply() caught each element's failure and only logged it, so as a
BibChange it reported a success it had not delivered - the one implementation
of the sealed interface quietly weakening the contract the others keep. A user
undoing such a step was told it was undone.

apply() now returns an ApplyResult naming what did not make it. Best-effort
application stays: aborting midway would leave the library in a state that is
neither the old nor the new one and that no later undo could describe. The
failures of nested sets travel up as they are, so what comes back names the
changes that failed rather than the sets that held them.

undo() and redo() return that alongside the step's name, and the Undo and Redo
actions say when a step was only partly taken back. applyEdit passes it on for
commands that want to report their own outcome; callers that ignore it behave
exactly as before.

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_0194MmVeMweN5EKQEx5yNoC1

* Hold a library against undo while a command writes to it (P21)

A command that mutates on a background thread writes to the library long
before anything reaches the stack: the block form applies as it goes and
pushes when the block ends, and the five manual collectors apply as they go
and push at the end of the task. An undo arriving in that window takes back a
change underneath those writes - the library then holds a state no step on the
stack describes, and the push that follows discards the undone change along
with the redo stack. P15 closed this for a single applyEdit; it cannot close
it for a whole block.

Undo now declines instead of waiting. Waiting would mean holding the journal's
monitor across the whole block, which is what its deadlock rule forbids, and
freeing the JavaFX thread from that wait would make undo asynchronous - far
more than the defect warrants.

UndoManager#reserveWrites(name) marks the window open; canUndo, canRedo, undo
and redo answer negatively while it is. Taking and releasing both notify, so
menu enablement falls when a command takes the library and rises when it gives
it back, and the keystroke path reports "Cannot undo while X is running"
rather than "Nothing to undo", which would be untrue.

The block form reserves for its own duration, so every caller of it is covered
without changing anything. Only the five hand-collecting commands reserve
explicitly, each closing after its push and on every path its task can end by
- closing is idempotent for exactly that reason. Reservations are per library,
so a long import in one library leaves the others undoable.

Not covered: a user edit recorded while a command is mid-flight still lands on
the stack out of order with the command's own writes. Blocking editing during
an import is too far; detecting it on apply is the follow-up.

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_0194MmVeMweN5EKQEx5yNoC1

* Apply the code checklist to the undo/redo branch

- The Undo and Redo actions consumed the "is a command writing?" Optional with
  isPresent() and get(); they use ifPresentOrElse now, with the stack path in
  its own method.
- The block form held the reservation in a nullable local. A nested block takes
  a reservation that does nothing instead, which says the same thing in the
  type rather than in a null check, and leaves one unconditional close().
- ApplyResult opened its body with a blank line, which checkstyle rejects.
- The CHANGELOG entries are one sentence each, within twenty words, and carry
  TODO placeholders until this PR has a number.

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_0194MmVeMweN5EKQEx5yNoC1

* Name the metadata copy operations, and stop sharing the group tree

MetaData#setContentsFrom was one method doing two jobs under a name that
described neither. It is now a pair: the static copyOf for a detached snapshot,
and copyFrom for taking over another's contents in place - which is what
UndoableMetaDataChange needs, since replacing the instance is the defect it
exists to avoid.

The copy shared the group tree with its source, because setGroups stores the
node it is given and group operations mutate nodes in place. A group edit made
after a metadata change was recorded therefore rewrote what undoing that change
would restore. The tree is copied now, as UndoableModifySubtree already does.
Both regression tests fail without that one line.

Also: ContentSelectors gained setAll, so copying no longer clears another
object's live set through a getter; the javadoc no longer claims a single event
where setGroups posts one of its own; and MetaDataTest asserts the four fields
MetaData#equals ignores, which the earlier test would have passed without.

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_0194MmVeMweN5EKQEx5yNoC1

* Replace ChangeOutcome with a flat StepOutcome

ChangeOutcome carried an ApplyResult, so the call site read
outcome.result().isComplete() - two types with "result" in the name, one inside
the other - and it was wrapped in an Optional the caller had already excluded by
testing canUndo() first, which made ifPresent guard a case that could not occur.

StepOutcome(name, complete) is what the UI actually needs: which step moved, and
whether all of it went through. The journal collapses the ApplyResult to that one
bit; the failures stay where ChangeSet already logs them.

The actions ask once instead of twice: an empty outcome is the journal saying
there was nothing to undo, so ifPresentOrElse covers both answers and canUndo()
is left to menu enablement, which is its job.

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_0194MmVeMweN5EKQEx5yNoC1

* Rename MetaData#copyFrom to overwriteWith

copyOf and copyFrom shared a prefix while differing in the two things that
matter: one returns a new instance, the other mutates the receiver. Which of
the two a call site was doing could only be told by noticing static versus
instance. overwriteWith says it, and says which object survives - the point of
the method, since keeping the instance is what keeps its listeners.

Note that AiPreferences#copyFrom has the same overwrite-the-receiver semantics,
so this diverges from that precedent; the confusable pair on one class is the
reason.

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_0194MmVeMweN5EKQEx5yNoC1

* Say what the undo suspension does, and name the right command

WriteReservation read like a write lock, which is the one thing it is not: two
commands may write to one library at the same time, and what is held is undo,
not the writes. It is UndoSuspension now, taken with suspendUndo(name) and read
back through suspendedBy().

The name reported could belong to a command that had already finished: it was
stored when the count went 0 to 1 and cleared only at 0, so with an import and a
lookup running, finishing the import still left "Cannot undo while Import
entries is running" on screen. The open suspensions are held in an ordered set
instead of a count plus a name, so the one named is the oldest still writing,
and a finished command is not in the set to be named.

Two readability fixes in the same area: a nested block takes UndoSuspension.NONE
rather than an unexplained no-op lambda, and the handle is a named inner class
instead of twenty lines of anonymous class in the middle of suspendUndo. The
type javadoc carries the whole story now, since a call site is where readers
arrive from, and both halves of the API point at each other.

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_0194MmVeMweN5EKQEx5yNoC1

* Cleanups

* Stop context menus from claiming global keyboard shortcuts

Ctrl+Z did nothing unless the entry editor had focus. The binding was right and
the Edit menu item was enabled: the search field's context menu, attached
eagerly in GlobalSearchBar, built its items through the same ActionFactory, so
its Undo item carried the global accelerator for StandardActions.UNDO. A
MenuItem's accelerator is scene-wide and JavaFX keeps one entry per key
combination, so that item owned Ctrl+Z - and since it is enabled only while the
search field itself has something to undo, JavaFX skipped it and passed the
event to nobody.

Typing in the search bar, focusing the entry table and pressing Ctrl+Z cleared
the search bar, which is the same defect seen from the other side.

Context menu items are reached with the mouse and lose nothing by leaving key
combinations to whoever owns them globally, so createContextMenuItem builds
them without an accelerator. The search field's menu and the field editors'
default items use it - the latter were claiming Ctrl+X, Ctrl+C, Ctrl+V, Delete
and Ctrl+A in the same way, which went unnoticed because MainTable handles
those four in its own key filter.

The entry editor kept working throughout because FieldEditorFX consumes the
keystroke in a filter before accelerators are reached, which is why the fault
looked like a focus problem.

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_0194MmVeMweN5EKQEx5yNoC1

* Make group operations undoable

Adding, removing, moving, sorting and editing groups left nothing on the undo
stack, so Ctrl+Z after a group operation either did nothing or undid whatever
came before it. Every registration for it had been commented out since the
group panel was rewritten, and the two edit classes they referred to were
deleted in this workstream because nothing constructed them.

Recorded as the tree the operation produced, not as a per-node delta. That is
how the operations already reach the model: the panel edits its nodes in place
and writes the root back with MetaData#setGroups afterwards, so one record -
UndoableGroupTreeChange - covers adding, removing, moving and reordering alike,
and undoing any of them is installing the tree that was there before. The
alternative, an inverse pair per operation, needs four of them: removing a node
while keeping its children is not the inverse of adding one.

Both states are copies, since nodes are mutated in place, and applying installs
a copy too - otherwise the next edit would rewrite what the step restores.

Operations that also change entries hand their FieldChanges to the same step,
so taking a group back takes its assignments with it: removing a group with its
subgroups, editing a group definition, assigning and unassigning the selection,
and clearing a group. Group assignment on import is recorded as its own step,
because the import path pushes before the entries reach the library.

MetaData#clearGroups is new: a library that had no groups has to end up with
none again, rather than with an empty root that a save would write out.

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_0194MmVeMweN5EKQEx5yNoC1

* Clear out the dead undo code the group panel carried

GroupTreeViewModel and GroupNodeViewModel kept the Swing-era registrations as
comments - NamedCompound, UndoableAddOrRemoveGroup, panel.getUndoManager(),
WarnAssignmentSideEffects - referring to classes that no longer exist, next to
"TODO: Add undo" markers for work that P10 has since done. Twenty-odd lines of
it, in the middle of the methods a reader has to follow.

The corpses are gone. Two intents in them are real and survive as one-line
TODOs: expanding the parent so a new group is visible, and warning before
assigning entries to a group whose membership is written to a field other than
keywords.

"TODO: Store undo" on GroupNodeViewModel#addEntriesToGroup could only be
deleted honestly by making it true, so the two callers that dropped the
returned changes now record them: dropping entries onto a group in the tree,
and auto-assigning newly added entries to the selected group. Both were on
P10's list. The method's javadoc says the recording is the caller's job, since
only the caller knows whether the assignment is a step of its own.

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_0194MmVeMweN5EKQEx5yNoC1

* Address the review of this branch

One recorder for group operations, not two. GroupNodeViewModel had its own copy

* Refuse a change the library has moved on from

P21 stops undo while a command is writing, but nothing stops the reverse: the

tidying. #6031 had to translate special field names, the translation already
lived on the view model, so the cheapest way to reach it was to construct one —
with Globals.undoManager, a static global that cost the call site nothing. #11342
("DI Part A") deleted Globals and made the constructor's dependencies explicit,
so a string lookup grew two parameters; the translation was mechanical and
correct, but nobody re-asked whether the label needed them. #16273 then added the
static getAction(SpecialField) and FieldsUtil.getDisplayName(Field), which made
the label reachable with no instance at all, while getNameWithType kept the old
route — two ways to compute one label in one file.

The label now comes from getDisplayName(Field), so the two cannot drift, and
getNameWithType has the signature it had before Globals went. SpecialFieldViewModel

the crash by moving the lookup into getDisplayName(), which left a value object
asking the service locator once per rendered cell, since nameProperty() builds a
fresh wrapper per call. Both lookups are gone now, together with the
CliPreferences field that existed only to be forwarded, so the class no longer
references Injector at all. SaveOrderConfigPanel loses both @Inject fields and the
jakarta.inject.Inject import; XmpPrivacyTab loses its injector field and import.

MainTableColumnModelTest no longer needs the @BeforeAll that registered a mock
CliPreferences to satisfy the constructor, and gains a test that builds a
special-field column with nothing registered at all and asserts the rendered
label — the startup crash pinned as a test rather than as a comment.

which is also why no existing test needed changing.

* Make a failed Cut leave the library alone instead of undoing the top of the stack

cutEntry copied to the clipboard, deleted the entries whether or not that copy
had succeeded, and then compared the two counts: on a mismatch it called a bare
undoManager.undo() to put the entries back. That reverts whatever is on top of
the journal, which is this deletion only if nothing else pushed in between — an
import or a cleanup finishing at that moment was undone instead, and the entries
stayed deleted. The deletion also moved to the redo stack rather than being
discarded, so the next redo re-applied a cut the user had just been told failed.

The copy already ran first, so the fix is to return when it fails: nothing is
deleted and there is nothing to roll back. Recording the cut as one invertible
step would also have worked, but an early return puts the invariant in the shape
of the method rather than in a compensating action that has to be got right.

The same branch also called clipBoardManager.setContent(""). The IOException it
reacts to comes from serializeEntries, which runs before the clipboard is written
(ClipBoardManager:186,189), so the clipboard still held whatever the user had put
there earlier; the failure handler discarded content this cut never owned.

This is latent rather than live, and no CHANGELOG entry goes with it. The branch
cannot currently be reached: entriesCopied is negative only when
ClipBoardManager.setContent throws IOException, which comes from
BibEntryWriter.write(List, mode) writing into a StringWriter, which does not
throw. Nor can the counts differ another way — both calls take the same selection,
getSelectedEntries() being mainTable.getSelectedEntries(), and doDeleteEntry
returns -1 only in DELETE_ENTRY mode, never for CUT. Observable behaviour is
therefore unchanged, including the empty-selection path, which still notifies
"Cut 0 entry(s)". What the change buys is that "compensate for a write by undoing
whatever is on top" is no longer in the codebase to be copied or made reachable.

No test: LibraryTab is not constructible in a test, every test that mentions it
mocks it, and the trigger is an IOException a StringWriter cannot produce.

* Give every library its own undo journal

Completes P18. Until now one journal served every open library, which had two
live consequences: Ctrl+Z in library B popped whatever was on top of the shared
stack, applying an edit made in library A to A's entries; and saving A stamped the
shared saved position, so B reported itself unchanged while holding unsaved edits.
No position scheme could fix the second, because identifying positions correctly
in a stack that mixes two libraries still answers the wrong question. The fix is
ownership.

JabRefGuiStateManager now keeps one journal per library and hands it out by
context. The map is keyed by BibDatabaseContext.getUid() rather than by the
context, as selectedGroups already is: a context's hashCode changes whenever an
entry is added, so a map keyed by the context itself loses its entries — its own
javadoc says as much. It is concurrent because changes are recorded from
background tasks as well as from the JavaFX thread.

* Make an accepted external metadata change undoable

Accepting external changes records every kind but one. MetadataChange took the
CompoundEdit it was handed and never used it: it set the new metadata on the
context directly, under a "TODO: Metadata edit should be undoable". So accepting a
change to a library's own settings — mode, encoding, citation key pattern, file
directories, save actions, content selectors, protection — could not be taken back,
while accepting an entry or string change beside it could.

This is the defect the record model exists to prevent, the same one that left
keyword management, file import and "Replace string" silently unrecorded.

UndoableMetaDataChange holds the context and both metadata objects and swaps them,
which is what applying already did; inverting swaps them back. The groups root is
pinned to its original value before the record is built rather than after the
metadata is installed, so redo does it too and does not fight GroupChange, which
owns the groups.

BibChangeTest covers it with the others: inverting twice is identity, and undoing
puts the previous settings object back.

LibraryTab and CoarseChangeFilter register their listeners on the instance
(LibraryTab:260, CoarseChangeFilter:31). After a swap they listen to the object
that was replaced. That predates this change and is not altered by it — undo
happens to restore the instance they are attached to.

* Fix status label update for reviews on fork PRs

On a fork pull request, pull_request_review* workflow runs get no secrets and
a read-only token, so the "Comment on PR" label step aborted with exit code 4

that only records the PR number, letting the privileged workflow_run path do
the labelling - the same pattern the changes-requested check already uses.

* Fix checklist issues in pdf extract-references: checkstyle order, markdown javadoc, add CitationsFromPdf test

with the project's markdown-javadoc [#method] syntax, extracted the
Grobid-URL-override logic into a testable helper, and added a unit
test for it plus a CHANGELOG entry (using the required TODO
placeholder for the not-yet-existing PR number).

* Replace CHANGELOG TODO placeholder with PR #16186 link

* Fix pdf extract-references: force Grobid enabled, create output dirs, add @NullMarked

- --mode=GROBID previously reused the stored preferences as-is, so if
  Grobid was disabled globally, GrobidService threw an uncaught
  UnsupportedOperationException instead of running the extraction the
  user explicitly asked for. Now always routes through the
  Grobid-enabled preferences override, using --grobid-url if given or
  the configured URL otherwise.

subject: Fix undo B - Ids on undo changes, rewordings and split of UndoManager, minor clarifications (#16680)
body:
* Identify the saved position, don't count edits

`hasChanged()` compared a net edit balance against the balance recorded
at save time. Two different histories reach the same balance, because
pushing a change clears the redo stack: save, undo, then make a
different edit, and the balance is back where it started although the
library now holds something that was never saved.

That is not only a stale modified marker. `hasChanged()` feeds
`LibraryTab.markChangedOrUnChanged()`, which sets `changedProperty`,
which `requestClose()` consults before offering to save — so the false
negative closes a library holding unsaved work without asking.

Positions are now identified rather than counted. Every push takes an
id from a counter that only ever increments, the id travels with the
change across both stacks so redo returns to the position it came from,
and `markUnchanged()` stores the id at the top of the undo stack.
Because ids are never reused, a saved position discarded by a
redo-stack clear or by the LIMIT trim can never be matched again, which
is the right answer in both cases: it is no longer reachable.

The id lives in a private `UndoJournalEntry` record rather than on
`BibChange`. A change is a value describing a modification; a position
in this journal is bookkeeping only the manager needs. Putting it on
the change would also cost `inverted()` its involution, since it would
have to either copy the id — giving two distinct positions one identity
— or drop it.

The empty stack needs its own id for the same reason: once a trim or a
`clear()` has discarded history for good, "undone back to nothing" is
no longer the state the library started in.

Three tests cover the defect and fail without this change. The two
existing trim tests pin the behaviour the id scheme had to preserve.

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_0194MmVeMweN5EKQEx5yNoC1

* Apply and record under one acquisition of the monitor

`apply()` was `change.apply(); addEdit(change);` — two separate
acquisitions of this object's monitor, with the model write outside it.
Between them the library holds the change and the journal does not, so
an undo arriving there reverts the *previous* change while the new one
stays applied but unrecorded. The history that ends up on the stack
then describes a library state that never existed.

The class header already stated the opposite as an invariant: "Applying
the change is inside the lock. It has to be: if the stack transition
and the model write could interleave, two threads could undo the same
change." `undo()` and `redo()` honour it; `apply()` was the one path
that did not, and commands do push from background tasks, so the two
threads the header describes exist.

The stack transition moves into a private `push()` that requires the
monitor, and `apply()` takes it once around both the model write and
the push. Applying foreign code under the lock is already the accepted
cost here — `undo()` does it — so this brings one path in line rather
than changing the design.

Inside an `addEdit` block there is no window to close: the recorder
belongs to one thread and nothing reaches the stacks until the block
ends, so that path takes no lock. `CompoundEdit.apply()` keeps its
two-step form for the same reason, and its javadoc now says so instead
of pointing at a lock invariant that does not apply to it.

The regression test asks the applying thread, from inside a `BibEntry`
subclass that probes on `setField`, whether it holds the journal's
monitor at that moment. Staging a second thread would only have shown
that it did not get in within some interval, which makes the assertion
a statement about a timeout; whether the lock is held is a fact
available on the spot, and no threads, executors or waits are needed to
read it. The probe overrides rather than subscribing to the entry's
field events, so the test adds no use of Guava's deprecated EventBus.

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_0194MmVeMweN5EKQEx5yNoC1

* Name the recording pair addEdit / applyEdit

P15 stopped `apply()` from delegating to `addEdit()`: it has to hold the
monitor across the model write and the stack push, and `addEdit()` ends
by notifying listeners, which must never run under the lock. The branch
deciding whether a change reaches the stacks at all therefore had to be
restated in `apply()`, and the two methods came to read as near
duplicates of one another.

They are not duplicates. The only difference is who performs the
change: `addEdit` records one the caller has already made — the common
case, because the model hands the caller a `FieldChange` as a
by-product — while the other makes it and records it as one operation.
Everything after that is the same journal entry. `apply` said only that
it performed the change and left the recording to its javadoc, so the
pair is now `addEdit` / `applyEdit`: one verb apart, same noun, and the
javadoc's first sentence states the recording outright. `CompoundEdit`
carries the same pair, so code inside a recording block reads like code
outside one.

The empty-step guard the two share is one `isEmptyStep` helper rather
than the same condition written twice with two different comments, so
each method now reads as the same three-branch dispatch: hand to the
enclosing recorder, skip an empty step, or lock and push.

Renames only; no behaviour change, and the compiler enumerated all 28
call sites.

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_0194MmVeMweN5EKQEx5yNoC1

* Carry the affected-entry count beside the step

`AutomaticFieldEditorUndoableEdit` existed to add one `int` to
`CompoundEdit`, and `CompoundEdit` gave up `final` to allow it. The
subtype added no behaviour: the count is what the "Automatic field
editor" notification tells the user, and nothing in the undo model ever
read it — a value type carrying a field for the benefit of a dialog.

The count now travels as a parameter, `addEdit(CompoundEdit, int)`, to
the one method that consumed it. Every call site already had it in a
local variable, so the change removes a setter call rather than adding
an argument to compute. `AutomaticFieldEditorUndoableEdit` is deleted
and `CompoundEdit` is `final` again, leaving the change model with no
inheritance at all.

Recorded in the plan as the P11 follow-up, and promoted from "no
behavioural gain" by the SOLID review: it is the only place where
inheritance was standing in for composition in this area.

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_0194MmVeMweN5EKQEx5yNoC1

* Split UndoManager into interface and JabRefUndoManager

Roughly 120 classes hold an undo handle, and almost all of them do one
thing with it: edit the library and hand the change over. Undoing,
redoing, asking whether the library differs from the last saved
position and subscribing to stack changes are the business of five
classes. Passing the whole manager to the rest handed every field
editor, cleanup and import task the ability to rewrite the user's
history, when all any of them does is describe what it just changed.

`UndoManager` is now the recording interface — `addEdit(BibChange)`,
`addEdit(String, Consumer)`, `applyEdit(BibChange)` — and
`JabRefUndoManager` is the implementation, following the shape JabRef
already uses for DialogService / JabRefDialogService. The class header
argued against a separate recording type on the grounds that it "would
mean threading a second handle everywhere the first one already goes";
that holds against a second object and not against an interface on the
same one, and the header now says so.

Keeping the interface under the old name is what makes this small. The
~118 recording clients keep the type name and the handle name they
already had, so the diff is 21 files rather than 133, and afterburner
keeps resolving injection sites because the registered key still
matches the declared type. `JabRefGUI` registers the one instance under
both keys, for the few classes that ask for the implementation.

Only five classes call anything beyond recording: GuiUndoManager,
UndoAction, RedoAction, EditAction and LibraryTab (SaveDatabaseAction
reaches markUnchanged through LibraryTab's getter). Sixteen further
classes hold the implementation and call nothing on it at all — they
carry it to reach one of those five, which is P12's problem, not an
interface gap: what they would need is undo/redo/canUndo/hasChanged,
which is the whole class again.

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_0194MmVeMweN5EKQEx5yNoC1

* Layer GuiUndoManager the way JabRef layers preferences

P16 left the implementation type threaded through the GUI: twenty
classes named `JabRefUndoManager`, and only five of them called
anything on it. The other fifteen carried it to reach one of those
five, so narrowing them meant narrowing what they carried it *to*.

The layering JabRef already uses for preferences does that in one
move:

    CliPreferences  <- JabRefCliPreferences
    GuiPreferences extends CliPreferences
        JabRefGuiPreferences extends JabRefCliPreferences implements GuiPreferences

    UndoManager  <- JabRefUndoManager
    GuiUndoManager extends UndoManager
        JabRefGuiUndoManager extends JabRefUndoManager implements GuiUndoManager

`GuiUndoManager` is now an interface: the recording half it inherits,
the stack controls the undo UI needs, and the two JavaFX properties the
menus bind to. It declares the controls rather than inheriting them
because an interface cannot inherit from a class; `JabRefUndoManager`
already implements every one, and `JabRefGuiUndoManager` brings the two
together.

No class type is threaded anywhere now. In jabgui, `JabRefUndoManager`
appears only in that extends clause, and `JabRefGuiUndoManager` only in
`JabRefGUI`, which creates the single instance and registers it under
both interfaces — as `Launcher` registers `JabRefGuiPreferences` under
`GuiPreferences.class`.

Extending rather than wrapping also removes the unwrap: `UndoAction`
and `RedoAction` already received the facade and did
`guiUndoManager.getUndoManager().undo()`. That accessor is gone, and
with it the second object the application never wanted — `JabRefFrame`
no longer builds a facade around the manager it was passed, and
`MainMenu` and `MainToolBar` take one handle where they took two.

This is inheritance for a layer specialization, which is why it does
not contradict the P11 follow-up two commits ago: that subclass hung a
dialog's counter on a value type and the owner never read it, while
this adds the GUI's view of a service, the shape this codebase already
uses for preferences and dialogs. The cost is that `JabRefUndoManager`
is now an extension point: it stays non-final, the subclass shares its
monitor, and the refresh runs from a listener the subclass registers on
itself, after the monitor is released.

Three tests that had to mock the class can now mock an interface.

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_0194MmVeMweN5EKQEx5yNoC1

* Name every undo step for the person who will read it

`CompoundEdit` takes any string and `toChangeSet()` hands it on as
`ChangeSet.name`, which that record's javadoc calls "the only
user-facing text in the change model". Nothing converts, validates or
localizes it in between, so the promotion from developer label to user
text happens silently at that one call.

Eight of the twenty-six step names had never been written for a reader:
CHANGE_SELECTED_FIELD, APPEND_TO_SELECTED_FIELD, CLEAR_SELECTED_FIELD,
COPY_FIELD_VALUE, MOVE_EDIT, SWAP_FIELD_VALUES, RENAME_EDIT, and
EDIT_FIELDS — the last published as `NAMED_COMPOUND_EDITS`, a leftover
of the `NamedCompoundEdit` class workstream A deleted. Each now carries
the label of the control the user actually activated: Set, Append,
Clear field content, Copy content, Move content, Swap content, Rename
field, and the dialog's own title for the step that spans all of them.
Every one of those was already a translated key, so no key is added and
none retired.

Four more names were hand-copies of a StandardActions label — three
"Merge entries" and one "Automatically set file links" — and now come
from the action, which is where the text the user just clicked already
lives and where it will stay correct when the menu wording changes.

Nothing renders these yet: the sole reader is the warning ChangeSet
logs when part of a set fails to apply. P5 is what will show them, and
this is its prerequisite — a name written for a log is a name written
for a person, or P5 ships "Could not fully apply CHANGE_SELECTED_FIELD".
The javadoc on both types now states that rule instead of leaving it to
the field's type.

`AutomaticFieldEditorViewModel#cancelChanges` is documented rather than
changed: it reverts what the tabs already wrote and records nothing,
which is correct because nothing reaches the stack until OK — but it is
the one deliberate write outside the journal and read like the defect
`applyEdit` exists to prevent.

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_0194MmVeMweN5EKQEx5yNoC1

* Align step names that nearly matched an action label

Three step names described the command the user had just invoked, in
wording that differed from the command's own label:

    "Autogenerate citation keys"  ->  GENERATE_CITE_KEYS  "Generate citation keys"
    "Update keywords"             ->  MANAGE_KEYWORDS     "Manage keywords"
    "Replace string"              ->  REPLACE_ALL         "Find and replace"

Each now takes its text from the action, so the undo step says what the
menu item said, and stays right when the menu wording changes. That
also settles the casing drift, which was the visible symptom: "Replace
string" beside a dialog titled "Replace String" beside a menu entry
reading "Find and replace", for one operation.

A fourth, "duplicate removal", is deliberately left alone, because the
rule is not "use the action label" but "name what will be reversed".
Find duplicates only searches; the removals and merges come from the
user's decisions about each pair afterwards, so the action's label
describes something no undo can take back. A comment at the call site
says so, since the substitution looks obvious until you read the step.

"Update keywords" existed only as a step name, so its key is removed
from the English properties file — the same handling A3 gave the 19
presentation-name keys it retired, with the translations left to
Crowdin. The other keys stay: KeyBinding still uses them.

Nothing rendered these names before this commit and nothing renders
them after it, so no user-visible text changes today. What changes is
that P5 can surface any of them without first having to ask whether

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_0194MmVeMweN5EKQEx5yNoC1

* Document why the editor context menu has no Undo item

Undo and Redo in `EditorContextAction` act on the text control's own
stack. That is correct for the search field, whose text is not a value
of the library, and wrong for a field editor, where `Ctrl+Z` is routed
to the library's journal by the filter in `FieldEditorFX` (#11420): a
menu Undo would revert the control's text, the text listener would see
that as a fresh edit, and the undo the user asked for would land on the
stack as a new forward change.

`getDefaultContextMenuItems` has left both items out since 2019
(d1307a8bbf), so the hazard is already avoided — but the avoidance
rested on a parenthesis reading "(except undo/redo)", with nothing to
tell the next contributor why the omission is deliberate or what to do
instead. Both javadocs now say it.

No behaviour change; the two items are still built for the search
field, which is the one control they suit.

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_0194MmVeMweN5EKQEx5yNoC1

* Say what undo cannot take back

Undo covers the bibliography, not the file system (decision D7). Two
operations left the user to discover that for themselves.

Deleting a linked file removes it from disk and journals the entry's
`file` field, so undo brings the link back and points it at a file that
is no longer there. Renaming one is worse in a quieter way: the rename
happens on disk, only the link is journalled, so undoing restores the
old link — a name no file has any more.

Both already ask before acting, so both now say so at the point where
the user decides, rather than notifying afterwards about something
already done.

Not covered, deliberately: renaming to the suggested name, moving to a
directory, downloading, and the file cleanups have no decision point to
attach a sentence to, and a toast on every such operation is noise that
teaches people to dismiss toasts. The cleanup that renames PDFs already
asks its own "does not support undo" question, which is the pattern to
follow if the others ever grow one.

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_0194MmVeMweN5EKQEx5yNoC1

* Bring the CHANGELOG entries into house style

One sentence each, under twenty words, starting with "We fixed" and
"We changed", with no internals named. The links were pointing at
#16627, the already-merged predecessor of this branch; they are TODO
placeholders until this pull request has a number, per AGENTS.md.

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_0194MmVeMweN5EKQEx5yNoC1

* Guard the undo stacks by emptiness rather than by null

`Deque.peek()` answers "empty" with `null`, so reading the top of a
stack meant a null check in three places. `isEmpty()` plus
`getFirst()` says the same thing without one, and keeps the order that
undo needs: the inverse is applied before the entry moves across, so a
change that throws stays undoable.

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_0194MmVeMweN5EKQEx5yNoC1

* Point the logger at the class that owns it

The logger still named `UndoManager`, which is now the interface, so
every message from the journal was tagged with a type that has no
implementation of its own. Caught by `rewriteDryRun`.

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_0194MmVeMweN5EKQEx5yNoC1

* Resolve the undo journal where it is used, not at construction

`MainTableColumnModel` asked the injector for an undo journal in its
constructor, although only `getDisplayName()` needs one, and only for
a special field's label.

trimmed, undo everything still on the stack, and the library is the one

time. `clear()` keeps taking a fresh id, because it discards history the
library keeps — the two cases look alike and are opposites.

undoing everything lands.

subject: First class Theme Support in JabRef (#15798)
body:
* First class theme support

Themes become a real concept instead of a pair of hardcoded stylesheets.

A theme is now a single file that declares the complete JabRef color token
set (`-color-*`), once per `@media (prefers-color-scheme: light|dark)`.

Theme, color scheme and an optional custom stylesheet on top are now three
independent preferences (ThemePreset, ThemeColorScheme, customTheme) rather
than one overloaded value, with a migration from the old `fxTheme` key.

Two themes ship: JabRef and Primer, both implementing the same token contract.

ThemeTokenContractTest guards the contract: the base stylesheet may not
declare or hardcode a color, and every theme must answer every token in both
color schemes.

* Restore main's light surfaces in the default theme

Side pane, canvas, menu/toolbar, tab strip and quick-settings buttons
drifted from main. Add a -color-bg-sidepane token and re-tune the
surface literals to the values main derives.

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01TePt6cD61FGjdvtVGi37G2

* Paint inactive tabs and the entry editor toolbar with the canvas color

Matches main: tabs used -jr-background-alt (= -fx-background) and the
entry editor's side toolbar had the same fill, which the token
migration dropped.

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01TePt6cD61FGjdvtVGi37G2

* Add CHANGELOG entries for theme rework

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_0188qN6eR1tT6tjE3mPp4bo3

* Use sentence case for theme-related UI strings

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_0188qN6eR1tT6tjE3mPp4bo3

* Revert unicode escapes to literal characters in JabRef_en.properties

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_0188qN6eR1tT6tjE3mPp4bo3

* Bridge Modena lookup colors onto the Primer palette

Without the bridge, everything JavaFX or jabref-base.css resolves through
Modena's color ladders (-fx-text-base-color, -fx-text-background-color, ...)
fell back to Modena's light-grey defaults: the entry preview rendered
near-black text in the dark color scheme and the preview-layout combo box
text was invisible.

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_0188qN6eR1tT6tjE3mPp4bo3

* Run the theme preferences migration only once

upgradeTheme ran on every startup and the old fxTheme/themeSyncOs keys were
never removed, so each start re-applied the migrated value and overwrote the
theme chosen in the new UI. A fresh install was also forced from the
follow-system default to light, because themeSyncOs was read with default
false while the old preference defaulted to true.

The old keys are now deleted after reading them, an absent fxTheme key means
there is nothing to migrate, and the old themeSyncOs default is respected.

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_0188qN6eR1tT6tjE3mPp4bo3

* Paint the entry editor tab content area with the content surface color

The tab content area is transparent by default, so the window-canvas color
showed through behind the classic field tabs (e.g. user-defined tabs like
General), while the Main tab paints its own container. Painting the content
area itself makes all entry editor tabs sit on the same surface.

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_0188qN6eR1tT6tjE3mPp4bo3

* Fix preferences dialog colors and fix type

* fix nullabillity and improve test

* fix javafx threading issues on updateTheme

* watching

* add validators

* add tests

* Mention removal of -jr-* custom theme variables in CHANGELOG

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01NexrEs9itF7UUEbMRRu7p3

* Declare theme color tokens on .root so custom themes can override them

With the tokens declared on every node via '*', a custom stylesheet's
'.root { -color-...: ... }' is shadowed on each descendant by the node's
own '*' declaration and never takes effect. Declared on .root, JavaFX's
variable lookup walks up to the root and finds the override.

Fix Control key not being recorded when setting keyboard shortcuts on macOS (#16643)
body:
* Fix Control key not being recorded when setting keyboard shortcuts on macOS

The keybinding preferences UI checked isShortcutDown(), isShiftDown(),
and isAltDown() when capturing a new shortcut, but never isControlDown().
On macOS, Control is a separate modifier from Shortcut (Cmd), so pressing
Control plus any key was silently ignored and no binding was recorded.

Windows/Linux are unaffected since Control is already their Shortcut key,
so isControlDown() and isShortcutDown() fire together there; the fix is
guarded to only add the extra Control handling on macOS to avoid
duplicating the modifier.

Fixes #16604

* Fix Control key not being recorded when setting keyboard shortcuts on macOS

The keybinding preferences UI checked isShortcutDown(), isShiftDown(),
and isAltDown() when capturing a new shortcut, but never isControlDown().
On macOS, Control is a separate modifier from Shortcut (Cmd), so pressing
Control plus any key was silently ignored and no binding was recorded.

Windows/Linux are unaffected since Control is already their Shortcut key,
so isControlDown() and isShortcutDown() fire together there; the fix is
guarded to only add the extra Control handling on macOS to avoid
duplicating the modifier.

Also fixes upgradeKeyBindingsToJavaFX, a startup migration that
unconditionally rewrote any "ctrl+" substring to "shortcut+". This
predates Control being a distinct modifier and was only ever meant to
convert the legacy space-separated format (e.g. "ctrl A"); left as-is,
it would have silently rewritten our new intentional "ctrl+" bindings
back into "shortcut+" bindings on every app restart. The migration now
only touches strings still in the legacy space-separated format.

Fixes #16604

Switched the macOS-only tests from a manual assumeTrue(OS.OS_X) check
to JUnit 5's declarative @EnabledOnOs(OS.MAC), per maintainer review.

subject: Add entry from url (#16435)
body:
* Add UrlBasedFetcher interface and GenericUrlBasedFetcher

GenericUrlBasedFetcher wraps an arbitrary URL into a @Misc BibEntry,
populating url, a best-effort scraped page title (falling back to the
URL itself if the fetch fails), and urldate.

Part of #15411.

* Add "Enter URL" tab to New Entry dialog

Wires GenericUrlBasedFetcher into a new tab, placed after "Enter
Identifier", following the same async fetch -> duplicate-check ->
import pattern used by the Interpret Citations and Specify BibTeX
tabs.

Fixes #15411.

* Fix URLUtil.isURL() rejecting URLs with surrounding whitespace

isURL() matched the raw string against the URL pattern before
trimming, so a pasted URL with a leading/trailing space (e.g. from a
clipboard paste) was incorrectly reported as invalid, even though
URLUtil.create() right after it already trims. Trim once up front,
matching create()'s behavior.

This also fixes the same latent issue in the library-table paste
handler and the URL field in the entry editor, which share isURL().

* Add CHANGELOG entry for Enter URL tab

* Address Qodo review findings on URL entry fetcher

- fetchTitle now skips non-http(s) URLs (e.g. ftp://) before calling
  Jsoup, which only supports http/https and threw an uncaught
  IllegalArgumentException for anything else, aborting entry creation
  entirely. Added a regression test for this.
- Add an explicit 30s connect timeout, matching the existing
  DoiResolution.java convention, so a stalled host can't hang the
  background task indefinitely.
- Annotate UrlBasedFetcher and GenericUrlBasedFetcher with
  @NullMarked, per AGENTS.md's rule for new classes.
- Drop the string concatenation in the one Localization.lang(...)
  call that's new to this PR; left the identical pre-existing
  "An unknown error has occurred..." message (shared verbatim with
  two other tabs in the same file) untouched to avoid making three
  copies inconsistent.

* Guard Enter URL tab's deferred focus request against stale selection

Per Qodo review: Platform.runLater(() -> urlText.requestFocus()) could
fire after the user switches away from the Enter URL tab, stealing
focus back to a field that's no longer visible. Re-check
tabEnterUrl.isSelected() inside the callback before requesting focus.

Scoped to only this new tab -- the three sibling tabs
(switchLookupIdentifier, switchInterpretCitations, switchSpecifyBibtex)
have the identical unguarded pattern already, pre-existing and out of
this PR's scope.

* Address second round of Qodo review findings

- Move ENTER_URL to the end of NewEntryDialogTab. JabRefGuiPreferences
  persists the last-used tab as the ordinal index into values();
  inserting it in the middle shifted every later constant's ordinal,
  silently remapping existing users' stored tab preference. The tab's
  visual position (right after Enter Identifier) is unaffected -- that
  comes from NewEntry.fxml's element order, not the enum's declaration
  order.
- Capture the expected urldate before calling performSearch in
  GenericUrlBasedFetcherTest, not after. The production code also
  calls LocalDate.now() internally during its (real, network-bound)
  title fetch, so asserting with a post-call LocalDate.now() risked a
  midnight rollover making the test flaky.
- Add req~fetchers.generic-url~1 (docs/requirements/fetchers.md) with
  a matching [impl->...] tag, closing an OpenFastTrace coverage gap
  for this new feature. Verified via ./gradlew traceRequirements.

* Address qodo and revert isURL helper change

- Revert URLUtil.isURL() trimming: widening it to accept surrounding
  whitespace created a validate/consume mismatch for existing callers
  that pass the raw string to strict URI consumers. Trimming is now
  scoped to the Enter URL tab's own validator; the fetcher already
  trims before use.
- Log only scheme and host of a failing URL, since userinfo and query
  parameters can embed credentials or access tokens.
- Remove the enum ordering comment from NewEntryDialogTab (ENTER_URL
  stays declared last; the last-used tab is persisted by ordinal).

* Address suggested improvements (round 2)

- Document the UrlBasedFetcher contract (multi-hit, validation
  ownership, graceful degradation on optional data)
- Remove the redundant non-http scheme guard: jsoup rejects such
  URLs with a MalformedURLException before opening a connection,
  which the existing IOException handling already covers
- Strengthen the live-scrape test so the URL-as-title fallback no
  longer passes as a scraped title; tag only the three tests that
  touch the network as @FetcherTest so the rest run per-PR
- Simplify WorkerEnterUrl to Task<List<BibEntry>>; a single
  empty-result check remains in onSucceeded per the interface
  contract
- Use FetcherException's URL redaction for log, dialog, and the
  invalid-URL message instead of a hand-rolled sanitizer
- Only prefill the Enter URL field when the clipboard holds a URL,
  mirroring the Enter Identifier tab's guard
- Drop the never-rendered duplicate "valid URL" localisation string

* Reword generic-URL requirement and sort NewEntryDialogTab alphabetically
