subject: Fix undo A - Replace swing undo (#16627)
body:
* PLAN

* Make "Manage keywords" changes undoable

ManageKeywordsViewModel built a NamedCompoundEdit describing every keyword
change and then discarded it, leaving a `// TODO` in its place. Keyword
edits were therefore applied to the entries but never reached the undo
manager, so they could not be undone.

Pass the UndoManager into the view model and push the compound edit, guarded
by hasEdits() like the other call sites. The dirty flag needs no explicit
handling: LibraryTab already marks the library changed on
BibDatabaseContextChangedEvent.

* Add change model and UndoScope alongside the Swing undo stack

Introduces the value-based change model that later commits migrate the
undoable edits onto. A BibChange knows how to apply itself and how to
produce its inverse, so undo is apply(inverted()) rather than a second
hand-written method per edit type that can drift from the first.

ChangeSet groups the changes of one user action and is itself a BibChange,
so sets nest; UndoScope pushes only the outermost one, keeping one user
action to one undo step. Recording goes through UndoScope, which owns the
build/discard-if-empty/push sequence that every call site currently repeats
by hand.

Nothing uses this yet. ChangeSetEdit adapts a ChangeSet to the existing
Swing stack so that migrated and unmigrated commands can share it, which
keeps the per-command migration reviewable one command at a time.

module-info is the only existing file touched, to export the new package.

* Replace UndoableKeyChange with FieldEdit

A citation key is a field: setCitationKey delegates to
setField(InternalField.KEY_FIELD, ...), and setField routes a null or empty
value to clearField, which is what FieldEdit does. UndoableKeyChange was
therefore a FieldEdit with the field hardcoded, and its undo/redo pair
duplicated logic FieldEdit derives from a single inverted().

Its presentation name was unreachable (nothing calls
getUndoPresentationName), so the l10n key it used is now obsolete and is
removed from the English properties file.

Also generalizes the bridge from ChangeSetEdit to BibChangeEdit so a single
change can be adapted to the Swing stack, not only a whole set: the call
sites migrated here add one change to a compound edit they do not own.

Drops the BibDatabaseContext parameter from apply(). The first real call
sites showed the cost of threading a context everywhere -- MergeEntriesHelper
is static and has none -- while FieldEdit never used it. Changes now hold
what they act on, as the Undoable* classes already did.

* Replace UndoableChangeType with EntryTypeEdit

UndoableChangeType could be built from a FieldChange, whose values are the
type *names*. Undo then had to rebuild the type with
EntryTypeFactory.parse(change.getOldValue()), so a typed value made a round
trip through a string on every undo. EntryTypeEdit holds EntryType directly.

Three of the four call sites already had both types at hand and only passed
them through the string-based constructor by accident of the API. The fourth,
ChangeEntryTypeAction, now captures the previous type before setting the new
one instead of recovering it from the returned FieldChange.

The parse round trip was lossy in principle: for a type outside the standard
lists it produced a fresh UnknownEntryType rather than the original object.
UnknownEntryType compares by name, so nothing observable changed, but the
value no longer depends on parse agreeing with getName().

The presentation name was unreachable, so its l10n key is now obsolete and is
removed from the English properties file.

* Replace UndoableFieldChange with FieldEdit

Mechanical swap of all 28 construction sites across 21 files: the two
constructors map one-to-one onto FieldEdit, which derives its undo direction
from inverted() instead of repeating the set-or-clear logic in both undo()
and redo(). Two sites held the edit in a local variable and only passed it to
addEdit, so they change type but not shape.

Behaviour is unchanged everywhere, including AbstractEditorViewModel, which
still records one change per keystroke. Coalescing typing into a single undo
step is a separate concern and is deliberately not addressed here.

The presentation name was unreachable, so its l10n key is now obsolete and is
removed from the English properties file.

* Drop the stale "add undo" TODO in JournalEditorViewModel

toggleAbbreviation writes through the text property, and the bidirectional
binding installed by AbstractEditorViewModel#bindToEntry both sets the field
and pushes the undo edit. Undo has therefore worked here since recording
moved into that binding; the TODO and its commented-out call predate it and
suggested a gap that does not exist. A test pins the behaviour down.

Also removes imports that the previous commit added for names occurring only
inside that comment, plus an import left unused in UndoScopeTest and a stray
blank line in ChangeSet -- all three fail checkstyle.

* Replace UndoableInsertEntries/UndoableRemoveEntries with entry records

Both classes only wrapped a database, a list of entries and a boolean that
fed a presentation name nothing renders, so the booleans and their eight
l10n keys go with them.

Carries the event source explicitly. UndoableRemoveEntries.undo re-inserted
with EntriesEventSource.UNDO while UndoableInsertEntries.redo used the
default LOCAL, and the difference is load-bearing: the group listener in
LibraryTab auto-assigns added entries to the selected group and skips that
only for UNDO. Inverting a change cannot derive this, since the same
insertion means "restore" in one direction and "add" in the other, so both
records keep the source as a component. Defaults reproduce the old
behaviour, and tests pin both directions down.

* Replace the string and preamble edits with change records

UndoableInsertString, UndoableRemoveString, UndoableStringChange and
UndoablePreambleChange map directly onto StringInserted, StringRemoved,
StringEdit and PreambleEdit across six call sites.

UndoableStringChange selected between name and content with a boolean;
StringEdit.Part names the two cases, so the call sites no longer read as
`true`/`false` at the point of construction.

Five more presentation-name l10n keys become obsolete and are removed.

With this, org.jabref.gui.undo holds no Undoable* classes: what remains is
the manager, the two actions, the recorder and the bridge.

* Delete the unreachable group undo edits

UndoableMoveGroup and UndoableAddOrRemoveGroup have no live callers. Group
undo registration is commented out throughout GroupTreeViewModel and
GroupNodeViewModel, and the one remaining construction site,
GroupTreeNodeViewModel#addNewGroup, is itself uncalled: the "Add group"
button routes through GroupTreeViewModel#addNewGroupToRoot instead. That dead
method goes too.

Converting them to change records would have meant designing a representation
for tree surgery that nothing performs. UndoableAddOrRemoveGroup would not
survive being revived as it stands: it addresses the edited node by its path
from the tree root but starts traversal from the handle it was constructed
with, which the only call site passed as the parent rather than the root.

Whether group operations should be undoable at all is a separate question,
and a real gap -- but reinstating them is a feature, not a refactor.

* Make change record equality consistent and identity-based

Uses Objects.hash throughout instead of a hand-rolled 31* combination in the
two entry records, and compares every component rather than a subset: the
string records ignored the database they carry, and the entry records left it
out of the hash.

Extends the identity rule to BibDatabase. Its equals compares entry lists,
string definitions and preamble, all of which change while a record sits on
the undo stack, so a content-based hash would not stay put. PreambleEdit
relied on the generated equality and now compares the database by identity
like the rest. A test pins the hash down across a database mutation.

* PLAN

* Remove the last direct users of the Swing edit classes

UndoableModifySubtree was a stateful memento rather than a value: it captured
the post-modification children during undo() and replayed them in redo(), so
a redo that had not been preceded by an undo cleared the subtree.
GroupSubtreeReplaced holds both snapshots from the start, and GroupChange now
takes them either side of its mutation. A test covers the redo-first case the
old shape got wrong.

FieldRowViewModel used a private CompoundEdit as a two-state latch for the
merge/unmerge toggle in the three-way merge dialog. It was never pushed to an
undo manager, so it was Swing machinery standing in for a boolean and two
strings; it is now exactly that.

Neither class was reachable from the undo stack in the sense the rest of this
work is about, but both extended javax.swing.undo types directly and so had
to go before that dependency can be dropped.

* Collect changes in NamedCompoundEdit instead of Swing edits

NamedCompoundEdit now gathers BibChange values and folds them into a
ChangeSet, rather than extending CompoundEdit and holding UndoableEdits. Call
sites hand it the change itself, so the 56 BibChangeEdit wrappers that only
existed to satisfy the Swing type disappear, and nesting one compound in
another is a method rather than a coincidence of both being UndoableEdits.

end() is gone with the class it came from. A builder that must be sealed
before use is a state a caller can forget to reach, and the 29 calls to it
had no counterpart in the new shape; several sat inside `if (hasEdits())`
guards that then guarded nothing.

The bridge survives only where a single change is pushed straight onto the
manager. Those call sites are what UndoScope replaces next.

* Add UndoScope.push and wire one scope per undo stack

Registers a single UndoScope alongside the undo manager. Nesting is what
keeps a command that delegates to another from producing two undo steps, and
that only holds if every caller shares one instance.

push(BibChange) is for the sites that record exactly one change. Routing
those through record(name, ...) would invent a group and a name where there
is neither: a ChangeSet exists to hold several changes together, and its name
describes that grouping. Inside a record block push joins the enclosing step
rather than starting its own.

EntryChange collected its two changes in a bare CompoundEdit, which is now a
NamedCompoundEdit carrying the change's own name.

* Push one undo entry for a whole file import

ImportHandler built its compound edit outside the per-file loop but called
end() and addEdit() inside it, so the same object was handed to the undo
manager once per imported file. Importing three files left three stack
entries pointing at one edit, and the second undo threw
CannotUndoException because that edit had already been undone.

The compound is now pushed once, after the loop, and only if it collected
anything. It is a NamedCompoundEdit rather than a bare CompoundEdit, so the
step carries the name of the operation it represents.

* Add UndoRedoManager: the journal and its recording API on one object

Holds changes rather than Swing edits: a Deque of BibChange, undone by
applying the inverse, with JavaFX properties for menu enablement instead of
CountingUndoManager's balance counter bolted onto java.desktop.

Recording lives here rather than on a separate UndoScope. A command must be
handed the journal to record anything, so a second type would have to be
threaded through the same six layers of constructors the manager already
travels -- an attempt at exactly that was reverted. push and record are
therefore methods, and adopting them later threads nothing new.

hasChanged compares stack depth against the last saved position, which
reproduces the balance arithmetic it replaces: undoing back to where the
library was saved reports unchanged again.

Property updates go through UiTaskExecutor.runInJavaFXThread as before,
because commands push from background tasks too. Nothing uses this yet;
CountingUndoManager is still the registered manager.

* PLAN

* Replace the Swing undo stack with our own UndoManager

Swaps javax.swing.undo.UndoManager for org.jabref.gui.undo.UndoManager
everywhere. Keeping the type name means the ~160 references that pass the
journal around are untouched: for most files the whole diff is one import
line.

Call sites hand the manager a change instead of an edit --
addEdit(new BibChangeEdit(x)) becomes push(x), addEdit(compound) becomes
push(compound.toChangeSet()) -- so the two adapter classes that made a
BibChange look like an UndoableEdit have nothing left to do. With them go
AbstractUndoableJabRefEdit, CountingUndoManager, and UndoScope, whose push
and record are now methods on the manager.

NamedCompoundEdit stops extending anything and is simply the builder it had
already become. UndoAction and RedoAction check canUndo/canRedo directly
rather than throwing CannotUndoException at themselves to catch it one line
later.

jabgui no longer references javax.swing at all. The module still requires
java.desktop, but only for the AWT clipboard in ClipBoardManager.

* Rename AutomaticFieldEditorUndoableEdit to AutomaticFieldEditorChanges

The class extends NamedCompoundEdit and is no longer an UndoableEdit of any
kind; it collects the changes an automatic-field-editor tab made, plus the
count of entries they touched. Last name in jabgui referring to the Swing
concept.

* Retire three more obsolete localization keys

"Modified groups", "move group" and "unknown edit" were the presentation
names of the group edits deleted earlier in this branch. Found by the full
LocalizationConsistencyTest run rather than the per-step ones.

* PLAN

* Cleanups

* Record changes through UndoManager#record in three commands

ChangeEntryTypeAction, ManageKeywordsViewModel and SpecialFieldAction now run
their mutations inside a record block instead of building a compound, testing
hasEdits and pushing it. The build/check/push sequence stops being something
a command can get wrong, which is the defect PR 0 and the file-import fix each
repaired by hand.

record reports whether anything was recorded, because SpecialFieldAction
decides from that whether to notify the user -- previously the same question
answered by hasEdits().

ManageKeywordsViewModel#updateKeywords takes a ChangeRecorder and returns
nothing: it no longer has a compound to hand back, and its Optional<FieldChange>
plumbing collapses into recorder.record(...).

* Make "Replace string" undoable

ReplaceStringViewModel collected every replacement into a compound edit and
then dropped it: the view model had no undo manager at all, so replacements
were applied and the compound went out of scope. Third instance of the defect
PR 0 and the file-import fix each repaired, and the reason record() exists.

Recording through the manager also exposed that replaceField recorded a
change even when it found no occurrences, producing an edit whose old and new
values were equal. Harmless while nothing was pushed; now guarded.

* Record changes through UndoManager#record in three more commands

MergeTwoEntriesAction, RelatedWorkResultDialogViewModel and
UpdateOriginalEntry now mutate inside a record block.

UpdateOriginalEntry loses the boolean each helper returned to say whether it
had contributed an edit, and with it applyFieldChange: record() answers that
question for the whole block, and recorder.record(Optional<FieldChange>)
already handles the empty case.

UpdateOriginalEntryTest mocked the undo manager, which no longer works: with
record() the manager drives the mutation, so a mock that never invokes the
callback silently performs no work -- the type-change assertions failed
against an entry nothing had touched. It uses a real manager and asserts on
the stack instead.

* Move the JavaFX properties off UndoManager

The manager hopped to the JavaFX thread on every push to refresh its
undoable/redoable properties, so any unit test that recorded a change failed
with "Toolkit not initialized" and had to pull in ApplicationExtension. That
tax would have been paid by every command test converted to record().

The properties were never the problem -- those are plain observable values
needing no toolkit -- the hop was. So the hop moves to the observer that
requires it: UndoManagerProperties adapts the manager for menu enablement and
owns the marshalling, and the manager notifies plain Runnable listeners.

UndoManager is now free of JavaFX, which also unblocks moving the journal out
of jabgui later (P8). UndoManagerTest, ReplaceStringViewModelTest and
UpdateOriginalEntryTest no longer need a toolkit; UndoManagerPropertiesTest
does, and says why.

* Record changes through UndoManager#record in the cleanup and duplicate paths

DuplicateSearch and both cleanup paths now mutate inside a record block.
doCleanup takes a ChangeRecorder and hands its FieldChange list over with
recordAll instead of wrapping each one.

Restores thread-safety lost in the Swing removal: stack operations are
synchronized again, as javax.swing.undo.UndoManager's were. Cleanup and
import both push from background tasks, so the plain ArrayDeque that replaced
the Swing stack was racy. record() stays unsynchronized on purpose -- it runs
caller code, and holding a lock across that invites deadlock.

Also replaces a javax.swing.undo.UndoManager import that arrived with the
custom entry editor tabs merged in from upstream, after this branch had
removed the last one.

* Record changes through UndoManager#record in three more places

CitationRelationsTab and OpenOfficePanel convert directly.

GroupTreeNodeViewModel#changeEntriesTo loses most of its shape. It built one
compound for the removals, conditionally nested a second for the additions,
and chose between two push paths depending on which list was empty -- all to
express "this is one undo step, unless nothing happened". record() says that
directly, so the branching, the two result lists and the
UndoableChangeEntriesOfGroup factory that produced the compounds all go. The
mutations move inside the block, which is where they belong.

Not converted, with reasons:
- GenerateCitationKeyAction collects in call() and pushes in onSuccess, so
  the collection and the push are on different threads.
- SourceTab returns early from the middle of its mutation sequence when a
  field fails to parse. Inside a block that return would leave the method
  running and push the partial edits.

* Collect external changes through ChangeRecorder

DatabaseChange#applyChange takes a ChangeRecorder rather than a compound to
fill, so the nine implementations record into the caller's block instead of
into an object the caller then has to remember to push. Its three callers --
the change monitor, the backup review and the library merge -- use record(),
and MergeLibraryAction gets its "did anything happen" answer from the return
value instead of hasEdits().

EntryChange no longer wraps its pair of changes in a nested compound: the
enclosing block already makes them one undo step, and the nested name was
never rendered.

* Fold NamedCompoundEdit into ChangeRecorder

The two classes had become the same thing: a named list of BibChange with a
toChangeSet(). One was handed to commands by record(), the other constructed
by hand, and nothing else distinguished them.

ChangeRecorder is now the single collector. Its constructor is public,
because the commands that cannot use a record block still need one: those
that collect on a background thread and push on the JavaFX thread
(GenerateCitationKeyAction, LookupIdentifierAction, AutoLinkFilesAction,
ImportHandler, BatchEntryMergeTask) and SourceTab, which abandons the
operation part-way through when a field fails to parse. They call
addEdit(recorder.toChangeSet()) themselves, and the class says so.

MergeEntriesHelper and the automatic field editor take ChangeRecorder
throughout, so the same helper serves both the block form and the manual one.

* Record save-action changes through UndoManager#record

registerUndoableChanges only collects changes that already happened, so
neither reason for building a recorder by hand applies: nothing is mutated in
the block and there is no cross-thread hand-off. Nine lines become one.

* PLAN

* Cleanups

* Remove PLAN

* Fix undo stack defects found in review

Four regressions against the Swing stack this branch replaced, each with a test:

Recording state was a field on the manager, but there is one manager for the
application and long commands record from background tasks. An edit made
while cleanup-with-progress was running folded into the cleanup's step, and
two threads appended to one recorder's ArrayList. It is a ThreadLocal now, so
a block captures only the thread that opened it.

An empty ChangeSet is no longer pushed. Swing treated a childless CompoundEdit
as insignificant and skipped it; addEdit did not, so SourceTab -- which runs
on every focus loss of the code area -- and the automatic field editor pushed
no-op steps that Ctrl+Z then consumed instead of the user's real last edit.
Guarding in addEdit fixes both call sites and any future one.

undo() and redo() apply the change before moving it between stacks. Applying
first and popping after means a change that throws, such as re-inserting a
BibTeX string whose name has since been taken, stays undoable instead of
being lost from both stacks with the listeners never notified.

The stack is bounded at 100 again, the default javax.swing.undo.UndoManager
had. It retains the BibEntry objects of removed entries, so unbounded meant
every deletion of a session stayed reachable.

* CHANGELOG.md

* Reworded to reduce cognitive load in review

* Reworded to reduce cognitive load in review

* Checkstyle

* Minor refactor for clarity

* Reworded

* Reworded

* Moved undo classes to jablib

* Small fixes

* Move UndoManager to logic

* undo idea files change

* undo idea files change

* undo idea files change

* fix checkstyle

* Track the saved position by a counter, not by stack depth

UndoManager compared the undo stack's depth against its depth at save
time. The stack is capped at LIMIT and trims old edits off the bottom,
on the far side of the save point, so the clamp that kept savedDepth in
range was only ever wrong: saving with a full stack and making one more
edit pushed to 101, trimmed back to 100, and reported the library as
unchanged. No asterisk, and requestClose() skipped the confirmation.

Count applied edits instead - +1 per recorded or redone change, -1 per
undone one - and leave the counter alone when the stack is trimmed,
since a discarded edit stays applied. This is what CountingUndoManager
did before the Swing stack was replaced.

* Hold the undo lock only for the stack transition

Listeners lived in a plain ArrayList that addListener wrote without
synchronization, while notifyListeners iterated it from the synchronized
stack operations. Registering during a notification threw
ConcurrentModificationException, and - the quieter failure - a listener
registered on one thread had no happens-before edge to a push on
another, so a background edit could leave the menu silently stale.

Notification also ran while the monitor was held, against this class's
own rule that foreign code must not run under the lock. That was safe
only because the one listener defers through Platform.runLater and never
blocks; a listener that joined the JavaFX thread would have deadlocked.

Move the listeners to a CopyOnWriteArrayList, which gives both safe
iteration and the missing visibility edge for the cost of a copy on an
operation that happens a handful of times while the window is built.
Take the monitor for exactly the stack transition and notify after
releasing it, applying the change inside the lock since the transition
and the model write must not interleave. Run every listener even if one
throws: the change is on the stack by then, so propagating would report
a completed operation as failed and starve the remaining listeners.

With listeners off the lock, GuiUndoManager can update its properties
inline when the edit was already made on the JavaFX thread, instead of
leaving menu enablement a pulse behind.

* Added missing annotation

* Read the undo stacks when the property update runs

GuiUndoManager read canUndo/canRedo on the thread the notification
arrived on and carried the two booleans to the JavaFX thread. Between
the read and the post, another thread can read newer state and post
first, so the older values win and the menu offers an undo over an empty
stack until the next edit.

Read inside the queued task instead. Every update then writes what the
manager holds at the moment of writing, which makes a superseded update
a no-op by construction rather than something to detect with a version
token - and a token cannot be made to work here anyway, since it can be
claimed neither before nor after the read without leaving an
interleaving that discards the fresher value.

Updates stay uncoalesced: each reads current state, so all but the first
in a burst set the value already there, which a JavaFX property ignores
without notifying anything.

* Bound every wait in the undo tests

The concurrency tests waited without a timeout, so a regression hung the
suite instead of failing it, and a background thread that threw took its
exception to the default uncaught handler while the test still passed.
Both are already solved elsewhere in the suite: MainTableDataModelTest
and PreferencesFormBuilderTest bound every wait.

Submit the background work to an ExecutorService instead of starting a
thread, so the Future carries a failure back to the test thread, and give
every wait five seconds with a message saying what did not happen. Two
helpers next to setAuthor hold the plumbing, so each test body shows only
its own interleaving.

BackgroundTask is not an option here: it only runs when handed to a
TaskExecutor, and neither implementation fits - UiTaskExecutor needs a
JavaFX toolkit this test deliberately does without, and
CurrentThreadTaskExecutor runs the work inline, which is exactly the
second thread these tests exist to provide.

* Hand over a failed block's changes instead of dropping them

addEdit(String, Consumer) pushed the collected step only when the block
returned normally. A block that threw part-way through left the library
with whatever it had already changed and nothing on the undo stack, so
the user could not take it back - which is the defect this overload
exists to make unexpressible, surviving on its own exception path.
DatabaseChangeMonitor is the call site that shows it: one accepted
external change throwing mid-forEach stranded every change merged
before it.

Move the handover into the finally that already restores the recorder.
That covers any abrupt completion rather than RuntimeException alone, and
needs nothing captured and rethrown, so the failure keeps its identity
and propagates once the step is on the stack. A failing nested block now
hands its changes to the enclosing one for the same reason.

An empty recorder still pushes nothing, failure or not: an empty step
would enable Undo and let the next Ctrl+Z consume a no-op instead of the
user's previous edit.

* Checkstyle

* Share one GuiUndoManager, drop FX hops around pushes, apply-and-record changes

- JabRefFrame owns the single GuiUndoManager; Undo/RedoAction take it instead
  of each registering their own listener on the manager.
- UndoManager is thread-safe by design, so ImportHandler, LookupIdentifierAction
  and BatchEntryMergeTask push directly instead of hopping to the FX thread.
- UndoManager.apply / CompoundEdit.apply perform a change and record it in one
  call; call sites that wrote to the model and recorded the change as two
  separate statements now use it.
- addEdit(name, mutations): hand over after the try/finally and rethrow the
  block's failure afterwards; trim with `if` since one push adds one element.

subject: Detect concurrent modification of the library file when saving (#16646)
body:
* Detect concurrent modification of the target file when saving

Two JabRef instances (or any other program) writing the same .bib file
could silently lose one side's changes: AtomicFileOutputStream committed
whatever was written last, and on the in-place overwrite path (hard
links, non-atomic file systems) two concurrent writers could even
interleave into a corrupted file.

AtomicFileOutputStream now snapshots the target file's existence, size,
and modification time when the stream is opened and verifies it again
before committing (once before creating the backup, once right before
the move/overwrite). On a mismatch it throws the new
FileChangedException, keeping the concurrently written file intact;
SaveDatabaseAction surfaces this as a "file was modified by another
program" error to the user, whose changes remain in memory.

The encoding-problem retry in SaveDatabaseAction is moved out of the
writer's try-with-resources: previously the outer writer's close()
committed the badly encoded content after the re-encoded save, silently
clobbering it (and it would now trip the conflict detection).

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_013pZNCbTYVPumAQAKcnHRht

* Offer the external-changes review flow when a save hits a concurrent write

Instead of surfacing the FileChangedException in an exception dialog,
SaveDatabaseAction now shows a short notification that the library was
not saved and triggers the standard "External changes detected" review
flow. The change monitor is suspended during saving and thus never sees
the concurrent write itself, so LibraryTab gains scanForExternalChanges()
to start that scan manually.

Also adds the requirement req~logic.exporter.concurrent-save-detection~1
with impl/utest traces.

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_013pZNCbTYVPumAQAKcnHRht

* Fix PR number in CHANGELOG entry

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_013pZNCbTYVPumAQAKcnHRht

* Fix CHANGELOG link text to match PR number

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_013pZNCbTYVPumAQAKcnHRht

* Delete the freshly written backup when the post-backup conflict check aborts

The re-check after createBackup() could throw FileChangedException with
the .sav file of the aborted attempt left on disk, although no save
happened and the target is untouched. Backups are still kept for actual
commit failures (where they have recovery value) and with keepBackup,
where a backup file is expected to persist across saves.

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_013pZNCbTYVPumAQAKcnHRht

* Skip the external-changes scan when a "Save as" hits a concurrent write

The DatabaseChangeMonitor is created from the context's database path,
which is only updated after a successful "Save as". A conflict abort in
that flow would therefore scan the old library file instead of the path
that actually conflicted. The scan is now only triggered for plain saves
(target path equals the context's database path); a "Save as" conflict
keeps just the notification.

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_013pZNCbTYVPumAQAKcnHRht

* Keep external change detection registered while saving

Integrates the approach of PR #16613: instead of unregistering the
DatabaseChangeMonitor around a save and recreating it afterwards (losing
every event in between), the watcher stays registered and only defers
handling; one scan runs on resume. On top of that, a cheap size+mtime
guard skips the full library parse when the file matches the last state
known to be consistent with memory (library load, successful save, all
external changes merged), so JabRef's own writes do not trigger scans.

This makes the explicit post-conflict scan in SaveDatabaseAction (and
its Save-As guard) redundant: resuming the monitor now performs it,
against the correct (monitored) path.

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_013pZNCbTYVPumAQAKcnHRht

* Abort the encoding retry when the file was saved externally meanwhile

Addresses review finding F-01: the encoding-retry writer took its
concurrent-change snapshot only after the encoding dialogs were closed,
so an external save landing while they were open became the retry's
baseline and was overwritten without detection. The retry now verifies
that the file still matches the state committed by the first write and
otherwise aborts through the regular concurrent-save-conflict path
(notification plus external-changes review flow on monitor resume).

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_013pZNCbTYVPumAQAKcnHRht

* Detect an external save behind the encoding dialogs also without a retry

The guard from the previous commit only protected the "Try different
encoding" path. When the user instead clicks "Ignore" (or cancels the
encoding choice) after the dialog sat open for a long time, an external
save in that window had replaced the committed first write — yet the
save was reported successful, marking the library clean and recording
the external state as consistent: no review flow, and closing JabRef
would discard the in-memory changes without any prompt. Every exit of
the dialog flow now verifies the file still matches the committed write
and otherwise aborts through the concurrent-save-conflict path.

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_013pZNCbTYVPumAQAKcnHRht

* Route the concurrent-save guard state through one shared FileSnapshot type

The size+mtime baseline concept existed as three private copies
(AtomicFileOutputStream, DatabaseChangeMonitor, SaveDatabaseAction).
It is now a single public value type, org.jabref.logic.util.io
.FileSnapshot — a version stamp for optimistic concurrency control on
files — and the guard information flows through the layers instead of
being re-derived:

- AtomicFileOutputStream accepts an inherited expected baseline (so a
  follow-up writer can span a longer logical operation) and exposes the
  state it committed, captured immediately after the commit.
- SaveDatabaseAction passes the committed state of the first write as
  the encoding retry's baseline (the retry writer now detects the
  conflict itself) and hands the final committed state to LibraryTab.
- LibraryTab.resetChangedProperties(FileSnapshot) forwards it to
  DatabaseChangeMonitor.markConsistentWithDisk, which no longer has to
  re-read the file after a save — closing the window in which a
  concurrent write could be mistaken for the consistent state.

The monitor now also correctly treats "file absent before and after" as
unchanged (no scan), which the adapted tests cover.

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_013pZNCbTYVPumAQAKcnHRht

subject: Reintroduce custom entry editor tabs with two-column preferences UI (#16598)
body:
* Reintroduce custom entry editor tabs with two-column preferences UI

The entry editor rework (#16166) dropped user-defined tabs. Bring them
back with a preferences UI modeled on the Custom entry types tab: a
"Tabs" column (visibility checkboxes for built-in tabs, add/remove for
custom tabs, drag reordering for all) and a "Fields" column editing the
selected custom tab's ordered field list. Field names may be regular
expressions (e.g. comment-.*), which capture every matching set field of
the entry, refreshed live on field changes. A field listed on more than
one tab is marked with a warning sign.

Custom tabs are persisted under the pre-rework preference keys, so tabs
configured in older versions are picked up again without migration; the
combined tab order is stored in a new entryEditorTabOrder key.

Fixes https://github.com/JabRef/jabref/issues/16594

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_011R3RHnvsmkk2CHm4uEjVDa

* Keep duplicate-named custom tabs when applying stored tab order

Persisted data can contain custom tabs sharing a name (older versions or
hand-edited stores; the preferences UI prevents new duplicates). The
order map keyed by tab ID silently dropped all but the last such tab, so
queue tabs per ID instead and consume one per matching order entry.

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_011R3RHnvsmkk2CHm4uEjVDa

* Unregister entry listener when field tabs are disposed

BibEntry's event bus holds listeners strongly, so AllFieldsTab and
UserDefinedFieldsTab instances stayed registered (and retained) after
EntryEditorViewModel.disposeTabs() dropped them. Release the
subscription in dispose().

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_011R3RHnvsmkk2CHm4uEjVDa

* Coalesce deferred refreshes of user-defined field tabs

A burst of field changes (imports, fetchers) queued one Platform.runLater
per event. Track a pending-refresh flag so only one callback is queued,
and read the entry's state at callback time instead of the event payload,
so a queued refresh can never apply stale state.

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_011R3RHnvsmkk2CHm4uEjVDa

* Revert unrelated doc comment reindentation

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_011R3RHnvsmkk2CHm4uEjVDa

* Fix CHANGELOG link style (heylogs dot-space-link-style)

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_011R3RHnvsmkk2CHm4uEjVDa

* Store custom entry editor tabs as JSON map in a single preference key

Replace the low-level parallel numbered series (customTabName_i /
customTabFields_i) with one entryEditorCustomTabs key holding a JSON
object {"tab name": ["field pattern", ...], ...} in display order,
serialized with Jackson (already required by jabgui). The old series is
still read as a migration fallback and purged on the next store.

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_011R3RHnvsmkk2CHm4uEjVDa

* Move old custom-tab format handling into PreferencesMigrations

Convert the pre-v6.0-alpha.7 numbered series (customTabName_i /
customTabFields_i) to the entryEditorCustomTabs JSON key once at startup
in the migrations package, instead of a read-time fallback in
JabRefGuiPreferences. The old keys are kept for use by older JabRef
versions and ignored once the new key exists.

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_011R3RHnvsmkk2CHm4uEjVDa

* Keep custom-tab preference key private to JabRefGuiPreferences

The migration hardcodes the key name locally (V6_0_* convention), like
the other migrations, instead of exposing the constant publicly.

subject: Close stale PRs based on the age of the stale label (#16564)
body:
* Close stale PRs based on the age of the stale label

actions/stale measures days-before-close against the GitHub field
updated_at, which is bumped by activity that is not the contributor's.
PRs whose updated_at keeps moving are therefore never closed. The stale
label carries a fixed timestamp, so the closing is done from that.

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01XubvYCwnYXvmX8ZbRoBovx

* Do not exempt "dev: no-bot-comments" from the stale process

The label usually stays on a pull request even after
"status: changes-required" was set, so exempting it took most pull
requests out of the process.

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01XubvYCwnYXvmX8ZbRoBovx

* Do not cap the candidate list at 100 pull requests

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01XubvYCwnYXvmX8ZbRoBovx

* Re-check the required labels before closing

The candidate list is a snapshot; a label can be removed while the list
is being processed.

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01XubvYCwnYXvmX8ZbRoBovx

* Do not close pull requests that saw activity after the stale label

Nothing removes the stale label when a pull request from a branch of
this repository is pushed to: pr-comment.yml only does that for pull
requests from forks, and a human comment never removes it. Closing by
label age alone would therefore have closed active pull requests - three
of the five current candidates.

A push or a comment by a human after the label now drops the label
again, so the marking step can start a new round.

subject: Fix CI (#16559)
body:
* Scope JBang cache to OS

* Add debug for jbang.cmd

* Use Google Mirror

* Pin JBang version used by the JBang gradle tasks

With the default version "latest", the dev.jbang plugin fetches
version.txt from jbang.dev whenever jbang is not on the PATH -- with a
10 s timeout and no retries. A CI run already failed on exactly that.

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01XubvYCwnYXvmX8ZbRoBovx

* Route JBang's Maven artifacts into the cached Gradle user home

JBang resolves script //DEPS into ~/.m2, which no cache in this
repository covers, so every job re-downloads them from Maven Central.
Setting JBANG_REPO into the Gradle user home's caches/ directory reuses
the cache gradle/actions/setup-gradle already maintains.

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01XubvYCwnYXvmX8ZbRoBovx

* Drop setup-jbang and the ~/.jbang cache from the shared gradle setup

The dev.jbang gradle plugin installs JBang itself into
~/.gradle/caches/jbang, which gradle/actions/setup-gradle already
caches. Installing JBang and restoring/saving a second cache in every
gradle job is wasted work.

The two jobs that call `jbang` from the shell (jbang-check, ghprcomment
in pr-comment.yml) now set up JBang themselves. The `jbang --version`
debug output in binaries.yml is removed with it.

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01XubvYCwnYXvmX8ZbRoBovx

* Cache the JBang dependencies of the madrlint and heylogs jobs

Both jobs cache ~/.jbang, but JBang resolves the script dependencies
into ~/.m2, so only the built script jars were cached. JBANG_REPO moves
them into the directory that is cached anyway.

Also: the heylogs job used actions/cache/restore without a matching
save, so its key was never written, and runner.os in the cache keys is
constant for these two ubuntu-only jobs.

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01XubvYCwnYXvmX8ZbRoBovx

* Let renovate bump the pinned JBang version

The gradle manager is disabled in this configuration, and the version is
a plain Kotlin val anyway, so a custom regex manager against the
jbangdev/jbang releases keeps the pin from going stale.

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01XubvYCwnYXvmX8ZbRoBovx

* Cache the JBang dependencies of the remaining JBang jobs

jbang-check caches ~/.jbang with a shared key, so the "JBang (PR)" job
restores what "JBang (main)" wrote - both build the same scripts. The
jablib snapshot is published into that repository accordingly.

pr-comment does not run Gradle at all, so it no longer pulls in
setup-gradle just to get a JDK; it sets up Java and JBang directly and
caches ghprcomment's dependencies under its own key.

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01XubvYCwnYXvmX8ZbRoBovx

* Move the pinned JBang version to gradle.properties

versions/build.gradle.kts is a java-platform for Maven coordinates;
JBang is a CLI, not a dependency, so it has no place there.
gradle.properties is the central spot the build already reads
project-wide settings from.

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01XubvYCwnYXvmX8ZbRoBovx

* order caching, move to build gradle in versions

---------

subject: Match citation results against library in background (#16518)
body:
* Match citation results against library in background

The Citations tab fetched in a background task, but matched the results
against the library in the onSuccess callback, which runs on the JavaFX
thread. Each fetched entry scanned the whole library, so switching the
provider froze the window until both searches finished.

The matching now happens inside the background task, on a snapshot of the
library taken beforehand, and stops when the search is cancelled.

Fixes #16270

* Fix CitationRelationsTab.createBackgroundTask(): bind the cancellation check to the task itself via CitationRelationsTab.createSearchTask()

* Add back removed TODO over method CitationRelationsTab.snapshotActiveLibrary()

* Remove SnapshotLibrary as a parameter from CitationRelationsTab.executeSearch()

* Drop DuplicateCheckTest.containsDuplicateInCollectionMatchesDatabaseOverload() test: the BibDatabase overload now delegates to the collection one

subject: Quote heredocs holding text that must not be expanded (#16508)
body:
The "Conflicts with target branch" comment body is written with an
unquoted heredoc, so the backticks around `upstream/main` in

    Please [merge `upstream/main`](https://docs.github.com/...)

run as command substitution. Every conflict comment JabRef has posted
reads "Please [merge ](https://...)" with the link text missing, and
the step log carries "upstream/main: No such file or directory".

The same construct in issue-comment.yml is worse: it expands $PR_BODY,
which is attacker-controlled, inside a workflow that runs with
"issues: write" on a workflow_run trigger. A pull request whose body
contains backticks or $(...) executes them. That heredoc only echoed
the body for the log, so it is replaced by printf, matching the line
below it that already parses $PR_BODY that way.

Do not mark PRs ready for review when they enter the merge queue (#16483)
body:
* Do not mark PRs ready for review when they enter the merge queue

Adding the label "status: to-be-merged" triggered "On PR labeled", which in turn triggered "Adapt PR status". By the time that workflow ran, the merge queue had already merged (and thus closed) the PR, so "gh pr ready" failed with "Pull request is closed. Only draft pull requests can be marked as ready for review".

Skip the pr_number upload for that label and additionally guard the follow-up workflow against non-open pull requests.

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_013iW9FXUKZrjJTPbgzZFCE9

* Gate on the actual precondition instead of the merge-queue label

"gh pr ready" only succeeds on an open draft pull request, so check that directly. This also covers PRs that were closed for other reasons, and it is race free - "isInMergeQueue" is already false once the merge queue has merged the PR, which is exactly when the follow-up workflow runs.

Fold the label lookup into the same "gh pr view" call, reducing the step to a single API request.

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_013iW9FXUKZrjJTPbgzZFCE9

* Report why the PR was skipped instead of one lumped message

"PR is not an open draft" told a merged PR that it was not a draft and an open non-draft PR that it was not open. Report the two cases separately, including the actual state.

subject: Add auto-merge main workflow (#15785)
body:
* Add Merge main workflow

* Take PR number as workflow_dispatch input

`github.ref_name` resolves to `<PR>/merge` on `pull_request` events,
which is not a real branch. Switch the `workflow_dispatch` input from
a branch name to a PR number, resolve the head branch via
`gh pr view --json headRefName`, and fall back to `github.head_ref`
for `pull_request` runs.

* Pin maven-flow/merge to SHA and merge main into PR branch

- Pin `maven-flow/merge` to commit
  `1a008472b7a881f9fa6779c53e0118cdaf66da22` (v1) instead of the
  mutable `@v1` tag.
- Swap `source-branch` and `target-branch` so `main` is merged into
  the PR branch (not the other way around).
- Set `pom-file: 'match-nothing.txt'` since JabRef is a Gradle
  project and has no `pom.xml` for the action to bump.

* Use origin/main

* Fetch main before merge and use number input type

- Add `git fetch origin main:main` step so the local `main` branch
  exists before `maven-flow/merge` runs `git merge main`. The
  checkout step only fetches the PR ref.
- Switch `workflow_dispatch` input `pr` to `type: number` for input
  validation.

* Auto-merge main into PR branch on conflict

When a PR opened from JabRef/jabref has merge conflicts, automatically
attempt to merge main into the PR head branch via maven-flow/merge.

* Use origin/main as source branch for merge action

* Auto-resolve CHANGELOG.md-only merge conflicts without commenting

Restructure conflicts_with_target so the merge attempt happens before
any labeling or commenting: if maven-flow/merge succeeds (which is the
case iff CHANGELOG.md is the only conflicting file), the merge commit is
pushed and no ghprcomment is posted. Only otherwise, the existing
label + comment / failure behavior applies.

- Also try auto-merge for fork PRs that allow maintainer edits
- Set up Java on ubuntu-slim (required by the changelog merge driver)
- Use gh --jq instead of jq (not available on ubuntu-slim)
- Merge from upstream/main so fork checkouts do not merge the fork's main

* Make push-changes: true explicit on maven-flow/merge

The auto-merge exists to push the resolved merge back to the PR branch;
that behavior was relying on the action's implicit default. Make it
explicit at both call sites, since the push is the workflow's purpose
and its main risk (pull_request_target with contents: write).

* Resolve PR head repo/ref for pull_request trigger in merge-main

On pull_request runs the resolve step was skipped, so checkout used the
base repo (github.repository) with the PR head branch name
(github.head_ref). For fork PRs that branch does not exist in the base
repo and checkout fails. Resolve the head repo and branch for both
triggers - from the event payload on pull_request, via gh on
workflow_dispatch - and drop the mismatched fallbacks so repository, ref
and target-branch all come from the same source.

* Make the concurrency group PR-specific for manual dispatches

On workflow_dispatch, github.head_ref is empty and github.ref is just the
ref the workflow was started from, so dispatches for different PRs all
landed in the same concurrency group and cancelled each other. Put
inputs.pr first in the fallback chain; it is empty on pull_request events,
where head_ref still applies.

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_019EeELtq1gTCTwtamHXovxT

subject: Improve localization tests (#16443)
body:
* Ignore Localization.lang(...) inside Java comments

The localization key scanner matched `Localization.lang("...")` anywhere in
a source file, including commented-out code. Such keys were reported as
"used", which hid obsolete keys from findObsoleteLocalizationKeys.

Blank out the content of all Java comments (`//`, `///`, `/* */`, javadoc)
before scanning. String literals, text blocks, and character literals are
left untouched, so a `//` inside a string does not start a comment. The
blanked source keeps its length and line structure, so the existing
offset-based bracket matching is unaffected.

Seven keys were only referenced from commented-out Swing-era code and are
now correctly detected as obsolete; they are removed from
JabRef_en.properties. No translation file contained them.

* Check localization parameters in all modules

findLocalizationParametersStringsInJavaFiles walked `src/main` relative to
the jablib working directory, so localizationParameterMustIncludeAString
only ever saw jablib sources, while the missing/obsolete scans already
walked all five modules. Walk the same module list everywhere.

This uncovered seven `Localization.lang(variable)` call sites in jabgui.
All of them passed a variable that already held localized text, so the
outer lang() looked up an already translated string as a key, missed, and
fell back to that string. Drop the redundant call:

- WalkthroughRenderer: button texts come localized from the step builders.
- WindowResolver.title / NodeResolver.menuItem: take the localized text
  instead of a language key, matching what all call sites already passed.
- OOBibBase: errorTitle is assigned from a literal lang() call.
- InsertUtil: the two message parameters carried localized text that was
  re-looked-up only to substitute %0..%2. They become a FeedbackMessage
  callback so the literal key stays at the call site.

NodeResolver.menuItem("Preferences") in WalkthroughAction passed a raw key
where every other call site passed localized text, so the walkthrough could
not find the menu item in a non-English UI.

* Enhance parser readability

* Close the Files.walk streams of the module scanners

Files.walk holds a directory handle that has to be released, but the three
module scanners piped the walk straight into a flatMap and never closed it,
leaking one handle per module and scan.

Merge the three scanners into a single findInModules helper that consumes
each walk inside a try-with-resources block and skips modules without the
requested source directory.

* Remove the dead Menu localization bundle

LocalizationBundleForTest.MENU has no counterpart in production code:
Localization offers no menuTitle method, and no Menu_*.properties exists,
so getKeysInPropertiesFile("/l10n/Menu_en.properties") would have failed
with a NullPointerException had it ever been reached. Both callers of
findMissingKeys and findObsolete always passed LANG.

Drop the enum and the bundle parameter it was threaded through, together
with LOCALIZATION_MENU_START_PATTERN and the branches selecting on it.
LocalizationEntry keeps only path and key; its identity was the bundle plus
the key, which now collapses to the key alone.

* Simplify findMissingKeys to a single filter

The missing keys were collected into an ArrayList and that list was then
queried once per entry, so the final filter ran a linear scan per key. The
intermediate set of keys existed only to build that list.

A key is missing exactly if the English properties file does not contain
it, which is one filter over the entries and a set lookup per key.

* Stop mutating the key set returned by getKeysInPropertiesFile

findObsolete called removeAll on the set it got back from
getKeysInPropertiesFile and then copied the remainder into a new TreeSet.
That only works as long as the getter hands out a fresh mutable set, and it
builds two sorted sets to return one.

Filter the declared keys against the keys found in the sources instead.

* Fold the English key lookup into one helper

findMissingKeys and findObsolete both asked getKeysInPropertiesFile for the
same file. That method has no caller outside this class and was never used
with any other path, so it becomes a private no-argument getEnglishKeys.

* Read a Java file in one place only

getLanguageKeysInJavaFile and getLocalizationParametersInJavaFile were the
same ten lines twice, differing only in which JavaLocalizationEntryParser
method they called. Pass that call in and keep the reading in one place.

The line ending normalization stays: readString would keep the CRLF of a
Windows checkout, and the parser ends a line comment at \n.

* Select the files to scan by their extension

Both callers of findInModules passed a predicate that did nothing but
compare the file name extension. Take the extension itself, which also
retires isJavaFile and isFxmlFile.

* Report a missing properties file by name

getResourceAsStream returns null for a file that is not on the classpath,
and that null reached the InputStreamReader constructor, so a missing
bundle surfaced as a NullPointerException without naming the file. Check
the stream and say which path could not be found.

The resource was looked up relative to LocalizationConsistencyTest from
inside LocalizationParser; use this class instead.

* Collect with Stream.toList

None of the three lists is modified after being built, so the shorter
terminal operation does.

* Try to fix formatter check

* Fix missing nullmarked

* Try to fix formatter false positive

* Add Nullmarked

subject: Automatically fetch identifier metadata (DOI, ISBN, eprint, ISSN) in PDF merge dialog (#16264)
body:
* add reusable helper for identifier fetched columns in multi-merge-view

Takes a localized column title, an IdBasedFetcher, and an identifier
value, and adds the fetched entry as a merge source.

* Automatically fetch DOI metadata in PDF merge dialog

The "Merge PDF metadata" dialog only fetched full bibliographic data
for a DOI when the user noticed it and clicked a small per-cell lookup
button. Make this automatic: once a PDF-extraction source finishes
loading and contains a DOI, fetch and add a "From DOI" column without
requiring a click.

- MultiMergeEntriesViewModel: track already-fetched DOIs and add
  findNewFetchableDoi(), normalizing via DOI.parse so equivalent forms
  dedupe correctly and unsupported ones (e.g. XMP's "info:doi/"
  scheme) are skipped instead of failing at the fetcher.
- MultiMergeEntriesView: add enableAutomaticIdentifierFetching(),
  independent of the existing manual DOI button, which is left
  untouched pending reviewer input on whether it's still needed.
- PdfMergeDialog: opt in for PDF-drop imports only, other
  MultiMergeEntriesView callers are unaffected.

DOI only for now; ISBN/eprint/ISSN follow in a subsequent commit.

Part of #15415

* Generalize automatic identifier fetching to all types i.e ISBN, eprint, and ISSN.

Extend the automatic DOI fetch in the PDF merge dialog to the other
identifier types JabRef already knows how to resolve.

- MultiMergeEntriesViewModel: replace findNewFetchableDoi with
  findNewFetchableIdentifiers(), scanning all of
  FetchAndMergeEntry.SUPPORTED_FIELDS (DOI, ISBN, EPRINT, ISSN).
  Each field is normalized through its own identifier class
  (DOI/ISBN/ArXivIdentifier.parse, plus a small ISSN helper) before
  dedup, so malformed values are skipped rather than sent to a
  fetcher and failing, same as the DOI fix.
- MultiMergeEntriesView: resolve the fetcher per field via
  WebFetchers.getIdBasedFetcherForField() instead of a hardcoded
  DoiFetcher. Manual per-cell DOI button still untouched.
- Add a parameterized "From %0" localization key for the new column
  titles; the existing "From DOI" key is unchanged and still used by
  the manual button.
- Tests renamed/extended to cover ISBN and ISSN dash-normalization
  and checksum validation, and invalid arXiv IDs.

Known limitation (out of scope for #15415): whether this actually
triggers for a given PDF depends entirely on the five importers this
dialog already wires in (Verbatim, Embedded, Grobid, XMP, Content),
not on this change.

  - ISBN and ISSN: none of the five importers ever populate these
    fields from a PDF's content or metadata today, so this path is
    currently unreachable from a real PDF drop. It's fully exercised
    by unit tests instead (BibEntry built directly with the field
    set), and will start working the moment an importer is extended
    to extract ISBN/ISSN.
  - EPRINT (arXiv): PdfContentImporter.getArXivId() only recognizes
    an arXiv id if it's literally the first word of the first
    extracted line on the page. That matches older, plain-text arXiv
    stamps (e.g. arxiv.org/pdf/hep-th/9711200, confirmed working) but
    misses most modern arXiv PDFs, which stamp the id as rotated
    sidebar text that doesn't land in that position in the extracted
    text stream.
  - DOI is unaffected by either limitation and was confirmed working
    end-to-end before this generalization (previous commit).

A proper fix belongs in the importers themselves, not this dialog:
teach PdfXmpImporter/PdfContentImporter to extract ISBN/ISSN where
present, and make getArXivId() search the whole page text (or at
least the last line, where rotated-stamp text often ends up) instead
of only the first line. That's a separate, unrelated change and a
candidate for its own follow-up issue/PR.

Part of #15415

* Add CHANGELOG entry for automatic identifier fetching in PDF merge dialog

Documents the user-facing change from the two prior commits (automatic
DOI fetch, then generalized to any of the identifiers i.e ISBN/EPRINT/ISSN) as a single bullet
under Fixed, per #15415.
