subject: Preferences builder (#16386)
body:
* Implement for general and preferences

* Implement LinkedFilesTab

* Implement Entry tab

* Implement Network tab

* Implement XMP tab

* Implement EntryEditor tab

* Implement AutoCompletionTab and improve FormsBuilder for consistency

* Implement Ocr tab

* Implement Groups tab

* Implement Export tab

* Implement External tab

* Implement CitationKeyPattern tab

* Implement Ai tab, enhance fluent style of PasswordFieldEditor

* Fix Ai tab, Implement Table tab

* Implement WebSearch tab

* Improve fluent style in groups

* Fix traps

* Enforce compile time correctness

* Enforce compile time correctness

* Fix accumulating key event filters in preferences dialog

The CLOSE key filter was added inside the tab-selection subscription,
so every tab switch registered another identical filter on the dialog
pane. Register it once in initialize().

* Remove duplicate validation on preferences save

The view validated all tabs and then called storeAllSettings(), which
validates again. storeAllSettings() now reports success instead, and
validSettings() becomes private.

* Rename PreferencesTab.getBuilder() to getContent()

The method returns the tab's content node, not a builder; the name was
a leftover from the JGoodies era.

* Render preference tabs via the PreferencesTab interface

The dialog only displayed tabs that extend AbstractPreferenceTabView.
Use getContent() from the interface instead, so tabs are no longer
required to inherit from a specific base class.

* Decouple AiTab and WebSearchTab via shared dialog state

WebSearchTab took AiTab's aiEnabledProperty() in its constructor, which
coupled the two tabs and forced a construction order. Both now receive
a PreferencesDialogState: the AI tab publishes its master switch there,
the web search tab observes it.

* Move DonationPreferences to the welcome package

Every other preference data object lives with its feature (e.g.
gui.groups.GroupsPreferences); the donation prompt lives in gui.welcome.

* Document why memory-stick mode is not a preference tab setting

* Migrate NameFormatterTab from FXML to form builder

* Migrate ProtectedTermsTab from FXML to form builder

* Migrate ExternalFileTypesTab from FXML to form builder

* Migrate CustomExporterTab from FXML to form builder

* Migrate CustomImporterTab from FXML to form builder

* Migrate JournalAbbreviationsTab from FXML to form builder

* Migrate KeyBindingsTab from FXML to form builder

* Migrate CustomEntryTypesTab from FXML to form builder

* Fold AbstractFormTabView into AbstractPreferenceTabView

All preference tabs are now builder-based, so the split between the
FXML/@Inject base class and the form base class is gone: the base
resolves its services via the Injector and provides form() directly.

* Narrow constructors

* Replace PreferencesDialogState with a working copy of AiPreferences

The preferences dialog now creates a dialog-scoped working copy of
AiPreferences. The AI tab edits the working copy and flushes it to the
live preferences on save; the web search tab observes the working
copy's master switch to offer or hide the LLM citation parser. The
switch is mirrored live via a bidirectional binding, while validated
fields are committed only in storeSettings().

This replaces the ad-hoc PreferencesDialogState holder with the same
working-copy pattern ExternalTabViewModel already uses, and gives
AiPreferences reusable copyOf/copyFrom operations.

* Unify section variants through one funnel in PreferencesFormBuilder

All four public section methods now delegate to a single private
funnel, which also gives sectionWithHelp the config overloads its
plain sibling already had.

* Remove stringCombo from PreferencesFormBuilder

Its boolean/prompt flag parameters are expressible through the regular
combo variant plus configure(), which its single caller now uses. This
also removes the nullable parameters from the addCombo funnel.

* Let TagsFieldEditor own its value binding

BrowseFileEditor and PasswordFieldEditor already bind the value they
edit; TagsFieldEditor left that to the builder's tagsField method. All
editors now follow the same rule: an editor binds its own value, the
builder only places nodes.

* Deduplicate the CRTP self() cast in the element handles

ElementBase and ControlElementBase each carried their own unchecked
self() cast; the hierarchy now has exactly one, package-private and
final in the base class.

* Replace 22 empty config lambdas with a shared noConfig() helper

* Give hyperlink the config overload every other control has

* Name the layout magic numbers in the forms package

* Document the forms package contract in package-info

* Replace click-to-reveal password fields with explicit buttons

NetworkTab's proxy password and git PAT now use the reveal and clear
buttons like the AI tab; the legacy withRevealOnClick variant is gone.

* Source preferences search from the form builder, not a scene scan

The builder now records every visible text it is given together with
the node it captions (SearchableElement); tabs serve these through
PreferencesTab.getSearchableElements(). PreferencesSearchHandler
matches and highlights those elements directly instead of reflecting
over the scene graph, which also drops the questionable matching of
user-entered field contents and combo item lists.

* Show the tab heading as dialog chrome instead of per-tab title calls

PreferencesTab gains getTitle() (default: the tab name); the dialog
renders it in a fixed label above the scroll pane, so the heading
stays visible while the content scrolls. All 24 .title(...) calls and
the builder's title() method are gone; the five tabs whose heading
differs from their tab name override getTitle().

* Turn secondary controls into attachments on the element handle

Help buttons, browse buttons and inline value fields are no longer
separate builder methods but attachments made through the control's
own handle: help(...), browse(...), attachField(...) and a generic
attach(...) append the node right after the control — into its row,
or by wrapping its grid cell — and couple its state to it. Each
attachment's config lambda makes it fully addressable (validation,
disable bindings, the node itself).

This dissolves browseField, radioWithField, radioWithBrowse and the
BrowseFileEditor helper; checkWithField stays as sugar over checkbox +
attachField. With help available on every control, the RowElement /
ControlElementBase split collapses into the single InputElement handle.

* Attach section help through the section's own handle

The four sectionWithHelp overloads are gone: a section's help button is
now attached in its configuration lambda, exactly like the help button
of a control. Sections therefore have the two overloads every other
region has.

The region handles gained the shape the element handles already had —
RegionBase with a CRTP self(), FormRegion for regions without a heading
and SectionRegion for those with one — so help() is offered exactly
where a header exists and nowhere else.

* Route preference tab validation through the form builder

The builder's validate(status, control) hatch existed so that a tab
needs no ControlsFxVisualizer of its own, but had no caller: seven tabs
still kept a visualizer field, a setDecoration call and a
Platform.runLater block to decorate between one and four controls. They
now register those controls with the form, which already defers
decoration to the FX thread in build().

AiTab's expert grid is assembled outside the builder and receives it as
a parameter; CustomEntryTypesTab needs the controls marked mandatory,
for which validateRequired joins validate on both the builder and the
element handle.

* Give label and info the config overload every other element has

info() is now visibly what it is: a label plus the italic style class
and an indent.

* Drop the nullable icon parameter from button()

A button without an icon now takes the two-argument overload instead of
passing null, mirroring how the other optional parts of an element are
expressed.

* Group section with the other regions and name two more constants

Also records why custom() hands back a NodeElement even for a Control.

* Remove validateRequired

* Express the AI expert settings grid with the form builder

stackedField places a caption above its control instead of beside it,
which is the cell shape the expert settings need. The grid is therefore
no longer assembled by hand: it is two columns of three cells, and each
field validates through its own element handle again, so AiTab neither
builds a GridPane nor receives the builder as a parameter.

The columns now share the surplus width rather than being forced to
exact halves, so a column follows the width of its captions.

* Cover the form builder's nesting and stacked-field layout with tests

* Make columns regions actually equally wide

A columns region documents that every element inside becomes an equally
growing column, but only the surplus width was shared equally: each
column first claimed its preferred width, so a column ended up as wide
as its longest caption made it. Columns now claim no preferred width,
which leaves the whole row to be shared out evenly.

This restores the geometry the hand-built grids got from percentage
column constraints, without a configuration method for it.

* Remove customField from the form builder

The labelled-node hatch had a single caller, and its row is expressible
with a real field plus attachments — which keeps the caption in the
shared field column and drops the hand-assembled HBox.

* Fold comboItems into combo

The two differed only in setting the items versus binding them, and
every caller but one already passed a list property — for which the
distinction is invisible. The one literal list moves into its view
model, where every other tab's options already live.

* Manual adjustements

* Move owned disable bindings onto the element handle

The builder kept an IdentityHashMap of the disable bindings it had
installed itself, so that a later disableWhen could combine with them
instead of replacing them. That map had a single writer (the value field
of attachField) and a single reader (disableWhen on that very field's
handle), which is state of one element rather than of the form.

ElementBase now holds that binding itself, and attachField installs it
on the handle it hands to the configuration lambda.

* Remove redundant state from the form builder

Four cleanups of state that was kept twice or not kept where it belongs:

- build() checked that no region was left open, which region() makes
  impossible; the region is now popped in a finally, so the invariant
  holds by construction instead of being re-asserted.
- The next free grid row is the grid's own row count, so the gridRow
  counter that was incremented in addField and reset in ensureGrid is
  gone.
- Only SectionRegion uses the builder back-reference (to place help
  buttons on its header), so the field moved out of RegionBase.
- A section header row was built without spacing, leaving an attached
  help button flush against the title.

* Move validation of custom controls onto the node handle

The builder carried a validate(status, control) of its own, the single
method on it that configured rather than added, and thus the single
exception to the rule the DSL is built on. Its callers all had the shape
custom(node) followed by validate(...) for a control inside that node,
which is what a config lambda is for.

NodeElement now offers validate(status, control), so decorating a control
the builder did not create reads like every other configuration: inside
the element's lambda. The builder keeps only a private decorate(...) that
both handles share.

Also drops the GridPane branch of RegionBase.spacing(): a region is only
ever a VBox, HBox or FlowPane, so the case was unreachable.

* Simplify attachTo and unify disable-condition combination

Every field the builder places now sits in an HBox row of its own (same
shape checkbox()/radio()/stackedField() already used), so attachTo() no
longer needs to special-case GridPane cells: it just appends to the
primary's row.

Collapsed the owned-vs-user distinction on disable bindings: instead of
tracking which binding the builder installed first, every disableWhen/
followDisable call just ANDs another condition onto a running
combination. Applied the same rule to RegionBase for symmetry with
ElementBase. browse() now goes through attach() instead of re-deriving
the wiring; help() stays independent since it must stay clickable while
its control is disabled.

Also: validation decoration now waits for a real scene via a one-shot
sceneProperty() listener instead of Platform.runLater (which only
guarantees the next pulse, not scene membership), and PreferencesFormBuilder
is annotated @NullMarked (JSpecify) instead of using a runtime
requireNonNull check.

* Extract placeField to remove duplicated field-placement tails

field(), stringField(), addCombo() and tagsField() all repeated the same
"place in the grid, then wrap in an InputElement handle" pair. One private
placeField(label, control) now does both, so each caller is left with only
what actually differs between them: how the control itself gets built.

* Revert "Extract placeField to remove duplicated field-placement tails"

This reverts commit ee426791145931e7e8d461295f9a003d68db275f.

* Collapse ownedDisable into a single combined-condition field

The previous commit's message claimed this was already done, but the
rename never actually landed in that diff. Doing it now: ElementBase and
RegionBase each drop the owned-vs-caller distinction on disable bindings
and just AND every condition onto one running combinedDisable, via
addDisableCondition. attachField's CheckBox/ToggleButton branches route
through the same method instead of a separately named ownDisable.

* Rename PasswordFieldEditor.build() to field()

build() did no work of its own -- it was a plain getter for the
underlying EnhancedPasswordField, dressed up in builder-terminal
clothing to match the rest of the DSL's convention. Naming it build()
implied it finalizes or assembles something, which it doesn't; field()
says exactly what it does.

* Add null annotations

* Polish

* Fix comments

* Polish

* Consolidate icon buttons and share the form layout metrics

Three tabs each carried a private iconButton(text, icon, action) helper:
CustomExporterTab's and CustomImporterTab's were byte-identical, and
ProtectedTermsTab's differed only by not setting a width. ControlHelper
already owns this kind of factory, so it gains labelledIconButton (plus a
uniform-width overload for the button rows under the editable tables) and
the three copies go away.

OcrTab's iconButton was a fourth variant: same name, different parameter
order, icon-only with a tooltip -- which is exactly what
ControlHelper.narrowIconButton already builds, so it uses that now. This
gives those two buttons the standard narrow 20x20 icon-button styling they
were previously missing, so their appearance changes slightly.

JabRefIconView exists to make icons usable from FXML; it is a Group that
hosts icon.getGraphicNode() and stays unclassed so the hosted child does
the theming. Constructing one from Java therefore only adds a wrapper, so
the six remaining Java uses in this package now call getGraphicNode()
directly (and withSize(24).getGraphicNode() for the one sized case).

Finally, the gap and button width the builder lays out with were private
to it, so every tab building part of its view by hand re-typed 10.0.
FormMetrics names both, and PreferencesFormBuilder, AbstractPreferenceTabView
and the tabs share them. The remaining 100.0 literals are table column
widths -- the same number for an unrelated reason -- and are left alone.

* Hold the tab's single form in a field instead of a list

Every tab calls form() exactly once, so the List, the ArrayList, and the
stream/flatMap in getSearchableElements were machinery for a collection
that never held more than one element.

Calling form() twice is now rejected outright rather than quietly
supported: the second builder's tree is what the tab shows, so the first
form's texts would be collected for the preferences search while the nodes
they point at are not in the scene.

* Let the form be the tab's content instead of nesting it in the tab

AbstractPreferenceTabView extended VBox and set its spacing, and every tab
then added the form's own VBox -- with the same spacing -- as its single
child. So each of the 24 tabs shipped a pane wrapping exactly one pane
configured identically, and which of the two owned the layout was a
coin toss.

The tab is no longer a node. It implements PreferencesTab and nothing
else, holding the built form as its content; the tabs hand that over with
setContent(...) rather than getChildren().add(...). The dialog is
unaffected: it only ever consumed getContent(), and the style class and
width binding it applies now land on the form root, which is the outermost
node either way.

* Fix error

* Add table() and buttonRow() so the list tabs stop reaching for custom()

Every tab used the custom(Node) hatch, and the shape it most often
escaped to was the same one: a TableView followed by a right-aligned row
of actions. Five tabs hand-rolled that row, and of the four with a table,
two set VBox.setVgrow on it and two did not -- so a short list left a gap
in half of them.

table() takes the height by default, which settles that inconsistency,
and returns an InputElement so a table can carry validation like any
other control. buttonRow() takes ready-made buttons, since what they do
is the tab's business.

CustomExporterTab, CustomImporterTab, ExternalFileTypesTab and
ProtectedTermsTab now use both and no longer call custom() at all.

The remaining custom() callers are a genuinely different shape -- a table
beside a vertical strip of buttons, or a filter box above one -- and are
left alone rather than forced through a primitive that does not fit.

Also fixes two compile errors introduced by the previous commit:
PreviewTab called startDragAndDrop on the tab, which resolved only while
the tab was itself a VBox. It now starts the gesture on the ListView the
handler is registered on, which is the more precise drag source anyway.

* Fix formatting

* Fix l10n

* Weird formatting

* Fix comment

* Fix checkstyle

* add mocks

* Fix rewrite

* Fix l10n

* Qodo comments and small fixes

* Make disable argless

* Make attached fields follow their control's disabled state

attachField placed the field as a sibling of the primary control in the
same row, so JavaFX disable inheritance never reached it. On a checkbox
or radio only the selection condition was installed, leaving the field
enabled when the toggle was disabled while still selected.

Install followDisable unconditionally and keep the selection condition on
top of it; addDisableCondition ORs, so a toggle-attached field is now
disabled when the primary is disabled or unselected.

No call site changes behavior today: no toggle with an attached field
carries its own disableWhen, and region-level disabling already reached
both nodes through the shared row.

* Address review findings on the preferences builder

- GeneralTab: the custom theme path row is disabled again while "Use
  System Preference" is checked, as the old FXML did on top of the
  theme != CUSTOM condition
- PreferencesFormBuilder: radio() outside a radioGroup() now throws
  instead of silently producing non-exclusive radios; radioGroup()
  restores the enclosing toggle group in a finally; the combinedDisable
  docs now say OR-combined, matching either()
- Add a reflective completeness test for AiPreferences.copyFrom, which
  the preferences dialog relies on to flush the working copy on save:
  a newly added property missing from copyFrom now fails the test
  instead of silently never persisting

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01KrP1Ek8sXMXoSywmqFy2jd

* Add and implement ADR for searchable and custom nodes

* Create ADR for preferences scanning

* docs: cover attach() in the preferences search ADR

The builder opens the same gap twice: custom(Node) takes a node the
caller assembled, attach(Node) a node the caller appends after a
control it placed. Both are scanned, so record attach() as an escape
hatch of the decision rather than only custom().

* docs: use markdown links in the preferences javadoc

The preferences package documents itself with markdown doc comments,
but kept the javadoc tags inside them: {@link} and {@code} render as
literal text there. Replace them with [reference] and backticks, and
drop the tags from a line comment where they never rendered at all.
{@value} stays, having no markdown equivalent.

* Improve javadoc for PreferencesFormBuilder

subject: Fail closed when checking for an existing conflict comment (#16381)
body:
* Fail closed when querying PR comments in conflict workflow

The "already commented about conflicts?" check ran `gh api graphql | jq |
grep -q ... && echo true || echo false` inside `set -ex` without
`pipefail`. A failing `gh api` was swallowed twice: once by the pipeline
(exit status came from `grep`), once by `|| echo "false"`. The step then
exited 0 and posted a duplicate conflict comment instead of failing.

Capture the comment bodies into a variable and grep that, so an API error
aborts the step via `set -e`, and add `pipefail` to guard future pipes.

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_019EeELtq1gTCTwtamHXovxT

* Do not let xtrace echo PR comment bodies into the Actions log

Capturing the GraphQL result in COMMENT_BODIES made "set -x" print the
expanded assignment - all 20 comment bodies - into the workflow log.
Redirect to a file and grep that instead: xtrace prints the command, not
the redirected data, and "set -e" still aborts the step if "gh api" fails.

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_019EeELtq1gTCTwtamHXovxT

subject: Add shell.nix providing the native libraries JavaFX needs on NixOS (#16399)
body:
* Add shell.nix providing the native libraries JavaFX needs on NixOS

JabRef consumes JavaFX as Maven artifacts, so the natives ship as
prebuilt .so files inside the jars. JavaFX extracts them to
~/.openjfx/cache/<version>/amd64/ and dlopens them from there. They
carry no RPATH and are not patchelf'ed, so the GTK/X11 stack they link
against must be reachable via LD_LIBRARY_PATH, which NixOS does not
provide globally. Without it, ./gradlew :jabgui:run fails with
"UnsatisfiedLinkError: no glass in java.library.path".

programs.nix-ld does not cover this: it supplies an ELF interpreter
(which is what lets the Gradle-provisioned Corretto toolchain run) plus
a small default library set that contains no X11 or GTK.

Also add xvfb-run for the GUI tests, and document the error and the
fix in the local-workspace troubleshooting guide.

* Add a bootstrap JDK to shell.nix and document the nix-ld prerequisite

The shell provided no JDK, so `./gradlew` could not start on a clean
NixOS box: the wrapper is a shell script needing an existing `java`, and
toolchain auto-provisioning only happens later, from inside that JVM.
This went unnoticed because a JDK in the user profile leaked into the
non-pure shell. Add pkgs.jdk25 and set JAVA_HOME. It is a bootstrap only
-- Gradle still resolves the pinned Amazon toolchain for compiling and
running JabRef, verified via `./gradlew javaToolchains`.

The documented commands also silently required `programs.nix-ld.enable`,
because the auto-provisioned Corretto asks for
/lib64/ld-linux-x86-64.so.2, which NixOS lacks by default. A shell cannot
provide that, so document it as a prerequisite and warn on shell entry
when the interpreter is missing, instead of failing later with a bare
"No such file or directory".

* Edit special fields with the same icon controls as the main table

The entry editor rendered special fields (ranking, priority, read status,
printed, quality, relevance) as plain text fields. They now use the same
icon-based selection as the main table's special field columns: a star

subject: Do not warn on DOI mismatch that differs only in the http(s) prefix (#16280)
body:
* Do not warn on DOI mismatch that differs only in the http(s) prefix

The DoiFetcher compared the fetched entry's raw DOI field string against
the bare requested DOI. That flagged a mismatch whenever the resolver
returned the DOI as a URL (https://doi.org/10.x vs 10.x), and the filter
was inverted so it warned on identical DOIs instead of differing ones.

Compare both sides as parsed DOI objects instead: DOI.equals already
normalizes away the http(s) prefix and letter case, so the warning now
fires only on a genuine DOI difference.

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01X3wNLCcRSZh7oTcf2FUmLz

* Warn on present-but-unparsable DOI field instead of skipping silently

Comparing via flatMap(DOI::parse) collapsed "invalid DOI value" into the
same empty Optional as "no DOI field", so a present-but-unparsable DOI
was silently skipped by both the mismatch check and the missing-field
check. Split the three cases explicitly: missing field, present-but-
unparsable value, and parsed-but-different DOI each get their own warning.

subject: Show error box to users during critical errors (#16281)
body:
* Show error dialog on critical startup failures

If start() throws before the main window exists, the exception was only
logged, leaving users with a silent crash and no way to tell what went
wrong short of digging through the log file. showStartupErrorDialog()
now surfaces it via a ControlsFX ExceptionDialog, skipping initOwner()
when the stage has no Scene yet (openWindow() sets it later), since
JavaFX throws a NullPointerException from initOwner() on a sceneless
owner. FallbackExceptionHandler is also installed earlier, before
initialize(), so background threads started during startup are covered
too.

Fixes #14967

* Use Markdown Javadoc links, drop dead null check, add UX requirement

Switches {@link} to the project's Markdown-link Javadoc convention,
removes a mainStage != null check that can never be false (mainStage
is assigned unconditionally as the first statement in start()'s try
block, before any exception this method handles can occur), and adds
a docs/requirements/ux.md entry for the startup-error-dialog guarantee
introduced in the previous commit, linked from the code via impl->req.

* Address Qodo review: localize FallbackExceptionHandler message, fix NPE risk

Two issues from Qodo's review on #16281:
- "Uncaught exception occurred in " + thread was a hardcoded string;
  now goes through Localization.lang with a %0 placeholder.
- FallbackExceptionHandler's callback called DialogService directly,
  which can NPE via initOwner() the same way the startup-crash path
  did before being fixed — it can fire for a background-thread
  exception before initialize() creates DialogService, or before
  openWindow() gives mainStage a Scene. Unified both callers into
  showCriticalErrorDialog(), which already had the safe fallback.

subject: Fix inspire texkey arxiv import (#16235)
body:
* Use INSPIRE texkeys for arXiv-based imports and merges

isidore.science and #12292 describe the same class of bug: when an
entry has no manually-assigned (journal) DOI, ArXivFetcher's own
merge logic still adopted whatever citation key the automatically
assigned arXiv DOI's CrossRef metadata suggested, which is usually
just that DOI's URL (e.g. https://doi.org/10.48550/arxiv.1405.2249).

- ArXivFetcher now falls back to querying INSPIRE (the standard
  literature database for high-energy physics) for a curated texkey
  whenever the entry would otherwise end up with no key or a
  URL-shaped one. Most arXiv categories aren't indexed by INSPIRE, so
  a miss there is expected and leaves the entry unchanged.
- MergingIdBasedFetcher dropped the citation key entirely when
  merging fetched data into an existing library entry, since citation
  key isn't a regular BibEntry field. It's now carried over unless the
  library entry already has one.
- MergeEntriesHelper (used by the "update with bibliographic
  information" batch action) never touched the citation key at all
  when applying a merge result back onto a library entry. It now
  adopts the fetcher-provided key the same way, with undo support,
  but never overwrites a key the entry already has.

A prior attempt at this (PR #15038) was closed for being too broad
(touched all fetchers instead of just this case) and lacking tests;
this change is scoped to the exact URL-shaped-key symptom and adds
coverage in ArXivFetcherTest and MergeEntriesHelperTest.

* Use Markdown Javadoc link syntax instead of legacy {@link} tags

* Apply IntelliJ code style formatting to ArXivFetcher

Fixes indentation on a Javadoc continuation line and a fluent
stream chain that the required CI formatting check flagged.

* Fix Javadoc continuation indentation flagged by CI formatter

Apply the exact patch produced by JabRef's CI formatting check
(the local IntelliJ install used a slightly different alignment).

* Avoid wrapped Javadoc @param continuation line

The IntelliJ CI formatter kept demanding more indentation on this
continuation line each run without converging. Move the EPRINT
detail to its own paragraph so @param fits on one line, sidestepping
the unstable continuation-indent formatting rule entirely.

* Address Qodo review findings on INSPIRE texkey import

- MergingIdBasedFetcher: exclude the citation key field from the
  generic field merge so it can no longer be silently overwritten
  before updateCitationKeyFromSource's non-overwrite check runs.
- ArXivFetcher: replace Optional.get() calls with an ifPresent chain,
  and treat a 404 from INSPIRE (paper not indexed) as an expected
  miss logged at trace level instead of a debug-level stack trace.

* Explain why URL-shaped citation keys are filtered in ArXivFetcher

Spell out two things that weren't obvious from the code alone:

- Why a URL-shaped key is filtered out and treated the same as no
  key at all: for arXiv-only preprints, BibEntry#mergeWith copies
  over whatever key the auto-assigned arXiv DOI's metadata suggests,
  which is usually just that DOI's own URL. Without this filtering,
  a plain "is a key present?" check would treat that URL as already
  resolved and skip the INSPIRE lookup entirely.

- Why the check uses Optional#filter to do this filtering instead of
  isPresent() + get(): filter lets both "no key" and "URL-shaped key"
  collapse into the same empty-Optional outcome without ever
  unwrapping the Optional, matching the Optional-idiom fix applied
  elsewhere in this file per review feedback.

subject: Fix PDF title extraction misreading kerns as word boundaries (#16246)
body:
* Fix PDF title extraction misreading kerns and gluing pages

The word-gap heuristic in TitleExtractorByFontSize compared the absolute
X advance between glyphs against a fixed 1pt threshold. TeX output kerns
pairs like "T"/"o" tighter than the previous glyph's advance width, which
exceeds 1pt at title font sizes and was misread as a word boundary
("T opology"). Word gaps now require a positive advance of at least a
quarter of the font's space width; an explicit backward-jump check keeps
inserting the space at title line wraps, which previously piggybacked on
the absolute-value comparison.

Title candidates are also collected per page instead of concatenating
same-font-size text across pages, which glued figure labels from page two
onto page-one titles. Candidates still compete on font size across the
scanned pages, so titles behind cover sheets keep winning.

body:
* HayagrivaImporter created and implemented to the list of importers.

* HayagrivaImporterTest created.

* Add changelog entry for HayagrivaImporter

* Fix code formatting

* Catch JacksonException instead of generic Exception in isRecognizedFormat

* Improve null-safety, add Reader overload, and add upstream basic.yml fixture test

* Improve null-safety, add Reader overload, and add and fix upstream basic.yml fixture test

* Compare full BibEntry in round-trip tests, add ParameterizedTest

* trigger CI re-check

* Remove redundant BibEntryAssert method, use plain assertEquals for BibEntry

* trigger CI re-check

* HayagrivaImporter created and implemented to the list of importers.

* HayagrivaImporterTest created.

* Add changelog entry for HayagrivaImporter

* Fix code formatting

* Catch JacksonException instead of generic Exception in isRecognizedFormat

* Improve null-safety, add Reader overload, and add upstream basic.yml fixture test

* Improve null-safety, add Reader overload, and add and fix upstream basic.yml fixture test

* Compare full BibEntry in round-trip tests, add ParameterizedTest

* trigger CI re-check

* Remove redundant BibEntryAssert method, use plain assertEquals for BibEntry

* trigger CI re-check

* relax HayagrivaImporter.isRecognizedFormat to avoid false negatives

* Optimize HayagrivaImporter memory usage during format recognition

* Support Hayagriva's polymorphic YAML structures in the importer

Parse the untyped node tree instead of fixed POJOs so that fields with
several allowed shapes (title/url as string or map, author/editor as
string, list, or maps, parent as map or list, serial-number as scalar
or map) import instead of throwing. The upstream basic.yml fixture now
imports fully and becomes the primary test file, as required by #15714.

Also:
- match entry types case-insensitively (upstream files use "type: Article")
- recognize all Hayagriva entry types, importing unmapped ones as Misc
- map thesis/report to the exact Thesis/Report types the exporter collapses from
- return an error ParserResult for malformed YAML instead of throwing
- map parent by its type (periodical -> journal incl. volume/issue/publisher,
  book -> series/booktitle, proceedings/anthology/conference -> booktitle)
- import editor, volume, issue, pages, chapter, edition, publisher, location,
  organization, note, abstract, language

* Preserve remaining Hayagriva data via standard and custom BibTeX fields

Scalar serial-numbers (RFC numbers, version strings, ...) go to number
unless issue already claimed it; the pmid/arxiv/serial map keys map to
pmid, eprint (+eprinttype), and number. affiliated roles land in the
matching BibTeX field where one exists (e.g. translator) and otherwise
in a custom field named after the role. runtime and time-range become
custom fields; page-total and volume-total map to pagetotal/volumes.

* Make the Hayagriva exporter symmetric to the importer

The exporter layout now writes chapter, top-level volume (when no
journal parent claims it), page-total, volume-total, language, runtime,
time-range, pmid, and an affiliated block covering all Hayagriva
person roles (translator, director, cast-member, ...), so everything
the importer reads survives an export.

Person values are kept in BibTeX's structured "Family, Given" form on
import instead of being flattened to "Given Family"; the structured
map form (name/given-name) is converted to it as well.

A new round-trip test case covers the added fields end to end.

* Attribute the basic.yml test fixture to the Hayagriva project

The fixture is taken from typst/hayagriva's test suite (MIT OR
Apache-2.0); record source and license in external-libraries.md and in
a header comment in the file itself.

* Shorten exporter CHANGELOG entry and link the PR

* Keep approximate-date marker, tighten description, link the spec

Hayagriva's leading `~` on dates is imported verbatim instead of being
stripped - JabRef stores the raw string even when it cannot parse it,
so keeping the marker loses nothing while dropping it loses data.
The importer description is shortened to "Importer for the Hayagriva
YAML format." and the recognized-types constant now deep-links the
entry-type section of the Hayagriva specification.

* Shrink recognition lookahead to a realistic budget and make it reset-safe

3000 characters comfortably cover leading comments plus the first
entry, whose type key conventionally appears within its first lines.
The scan now block-reads exactly the marked budget instead of using
readLine(), which could read past the mark limit on a single overlong
line and make reset() throw; this also makes the separate line cap
redundant.

subject: Fix ISIDORE fetcher SSL handshake failure (#16229)
body:
* Fix ISIDORE fetcher SSL handshake failure

isidore.science rotated its certificate to a root (HARICA TLS ECC Root
CA 2021) that was missing from the bundled truststore. Separately,
URLDownload was building a blank SSLContext on every connection
instead of using the JVM's configured default, which silently
bypassed TrustStoreManager's merged trust list for every fetcher, not
just this one.

- Use SSLContext.getDefault() instead of a bare TLSv1.2 context with
  null trust managers, so the custom trust store actually takes effect
- Add the missing HARICA TLS ECC Root CA 2021 certificate to
  truststore.jks
- Install the trust store before ISIDOREFetcherTest runs, since tests
  don't go through the app's Launcher bootstrap; re-enable the test
- Bump org.gradlex:java-module-testing to 1.8.1, matching upstream,
  to fix a Gradle 9.5.0 incompatibility that otherwise blocks running
  this test suite at all

Verified with a real ./gradlew fetcherTest run against the live API
(0 failures) and a full jablib:test regression pass.

* Add CHANGELOG entry for ISIDORE fetcher SSL fix

* Use Markdown Javadoc style and @TempDir per checklist

Switch the trust-store setup comment from legacy {@code}/{@link}
JavaDoc tags to the project's Markdown Javadoc style, and use a
static @TempDir field instead of manually creating a temp directory.

* Remove unused Files import flagged by checkstyle

* Merge newly bundled certificates into existing truststores

Qodo review: createTruststoreFileIfNotExist only copied the bundled
truststore.jks when the per-user file didn't exist yet, so upgrading
JabRef installations kept their old truststore and never picked up
the HARICA TLS ECC Root CA 2021 root added in this fix. Merge any
bundled certificate missing from an existing truststore instead of
skipping it outright, and add a test covering that merge.

Also rewrote the CHANGELOG entry in user-facing terms instead of
naming internal classes, per review feedback.

subject: Fix html-to-node preview font size: convert pt to CSS px (#16197)
body:
ThemeManager sets -fx-font-size in CSS `pt` units, but JavaFX's Font API
(Font.font(size)) takes CSS pixels (user units), not typographic points.
1 CSS pt = 96/72 CSS px, so passing the raw stored pt value caused the preview
to render at ~75% of the surrounding UI font size (matching the observed ~80%
mismatch). Multiply by 96.0/72.0 before handing the value to html-to-node.

subject: Open add-file link dialog when File field added; add on empty-area double-click (#16192)
body:
* Open add-file dialog when File field is added; add on empty-area double-click

When the File field is added via its "+" chip in the entry editor, the
LinkedFilesEditor now immediately opens the add-file dialog, since an empty
File editor has no other purpose than to receive a file.

Also, double-clicking anywhere in the empty area of the file list (not just
the trailing "+1" row) now triggers adding a new file, including when the
list is still empty.

* Guard empty-area double-click and deferred File-field editor open

Restrict the empty-area double-click that adds a new file to clicks on the
list's content background: walk up from the event target to the ListView,
returning the enclosing cell's emptiness if a cell is reached and treating
scrollbars (and other skin sub-controls whose events also bubble up to the
ListView handler) as non-empty rather than emptily falling through to
addNewFile().

Guard the deferred showFieldEditor() runnable against a stale entry: if the
tab was rebound to a different entry before the Platform.runLater block runs,
the editors map belongs to that other entry, so bail out unless getCurrentEntry()
still matches the entry we started with before focusing or opening the dialog.

subject: Add CSL-JSON import endpoint for correct entry-type mapping (#16151)
body:
* Add CSL-JSON import endpoint for correct entry-type mapping

Extend `POST /libraries/{id}/entries` to accept CSL-JSON
(`application/vnd.citationstyles.csl+json`), so browser translators (and any
CSL-JSON producer) can hand items to JabRef and get the correct entry type
instead of a flat @article.

Rather than a bespoke Zotero-itemType -> BibTeX map (rejected by ADR 0064),
reuse the merged citation-js-based CSL mapping (`CSLItemTypeDefinitions`,
PR #15946): extract the CSL-JSON -> BibEntry core from
`ZoteroCitationMarkParser.toBibEntry` into a new public
`parseCslJsonItems(String)` that accepts a bare CSL item or an array.

`EntriesResource.addCslJson` serialises the mapped entries to BibTeX and
appends them via the existing `AppendBibTeXToLibrary` command, preserving
duplicate handling and group assignment. Entries carry no citation key so
JabRef generates keys on import. Freshly built entries are written with
reformat=true (empty parsed serialisation otherwise writes nothing).

Tests: type/field mapping and array/object/blank/invalid handling in
`ZoteroCitationMarkParserTest`; endpoint conversion + 400 paths in
`EntriesResourceTest`.

Related to https://github.com/JabRef/jabref/issues/15875

* docs(changelog): link CSL-JSON endpoint entry to PR #16151

* Drop dead null guards in parseCslJsonItems

The isJsonArray/isJsonObject guards already ensure Gson returns non-null, so
the != null checks were unreachable; removing them also satisfies the
no-null-check style rule.

* Add CSL-JSON demo requests to import.http

* Guard CSL-JSON import against explicit null fields

CSL-JSON that sets optional properties explicitly to null ("type": null,
"author": null, "issued": null, "issued": {"date-parts": null}) crashed the
import path with an NPE (Gson overwrites the field defaults with null, and the
immutable CSL mapping tables reject a null key lookup), surfacing as HTTP 500.

Normalise type/author/issued and guard date-parts before use. Add a
parameterised regression test covering each null shape.

* Use Markdown Javadoc for the group parameter of addCslJson

Replace the traditional @param tag with a Markdown sentence, per the
project's Markdown-Javadoc guideline for new docs.

* Table-ise the null-field test with @CsvSource

Use @CsvSource with a `|` delimiter (JSON keeps its commas) so the null-field
cases read as a table of input -> expected entry type, and clean up the
provider imports.

* Apply OpenRewrite cleanup to ZoteroCitationMarkParserTest

Replace list.get(0) with list.getFirst() per SequencedCollection recipe.

* Update jablib/src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/openoffice/ZoteroCitationMarkParser.java

subject: Add focus-triggered remove button for empty optional fields in entry editor (#16185)
body:
* Add focus-triggered remove button for empty optional fields in entry editor

Non-required, currently-blank field rows in the "Main" all-fields tab now
show a small gray remove icon in the top-right corner while focused, letting
users hide a still-empty row they added via a chip without needing a
hover-only affordance. Required fields and the citation key never get one.

* Document the remove-field button as a traced requirement

Adds req~entry-editor.main-tab.remove-field~1 to the entry-editor
requirements doc and tags the implementation, matching this tab's
existing traceability convention.

* Fix stale required-field suppression and sibling focus binding

An entry-type change can leave the shown field set unchanged while
still changing which of those fields are required, and the tab only
rebuilt when the field set itself changed — force a rebuild on any
InternalField.TYPE_HEADER change so rows are re-wrapped with the
correct required/optional classification.

Also rebind the remove button's visibility to the row wrapper's
focus-within instead of the editor node's: the button is a sibling of
the editor inside the StackPane, not a descendant, so focus moving
onto the button itself must not read as "focus left the row."

Verified manually: switching entry type, and typing/clearing a
multi-line field (Comment), still show/hide/remove the button
correctly.

* Skip the remove button for fields whose editor has its own buttons

Identifier editors (DOI, ISBN, ISSN, ...), the URL editor, and others
already draw their own trailing buttons (fetch, shorten, open, ...) in
the same top-right corner where the remove button would overlay,
producing visually overlapping icons. Detect any editor with its own
Button children and skip wrapping it, leaving the remove affordance
only on plain fields where it doesn't collide with anything.

Verified manually: ISBN (has its own buttons) no longer shows an
overlapping remove icon; PMID (no built-in buttons) still shows it
correctly when focused and blank.

* Overlay remove-field button inside the text input

The focus-triggered remove button was stacked over the whole editor node,
pinning it to the row's far right — past an editor's trailing option
buttons (e.g. the ICORE lookup / external-link icons), so it floated
outside the field box.

Re-parent just the editor's primary text input into a StackPane (kept in
the input's own HBox, preserving its grow priority) and overlay the button
on that instead, so it sits inside the field box. Composite editors with
no plain text input fall back to stacking the whole editor node.

* Fix IndexOutOfBounds when overlaying the remove button

new StackPane(input, button) re-parents the text input as it is
constructed, detaching it from the editor's HBox before the following
getChildren().set(index, overlay) runs — by then the list is one shorter
and index points past its end, throwing IndexOutOfBoundsException while
building any field row.

Insert an empty StackPane into the input's slot first (which detaches the
input), then re-parent the input and button into it.

* Fix OpenRewrite: use == for enum field comparison

OpenRewrite's cleanup recipe flagged .equals() on the InternalField
enum constant; == is the project's preferred form for enum identity
comparison.

subject: Render entry preview with html-to-node and remove javafx.web (#16145)
body:
* Render entry preview with html-to-node instead of WebView

PreviewViewer now uses org.jabref:html-to-node (HtmlView), which renders
the preview HTML as plain JavaFX nodes - first step towards dropping
javafx.web:

- Base URI is passed via render options instead of an injected
  <html><base> wrapper; link clicks go through the options' link handler
  instead of DOM event listeners on the WebEngine document.
- Plain-text copy uses the library's text extraction instead of
  executing document.body.innerText JavaScript.
- Printing uses PrinterJob.printPage(node) instead of WebEngine.print.
- Search-hit highlighting (Highlighter.highlightHtml's <mark> tags) is
  rendered as real background shapes by the library.
- MainTableTooltip resizes on content layout changes instead of
  WebEngine load-worker state.
- EntryChangeDetailsView synchronizes the two previews with a
  bidirectional ScrollPane vvalue binding, replacing the WebView
  JavaScript scroll glue.
- Text selection inside the preview is not supported yet; "copy
  selection" falls back to copying the whole preview.

The library is consumed from mavenLocal for now (not yet on Maven
Central): clone https://github.com/JabRef/html-to-node, run
./gradlew publishToMavenLocal there, then build JabRef with
-PuseMavenLocal=true.

* Fix preview panel layout and tooltip sizing without WebView

WebView reported a fixed 800x600 preferred size, which the surrounding
layouts silently relied on. PreviewViewer now sets that preferred size
on its ScrollPane and restores fitToHeight, and PreviewPanel lets the
preview grow so the layout selection bar stays at the bottom regardless
of panel height. Tooltips size their viewport to the rendered content
instead (replacing the old JavaScript height measurement).

Also, a bare -PuseMavenLocal (without =true) now enables the local
Maven repository.

* Replace MathSciNet browser tab with an identifier field editor

The MR number field now behaves like DOI: MR_NUMBER carries
FieldProperty.IDENTIFIER and gets the IdentifierEditor with a button
that opens the MathSciNet page in the external browser
(IdentifierParser already mapped mrnumber to MathSciNetId).

The MathSciNetTab, which embedded the live MathSciNet website in a
WebView, is removed together with its preference plumbing - it was the
last feature requiring an embedded browser.

The IdentifierEditor text field no longer overrides EditorTextField's
fill-available-space preferred height, so identifier fields align with
their row label in sparse entry editor tabs (e.g. "Other fields").

Note: MR_NUMBER now also participates in identifier-based duplicate
detection (DuplicateCheck).

* Remove javafx.web

With the entry preview rendered by html-to-node and the MathSciNet tab
replaced by an identifier field, nothing needs an embedded browser
anymore:

- AiSummaryShowingView renders the summary HTML with HtmlView in a
  ScrollPane instead of a pooled WebView.
- WebViewStore and its warm-up in JabRefGUI are deleted.
- EditAction no longer special-cases a focused WebView.
- The theme subsystem loses all WebEngine machinery:
  installCssOnWebEngine, the tracked WebEngine set, and the data-URL
  embedding in StyleSheetFile/StyleSheetDataUrl (it existed only so a
  WebView survived deletion of a custom CSS file). Live CSS updates now
  reinstall the scene stylesheets.
- jabgui's module-info drops javafx.web and jdk.xml.dom (the latter was
  only needed for WebView DOM access in PreviewViewer).
- The javafx-web/jdk-jsobject version pins, the platform-variant
  special-casing and the JDKjsobjectDependencyMetadataRule workaround
  for JDK-8342623 are removed from the build.

* Add CHANGELOG entries for preview rendering and MathSciNet change

* Null-mark MathSciNetIdentifierEditorViewModel

New classes are explicitly @NullMarked (JSpecify) so nullability
defaults are explicit. The pre-existing sibling identifier view models
are left unchanged.

* Express base URI absence without null in PreviewViewer

Uses html-to-node's new withoutBaseUri() instead of collapsing the
Optional to null via orElse(null).

* Spool print jobs in the background

PrinterJob.printPage must run on the JavaFX thread while the printed
node is attached to a scene and only renders a single page; the
potentially blocking spooling (endJob) is moved to a background task,
keeping the UI responsive. Failures surface via the dialog service.

* Route the copy shortcut to the preview when it has focus

WebView consumed shortcut+C natively, which is why EditAction ignored
it as focus owner. The node-based preview (a plain ScrollPane) fell
through to the entry-level actions instead, so pressing the copy
shortcut with the preview focused copied the selected entry. EditAction
now detects a focus owner inside a PreviewViewer: COPY copies the
preview content, all other edit actions are ignored as before.

No test added: constructing a PreviewViewer requires the DI container
and the JavaFX toolkit; the routing itself is a parent-chain walk.

* Open links in the AI summary in the external browser

The summary HTML comes from Markdown and can contain anchors; the
HtmlView's default link handler is a no-op. Configure it like the
entry preview: clicks open the link via NativeDesktop.openBrowser.

* Exclude html-to-node from architecture analysis

The library shares the org.jabref namespace, so JabGuiArchitectureTest
scanned its jar and flagged HtmlToNode.stylesheet() for using
Class.getResource (which is exactly what Parent#getStylesheets needs).
External dependencies are not subject to this repository's architecture
rules; a dedicated ImportOption filters them from the scan.

* Map the html-to-node module name in gradle/modules.properties

That file is the established place for Module Name -> GA mappings of
real modules (afterburner.fx, easybind, mslinks), instead of an ad-hoc
javaModuleDependencies block in the dependency rules. Once the library
is released, the entry can be contributed upstream to the gradlex
shared mapping list.

* Point agents to the dependency-management howto

The procedure (module-info requires + versions platform +
gradle/modules.properties mapping) is documented in
docs/code-howtos/dependency-management.md, but AGENTS.md never
referenced it, so agents adding dependencies would not find it.

* Coalesce tooltip preview relayouts

Rendering the tooltip preview changes the content's layout bounds
several times (initial render, cover refresh), and every change queued
a sizeToScene call while the viewport height was rewritten on each
bounds update. Tooltip re-fits are now coalesced to at most one queued
sizeToScene (skipping sub-pixel changes), and the viewport height is
only written when it actually changed.

* Exclude html-to-node from jablib's architecture analysis too

jablib's tests have jabgui on their runtime classpath (FXML loading in
localization tests), so JabLibArchitectureTest scanned the html-to-node
jar just like JabGuiArchitectureTest did. JabSrvArchitectureTest only
analyzes org.jabref.http and is not affected.

* Use asterisk emphasis in AGENTS.md (MD049)

* Use the preview's text selection for copy and drag actions

html-to-node now provides mouse text selection across blocks:

- "Copy selection" and the copy shortcut copy the selected text and
  fall back to the whole preview when nothing is selected.
- Dragging over the preview extends the selection; drag-and-drop of
  the preview content only starts when the drag begins on an existing
  selection (previously the DnD gesture interrupted every selection
  drag after a few pixels).

* Embed custom theme CSS as data URLs for scenes

The data-URL embedding removed together with the WebEngine machinery
was in fact valuable beyond WebView, so it is ported to scene
stylesheets (supported since JavaFX 17): the custom theme survives
removal of its CSS file while JabRef is running, and live reloads
cannot be served stale from JavaFX's stylesheet cache because the URL
changes with the content. Ironically, the WebView-era code applied
both benefits only to WebViews, never to scenes.

StyleSheet#getSceneStylesheetLocation() returns the data: URL when the
CSS fits the 48k in-memory limit and falls back to the plain URL
otherwise; ThemeManager installs these locations on scenes. The test
coverage removed with the WebEngine machinery is restored accordingly.

* Check html-to-node in architecture tests, exempt only the getResource rule

html-to-node shares the org.jabref namespace, so instead of excluding it
wholesale via DoNotIncludeHtmlToNode, keep it in scope for all architecture
rules and carve out only useStreamsOfResources. That rule cannot be satisfied
by html-to-node: it needs a stylesheet URL for JavaFX (Parent#getStylesheets()),
which getResourceAsStream cannot provide, and it cannot use
@AllowedToUseClassGetResource without depending back on JabRef.

* Render the entry preview with the incubator RichTextArea

PreviewViewer and the AI summary switch from the TextFlow-based
HtmlView to html-to-node's RichHtmlView, backed by the JavaFX
incubator RichTextArea: text selection now supports mouse and
keyboard, with caret navigation and accessibility. The area sizes to
its content so the surrounding ScrollPane keeps scrolling (scroll
synchronization in the change resolver and tooltip sizing continue to
work); copy actions and the drag-out guard use the native selection.

The theme maps the new .rich-text-area selectors to JabRef's palette -
Modena styles them from -fx-accent, which JabRef deliberately sets to
red as an "unthemed control" canary (selection showed red before).

Build: jfx-incubator-richtext/-input version pins, platform-variant
patching, module mappings, and requires jfx.incubator.richtext.

* Remove historical comments from the preview code

Comments should state constraints the code cannot express, not
describe the previous implementation.

* Use the selection facade of RichHtmlView

html-to-node now hard-requires the incubator module and exposes
getSelectedText/isPressOnSelection/setUseContentHeight, so the GUI no
longer touches jfx.incubator.richtext types: the module-info entry
shrinks to a runtime-only requirement that provisions the artifact.
Also removes an unused import that the stylesheet-location change left
behind.

* Drop the unused ThemeManager parameter from PreviewViewer

Theming works via regular JavaFX CSS; the parameter only survived for
call-site compatibility. Removing it cascades through all seven
construction sites and frees MainTableTooltip, PreviewPanel,
EntryChangeDetailsView, CitationRelationsTab, EntryEditorTabFactory,
DatabaseChangeDetailsViewFactory, and EntryEditor from their
pass-through parameters, fields, and injections.

* Apply OpenRewrite suggestion in ThemeManager

* Fix ThemeManager imports and doc reference

The OpenRewrite patch brought an unused plain Predicate import along
with the static one, and the /// documentation used a JavaDoc inline
tag instead of a Markdown reference.

* Document and enforce that javafx.web is not wanted

Add a note in dependency-rules explaining why javafx-web is stripped
and add CommonArchitectureTest.doNotUseJavaFXWeb to enforce it.

* Add MathSciNet browser-sync toggle and requirements/plan docs

Restores live MathSciNet browsing after the WebView-based
MathSciNetTab was dropped (javafx-web is now architecturally banned,
see CommonArchitectureTest.doNotUseJavaFXWeb): a "Sync with browser"
toggle on the MR_NUMBER identifier editor asks the JabRef Browser
Extension's native-messaging bridge to open or focus a MathSciNet tab
for the entry currently shown, instead of embedding a browser.

BrowserExtensionBridgeClient discovers and talks to the bridge process
(same discovery file/provider as the existing fulltext-fetch bridge);
sync fails silently when the extension isn't running. See
docs/requirements/mathscinet.md (req~mathscinet.sync.*~1) and PLAN.md
for the full cross-repo design; the browser-extension half lives in
JabRef-Browser-Extension-experimental PRs #82/#83.

* Surface MathSciNet browser-sync failures with a notification

Previously every outcome (opened/focused/unreachable/failed) only
logged at debug level and nothing was ever shown to the user, so a
failed sync looked identical to a successful one from the GUI. Bump
logging to info and notify the user when the bridge is unreachable or
the request fails, per req~mathscinet.sync.unavailable~1.

* Fix CI: markdownlint and formatting failures

- PLAN.md: give the architecture-diagram fence a language (MD040) and
  add the missing blank line before a list (MD032).
- BrowserExtensionBridgeClient.java: apply the formatter's own patch
  from the failing CI run (indentation of the chained HttpClient
  builder and two ternary continuations).

* Fix preview font size and background color in html-to-node rendering

The preview text was rendered with explicit Font objects, bypassing the
"-fx-font-size" scene-root style that normally applies the "Override
default font size" preference (see ThemeManager). Pass the resolved
size through HtmlRenderOptions#withBaseFontSize instead, and keep it in
sync when the preference changes.

Also give the preview a white background (matching the entry editor's
-fx-control-inner-background) instead of the transparent one it
inherited from the generic .scroll-pane/.stack-pane rules, which let
the gray window chrome show through.

* Fix preview font size not matching the app's default when not overridden

resolveBaseFontSize() fell back to the JavaFX/system default font size
when "Override default font size" is off, but ThemeManager never
actually relies on that system default either — it applies
WorkspacePreferences.getDefault().getMainFontSize() to the whole scene
regardless. Match that so the preview's font size lines up with the
rest of the UI instead of using an unrelated system value.

* Remove PLAN.md

* Fix formatting of chained method call and ternary in PreviewViewer

subject: Fix file field editor: button placement, sizing, live refresh (#16172)
body:
* Fix file field editor in new entry editor: layout, sizing, live refresh

- Move the add/fetch-fulltext/download-URL buttons to the left of the
  file list, since they act on the whole field, not the selected file.
- Size the file ListView to exactly (file count + 1) rows instead of a
  fixed max height, removing dead whitespace below the last file; skip
  AllFieldsTab's generic weight-based height override for this editor
  since it now sizes itself.
- Fix linked files not appearing live when added via the "+" button:
  LinkedFilesEditor wrapped its file list in UiThreadObservableList
  before handing it to JavaFX's Bindings.bindContentBidirectional,
  which dispatches change events by list identity. The wrapper
  forwards listener registration to its delegate, so every Change's
  getList() reported the delegate instead of the wrapper JavaFX was
  tracking, silently breaking the live sync into the ListView (only
  the one-time initial setAll ever populated it). Bind directly to
  viewModel.filesProperty(), which is only ever mutated on the FX
  Application Thread.
- Double-clicking the empty row below the files now adds a new file,
  same as the add button.

* Avoid raw null checks when walking up to the enclosing ListCell

* Add CHANGELOG entry for file field editor fixes

* Replace CHANGELOG TODO placeholder with PR #16172 link

* Align ternary continuation indentation in isEmptyRow

* Cap file list height and derive row height from CSS

Bound the LinkedFilesEditor ListView to at most MAX_VISIBLE_ROWS so
entries with many linked files scroll internally instead of expanding
the entry editor layout indefinitely, and bind maxHeight to the same cap.

Move the row height from a hard-coded 30px constant to a CSS
-fx-fixed-cell-size on .linked-files-list (em-based), so theming and
font scaling adjust it. Java now binds pref/max height to the ListView's
fixedCellSizeProperty instead of a Java constant.

subject: Add madrlint MADR linter to test workflow (#16168)
body:
* Add madrlint MADR linter to Source Code Tests workflow

Add a `madr` job to `.github/workflows/tests-code.yml` that lints the
Architectural Decision Records under `docs/decisions/` with madrlint
(https://github.com/adr/madrlint) via JBang.

The linter always exits 0, so the job counts emitted `::error` lines and
fails when any violation is reported; `--output-format github-actions`
surfaces them as inline annotations. External-link checks (MADR11) are
disabled because JabRef verifies external links elsewhere. A new
`.madrlintignore` excludes the non-ADR files `adr-template.md` and
`index.md` from the directory naming rules.

Fix all existing ADRs so the corpus passes:

- Convert `-` list markers to `*` (MADR31) in the affected records.
- Add missing Context/Chosen-option/rationale statements and correct
  heading levels and an empty section (MADR01/02/03/04/06/07).
- Shorten an over-long YAML front-matter title (MADR21).
- Fix a broken local link in 0042 that pointed to a renamed 0036 file
  (MADR12).

* Save the JBang cache in the MADR job

Use the combined `actions/cache@v6` action instead of `cache/restore`, so
`~/.jbang` is persisted on a cache miss in the post-job step. The
restore-only variant never wrote the cache, so the monthly key could only
ever be populated by another job. The key stays madrlint-specific to keep
it separate from the shared `jbang-` cache used by setup-gradle.

* Pin madrlint and setup-jbang for deterministic CI

Pin the MADR lint job to fixed versions so upstream changes cannot alter
CI results without a deliberate repo change:

- `jbangdev/setup-jbang` is pinned to commit 2b1b465 (v0.1.1) instead of
  the moving `@main` ref.
- madrlint is run from a fixed https://github.com/adr/madrlint commit via
  a blob URL (in a `MADRLINT` env var) instead of the unversioned
  `madrlint@adr/madrlint` alias, which tracks upstream HEAD. The script's
  //DEPS are already version-pinned.

subject: Support http(s)/ftp URLs as jabkit --input (#16165)
body:
* Support http(s)/ftp URLs as jabkit --input

`jabkit convert --input <url>` was documented as accepting URLs but
silently failed, since --input was parsed straight into a filesystem
Path with no scheme detection. InputOption#getInputFile() now detects
http(s)/ftp URLs and downloads them via the existing URLDownload
utility before resolving the local Path, so all InputOption-consuming
commands gain URL support consistently. Download failures surface
through the existing CliException/exit-code handling instead of a
"file not found" usage error.

* Add CHANGELOG entry for jabkit URL input support

* Assert concrete BibEntry fields in InputOptionUrlTest instead of substring check

assertTrue(...contains("Darwin1888")) only checked the citation key appeared
somewhere in the output, missing regressions in author/title/year handling.
Compare against a BibEntry built from the expected fields via
BibEntryAssert.assertEquals(List<BibEntry>, Path, Importer) instead.

* Fix case-sensitive scheme check in jabkit --input URL detection

startsWith("http://"|"https://"|"ftp://") missed uppercase/mixed-case
schemes (e.g. HTTP://), silently treating them as local file paths.
Normalize to lowercase first, consistent with LinkedFile.isOnlineLink's
existing convention. Added a regression test with an uppercase scheme.

* Redact URL userinfo from jabkit download error messages

A --input URL like https://user:pass@host/file.bib had its credentials
echoed verbatim to stderr on download failure. Extend the existing
FetcherException.getRedactedUrl helper (already used for API-key query
params) to also strip userinfo, and route jabkit's error messages
through it.

* Catch InvalidPathException for local jabkit --input paths

FileUtil.convertCygwinPathToWindows() calls Path.of(), which throws the
unchecked InvalidPathException on malformed input. Uncaught, this bypassed
CliExceptionHandler's ImportServiceException/CliException handling and
would surface as a raw stack trace instead of a clean USAGE exit.

body:

* AllFieldsTab: natural-height scroll-list layout

'Show more' reveals the secondary-optional ones (#12711, Google-Contacts
style). Arbitrary fields can be added via an editable combo box using
FieldFactory.parseField. Still-empty user-added fields stay visible until
another entry is opened.

* AllFieldsTab: live refresh when fields are set/unset externally

Subscribes to the entry's event bus; rebuilds only when the computed
shown-field set differs from the visible one, so typing inside a visible
editor never rebuilds or steals focus. A field cleared in a visible editor
stays visible until another entry is opened.

Per feedback in #12711: Identifiers, Files and links, and Comments are
always-present collapsible sections - collapsed when empty, expanded
when a member field is set; a manual toggle survives rebuilds for the

grouping); the free-form add row stays at the bottom.

collapsible sections: Bibliometrics (citation count, ICORE ranking)
and Meta (crossref, groups, owner, timestamps, special fields - fields
about the entry rather than the paper). Meta offers add-chips only for

be added via chips like the other meta fields; only the auto-managed
timestamp fields stay chip-less. Also records two follow-ups in PLAN.md

offer fields not already available above) and resolves the ABSTRACT
placement question (stays in main).

Decisions from live review (#12711): the Main tab replaces the classic
category tabs entirely, so their code is removed rather than kept as
opt-in: RequiredFieldsTab, OptionalFieldsTabBase, ImportantOptional-,
DetailOptional-, DeprecatedFields-, OtherFields-, CommentsTab and their
BuiltIn constants, factory cases and SHOW_* preference keys. Stored
keys from older versions become dead entries; no migration needed.

cell rendering, StringUtil.isBlank); isPresent/get blocks replaced with

with impl tracing tags; PLAN.md markdownlint-clean.

subject: Fix jabkit -p/-d flags not propagating across command levels (#16164)

* Fix jabkit -p/-d flags not propagating across command levels

Each jabkit (sub)command mixed in its own `new SharedOptions()` instance,
so e.g. `jabkit -p check consistency` set the root command's copy of

picocli IFactory) so the flag has one value across the whole command
tree, regardless of where it's placed.

Also detect the short forms -p/-d (not just --porcelain/--debug) during
early logging setup, which runs before picocli parses arguments.

ArXivIdentifier.parse uses an anchored matches(), so a url field ending

matches() succeeds while the field stays a whole-URL value (no substring
excision, no data loss). Consolidate the html-url parse tests into a
parameterized test covering the fragment case.

subject: More parallel actions (#16134)
body:
* Try parallel builds

* Remove unnecessary ${{ ... }}

* Unify if: expression style in package action.yml

Drop redundant ${{ }} wrapping on three if: conditions to match the
bare style used elsewhere in the file.

* ci(binaries): run all Gradle tasks in one invocation

Parallel package actions each spawned their own Gradle daemon on the
same checkout. Gradle's stale-output cleanup then deleted shared
upstream outputs mid-build: :jablib:processResources failed with
'Unable to delete directory jablib/build/resources/main' and jabsrv
compilation lost jablib.jar ('package org.jabref.logic does not
exist').

- Build jpackage + shadowJar for all components in a single Gradle
  invocation; org.gradle.parallel provides subproject parallelism
  within one daemon and one task graph
- Make the package action Gradle-free so its instances can run in
  parallel; smoke test now exercises the packaged launcher instead
  of 'gradle run'
- Run jbundle sequentially in the workflow (it drives Gradle itself)
- Fix Validate Signature condition: 'macos-latest' never matched the
  matrix (macos-15/macos-15-intel); use startsWith(inputs.os, 'macos')

* ci(binaries): validate signature of app inside dmg, not dmg itself

jpackage signs the .app bundle inside the dmg and the pkg
(productbuild --sign), but never the dmg container - that one is only
notarized and stapled later. 'codesign --verify' on the dmg therefore
always fails with 'code object is not signed at all'; the check never
fired before because its 'macos-latest' condition stopped matching the
matrix.

Mount the dmg and deep-verify the contained .app including its
Developer ID Application authority, and check the pkg signature via
pkgutil.

* ci(binaries): agree to dmg license when mounting for validation

The dmg embeds a license (jpackage --license-file); hdiutil attach
prompts for agreement and aborts in non-interactive mode after dumping
the license text.

* ci(binaries): build jbundle only on explicit workflow_dispatch input

jbundle was built on every tag build, main push, and 'dev: binaries'
PR - adding four sequential Gradle-driven builds to the critical path.
No release workflow consumes the jbundle artifacts, so gate it behind
a dedicated opt-in dispatch input instead.

* ci(binaries): keep jbundle on tags and 'dev: binaries', skip on main push

Restores the per-event jbundle activation: tag builds and PRs labeled
'dev: binaries' build jbundle again. Only pushes to main skip it now.
workflow_dispatch uses the dedicated 'jbundle' input instead of
piggybacking on 'upload'.

* ci(binaries): simplify disk cleanup, background pigz install

Merge the three background rm steps into one foreground step - they
finish in seconds and are not worth the parallelism. Background the
pigz install instead: it is first needed when archiving application
images, long after the Gradle build.

* Real sync point for pigz+

* Sequential repackaging (parallel saves only 15 seoncs and has a risk to break on Windows)

* Trigger CI

* Update binaries.yml

* Update binaries.yml

* Speedup ARM build

* Run jbundle components in parallel

Each jbundle invocation targets a different subproject's build output, so running them concurrently is safe despite jbundle driving its own Gradle process per call.

* fix parallel syntax

* Speedup through background jbundle installation

* Remove jbundle from binaries build

jbundle binaries are no longer produced. Drop the dispatch input,
should-jbundle conditions, the jbundle build steps in the workflow,
and the corresponding smoke test / upload steps and shouldJbundle
input in the package action.

* Start background steps right after checkout

Move "Free disk space" and "Install pigz and cache" to directly after
the checkout step so they run earlier and overlap with JDK/Gradle setup.

subject: Add batch lookup and cache (#16121)
body:
* Cache /citations/lookup by text hash and add batch endpoint

The SumatraPDF page-scan flow needs one HTTP round-trip per visible page
to paint per-citation marker dots, not one per link. Two server-side
changes make that affordable:

1. CitationCacheService gains a second Caffeine map keyed by SHA-256 of
   the raw citation text (max 1024 entries, 24h TTL — longer than the
   CUID2 token cache because the parsed BibEntry stays valid as long as
   the citation text does). /citations/lookup now checks this map first;
   on hit it reuses the prior parse and skips the LLM / fetcher call
   entirely. Each lookup still mints a fresh CUID2 token so the
   add-from-cache flow remains unchanged.

2. New POST /libraries/{id}/citations/lookup:batch accepts a JSON array
   of citation texts and returns a parallel array of LookupResponse,
   aligned by index. Blank slots and per-citation parse failures yield
   a "none" response so one bad entry can't fail the whole batch. The
   shared body is factored into a private doLookup helper so single and
   batched paths stay in lock-step.

Token cache TTL stays at 1h: tokens are short-lived by design (lookup →
add round-trip). The text-hash cache picks up the slack for repeat
lookups across longer reading sessions.

* Add JSpecify null annotations to citation lookup records

Mark all CitationsResource DTOs with @NullMarked. LookupResponse fields
parserCacheKey and parsedEntryType are @Nullable — null in the batch
lookup blank-slot and parser-failure paths.

* Add per-field Javadoc to LookupResponse record

* Single-line @param tags in LookupResponse Javadoc (IntelliJ-friendly)

* Convert LookupResponse.matchScope to MatchScope enum

Three states (ACTIVE / OTHER / NONE) replace the string-typed field. @JsonValue
keeps the lowercase wire format ("active" / "other" / "none") so clients are
unaffected.

* Hoist @NullMarked to CitationsResource class level

Applies to every nested record via JSpecify's inheritance rules. @Nullable
on LookupResponse.parserCacheKey/parsedEntryType still needed to mark the
exceptions.

* Drop trivial 'resolve once' comment in lookupBatch

* Reuse BibEntryTypesManager via Injector in CitationsResource

* Bind BibEntryTypesManager into HK2 for @Inject use

Server registers the afterburner singleton as an HK2 constant once at
startup; resources @Inject it like any other service. CitationsResource
drops 4 ad-hoc `new BibEntryTypesManager()` (already collapsed to Injector
calls in the prior commit) in favour of a single injected field.

* Bind BibEntryTypesManager from prefs (carries user-customised types)

* Forbid afterburner Injector in jabsrv via ArchUnit

LibraryResource and EntriesResource now @Inject BibEntryTypesManager instead
of reaching into the GUI's afterburner singleton. JabSrvArchitectureTests
locks the rule in so future resources don't smuggle the dependency back.

* Document lookup:batch endpoint in import.http

* Add minimal tests for citation lookup endpoints

Covers blank text -> 400, unknown library -> 404, empty batch -> 400, and
blank-only batch returning matchScope=none (exercises wiring + JSON
serialization without a real parser). Adds the BibEntryTypesManager
binding so resource-level @Inject resolves.

* Add 2-arg LookupResponse constructor for no-entry rows

* Carry FetcherException through Optional chains via UncheckedFetcherException

doLookup now resolves the cached BibEntry with a clean
`getByText(...).map(...).orElseGet(() -> parseAndCache(...))` chain instead
of the `orElse(null)` + null-check anti-pattern. parseAndCache wraps the
checked FetcherException in UncheckedFetcherException; lookupBatch catches
the carrier per-citation so a single fetch failure still leaves the rest of
the batch intact, and GlobalExceptionMapper unwraps any escape to surface
the original fetch failure message in the HTTP response.

* Document parseAndCache exceptions via @throws

* Mark UncheckedFetcherException @NullMarked

* Use Gson @SerializedName for MatchScope wire format

jabsrv serializes via GsonMessageBodyWriter, which ignores Jackson's
@JsonValue and would emit "NONE" instead of "none". @SerializedName on
each enum constant restores the documented lowercase wire format and
keeps the existing batchLookupBlankSlotReturnsNoneScope test green.

* Forbid Jackson outside the command package via ArchUnit

jabsrv writes application/json with Gson, so Jackson annotations
(@JsonValue, @JsonProperty, …) silently no-op and ship the wrong wire
format — the @JsonValue/@SerializedName mishap on MatchScope was exactly
this class of bug. Only org.jabref.http.server.command stays exempt; it
uses tools.jackson.databind.ObjectMapper directly for command dispatch.

* Don't fail batch lookup on per-citation parser-empty result

* Format CitationsResource per project rules

* Don't leak upstream URL/body in fetcher error responses

FetcherException#getLocalizedMessage embeds the upstream URL, HTTP status,
and full response body — sending it as the HTTP response body exposes
internal network details to clients. Return a generic message instead;
keep the full chain in the server log via the existing LOGGER.warn.

* Align @throws padding in parseAndCache Javadoc

* Pin direct ArchUnit deps in jabsrv testModuleInfo

org.jabref.testsupport carries ArchUnit only transitively, which the
dependency-analysis Gradle plugin flags as unused since JabSrvArchitectureTests
imports the archunit packages directly. Replace it with explicit
com.tngtech.archunit + com.tngtech.archunit.junit5.api requires plus the
junit5 engine as runtimeOnly.

* Bind BibEntryTypesManager in Entries + Library resource tests

EntriesResource and LibraryResource @Inject the manager now, so their
test ResourceConfig must bind it or HK2 reports 500 for every request.
Extract a reusable addEntryTypesManagerToResourceConfig helper on
ServerTest and call it from the three resource tests that need it.

* Add UncheckedFetcherException to JabSrvLauncher SOURCES list

* Sort dto/ SOURCES list alphabetically

* Drop unused afterburner.fx requires from jabsrv module-info

* Match Gson pretty-printed spacing in batch lookup test

* Use Duration.ofDays(1) for TEXT_TTL

* Rename *ArchitectureTests to *ArchitectureTest, inherit Common rules

Follow the project's ...Test naming convention (not ...Tests) for the
three ArchUnit classes and record the rule in AGENTS.md.

Make JabSrvArchitectureTest extend CommonArchitectureTest so jabsrv
gets the shared architecture checks (no-Swing/AWT, slf4j-only,
JSpecify, no Paths/URI.create, Caffeine-not-Guava, ...). Scope stays
org.jabref.http, so the inherited logic/model rules match no classes;
archunit.properties sets archRule.failOnEmptyShould=false for that.

* Reflow

* Apply suggestion from @subhramit
