subject: Build binaries in parallel where safe (#16100)
body:
* Build binaries in parallel where safe

Use the new GitHub Actions step-level parallelism together with Gradle's
own parallel execution:

- Merge the jabls and jabsrv jar builds into one `gradle --parallel`
  invocation. One daemon builds both subprojects concurrently, avoiding
  the lock contention and heap blow-up of two separate `gradle`
  processes.
- Run the disk-space cleanup steps (`rm -rf`) in the background so they
  overlap with the build.
- Run the end-of-package artifact uploads / rsync in the background so
  they overlap with the following Gradle steps.

The per-component package steps stay sequential on purpose:
backgrounding all four would start four Gradle daemons at -Xmx4g each
and exhaust the runner.

Also drop the prepared comments that would not have worked as written:
the cross-job `wait: gitversion` (step-level wait resolves ids in the
same job only; cross-job order is already handled by `needs:`), and the
pre-build background/wait pairs whose waiter directly depends on the
backgrounded step (zero parallelism, only overhead).

* Remove unsupported background: from package composite action

GitHub Actions step-level background:/wait: is only supported for
job steps, not for steps inside a composite action.yml. Revert the
package action to main so its upload steps run sequentially as before;
the real parallel wins stay in binaries.yml (gradle --parallel jars,
backgrounded disk-space cleanups).

---------

subject: fix(preview): fix initial text for preview combobox (#16104)
Support importing into any open library via HTTP (#15929)
body:
* Support importing into any open library via HTTP

The HTTP import endpoint POST /libraries/{id}/entries previously rejected any id other than 'current' with 400. It now resolves the id to an open library, switches JabRef to that library, and imports there. Unknown or closed ids yield 404 via ServerUtils.getLibraryPath.

The append UiCommands carry the target library (empty Optional = current); the GUI selects the matching tab before appending.

* Add EntriesResourceTest for library-targeted import

Covers: import to an open library carries that library as target, 'current' carries empty target, unknown id returns 404, empty bibtex returns 400.

* Apply same library-targeting to CitationsResource

Replace the hardcoded 'current'-only check in lookup and addFromCache with the shared resolution (ServerUtils.getBibDatabaseContext): 'current' -> active library, any other id -> that open library, unknown/closed id -> 404. addFromCache now duplicate-checks against and appends to the resolved library, switching JabRef to it.

* Annotate nullable targetGroup in UiCommand

The AppendBibTeXToLibrary convenience constructors receive @Nullable group values from the HTTP resources; mark the String targetGroup parameters (and toGroup) @Nullable so the null handling is consistent with @NullMarked.

* Fix Javadoc param alignment in UiCommand

* Fix checkstyle unused import and duplicate CHANGELOG entry

* Restore csl-styles submodule to main

* Enforce CHECKLIST.md walkthrough before PR creation

Add a PreToolUse hook (checklist-done-guard.py) that blocks
`gh pr create`/`gh pr edit` unless every CHECKLIST.md item appears in the
PR body marked [x] or [/]. Update PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md so the AI must
walk CHECKLIST.md item by item and paste the completed checklist as
evidence in the AI usage section.

* Add XSS escaping rule to code checklist

* Ignore more agents in .gitignore

* Begin to fix http UiMessageHandler

* ignore skills-lock.json

* Create import.http

* Refine .gitignore

* Fix ExceptionMapper to include the exception text

* Use StringUtil

* Add seperator

* Add GroupsHelper to assign entries to a (created-if-missing) group

Extracts the duplicated find-or-create-explicit-group-then-assign logic into
a GUI-free helper in jablib so both the direct-import and import-dialog paths
share one implementation.

* Honor REST ?group= in the import-dialog path

When the direct-HTTP-import preference is off, HTTP imports go through the
import dialog, which previously dropped the ?group= parameter. The dialog now
pre-selects the requested group; on confirm the import creates it (top-level,
if missing) and assigns the entries via GroupsHelper. An explicit pick in the
dialog overrides the requested group; cancelling imports nothing.

* Refine import.http

* Auto-open requested library when not already open

`selectLibraryTab` previously logged a warning and appended to the current
tab when the requested library was not open. Now it opens the library in a
new (raised) tab via `OpenDatabaseAction.openFile`.

Since the newly opened tab loads in the background, the `AppendBibTeXToLibrary`
path now runs the import via `waitForLoadingFinished`, matching the existing
`AppendFilesToLibrary` path, so the import targets the loaded tab.

* docs: collapse @param targetGroup javadoc to single line

IntelliJ formatter mangles multi-line javadoc param descriptions, so
keep each description on one line.

* Revert .gigignore changes

* Fix checkstyle: declaration order and unused import

* Fix EntriesResource: validate before GUI check

Move blank/library-resolution checks ahead of the isGuiConnected()
guard so validation errors (400/404) surface without touching the
handler. Mock UiMessageHandler with CALLS_REAL_METHODS so the default
isGuiConnected() returns true in tests.

* Use overloaded constructor instead of Optional for library path

Replace Optional<Path> with a non-null Path parameter on the
AppendBibTeXToLibrary convenience constructor and let callers pick the
no-path overload when the target library is absent, instead of passing
an Optional.

* Add @NullMarked to GroupsHelper

* Assign target group to actually imported entries

Group assignment after a duplicate-check import used the original
entriesToImport list, but ImportHandler inserts copies created via
`new BibEntry(entry)`. The group was therefore applied to entries
that never reached the database, and the import runs asynchronously
so assignment happened before insertion completed.

Use the EntryImportHandlerTracker's onFinish callback to assign the
group to the tracked, inserted BibEntry instances once all entries
are processed.

* Use Markdown syntax in /// comments instead of JavaDoc inline tags

* Reject non-GUI mode before resolving target library

In standalone mode resolving an unknown library id threw 404 before the
GUI-required check could run. Move the isGuiConnected() check ahead of
resolveTargetLibrary() in addBibtex, addPlainCitation, and addUnknown so
the documented 400 "Only possible in GUI mode." takes precedence.

* Use dialog's selected library context for group selection

ImportEntriesDialog read and restored the selected groups against
stateManager.getActiveDatabase().orElse(null), which could pass null
(NPE in getSelectedGroups/setSelectedGroups via context.getUid()) and
operated on the wrong context when the active database differed from the
library entries are imported into. Use the dialog's selected library
context consistently instead.

* Let test setup/teardown failures propagate in useStandaloneMode

Catching and wrapping the exception in an unchecked IllegalStateException
obscured JUnit's reporting of setup/teardown failures. Declare throws
Exception instead, per project testing conventions.

* Make EntryImportHandlerTracker updates atomic

Imports run concurrently (one BackgroundTask chain per entry), so the
counter increment, list append, completion check, and onFinish execution
could interleave: onFinish could fire before all entries were appended to
importedEntries, and the plain ArrayList was mutated from several threads.

Synchronize the mutating/reading methods so each update and the completion
decision are atomic, guard onFinish with a finished flag so it runs exactly
once, and return an immutable snapshot from getImportedEntries().

* Reject path-less library ids for citation append target

CitationsResource derived the append target from the resolved context's
getDatabasePath(), which is empty for the bundled "demo" library (parsed
from a BufferedReader with no path). An empty Optional makes
UiCommand.AppendBibTeXToLibrary append to the active library, so POST
.../citations/{key} with id=demo silently added to the current library.

Resolve non-"current" ids via ServerUtils.getLibraryPath (open libraries
only), mirroring EntriesResource, so demo and unknown ids return 404.

* Update CHANGELOG.md

* Change group name to be more test-ish

* Change group name

* Change test entries

* Show group membership live when importing into a new group

When importing entries into a not-yet-existing group (e.g. via
POST /libraries/current/entries?group=...), the group was created but the
imported entries did not appear in it until switching tabs back and forth.

Cause: GroupsHelper.assignEntriesToGroup attached the new group node to the
tree before assigning the entries. Attaching creates the GroupNodeViewModel,
whose constructor computes its membership in a background task. That task ran
with the entries not yet assigned (empty result) and could complete after the
assignment, overwriting the correct membership with the stale empty one.

Fix: for a new group, assign the entries before attaching the node, so the view
model's first computation already sees them. Split find/create out of
GroupTreeNode.findOrCreateExplicitGroup into a reusable findGroupByName so the
finder is not duplicated, and document why findOrCreateExplicitGroup cannot be
used here (it attaches before the caller can assign).

* Remove unused import in CitationsResourceTest

subject: Fix force-push detection in Check PR Modifications (#16086)
body:
The `no-force-push` job used `git cat-file -e <before>` to decide whether
a push was a force-push, assuming the pre-push commit becomes unfetchable
after a force-push. With `actions/checkout` fetching `fetch-depth: 0`
against GitHub (which retains unreachable objects and serves arbitrary
SHAs), the `before` commit is frequently still present locally, so the
check reported "Regular push detected" for genuine force-pushes. The job
then passed and ghprcomment never posted the force-push notice.

Switch to an ancestry check: after a regular push `before` is an ancestor
of the new head; after a rebase/amend force-push it is not. This holds
regardless of whether the orphaned `before` object was fetched.

subject: Fix OpenAlex offline tests and stop sending empty api_key param (#16044)
body:
* Fix OpenAlex offline tests and stop sending empty api_key param

The OpenAlex fetcher built its query URL by unconditionally adding the
api_key parameter whenever getApiKey(FETCHER_NAME) returned a present
Optional. The configured key defaults to an empty string (the unset
state), so the Optional is present-but-empty and JabRef sent
?api_key=&search=... to the OpenAlex API on every search and full-text
lookup. Guard the parameter on a non-blank key in both getURLForQuery
and getUriBuilder.

This also fixes the offline OpenAlexFetcherTest methods, which had two
stale fixtures: the URL-builder tests expected a clean ?search= URL
(now produced by the non-blank guard), and the parser fixtures still
placed doi at the JSON root, whereas the parser has read it from the
nested ids.doi object since #15023.

* Update CHANGELOG with PR number

* Treat blank API key as absent in ImporterPreferences#getApiKey

The empty api_key= parameter was not OpenAlex-specific: getApiKey returned
a present-but-empty Optional whenever a fetcher's key defaulted to the
empty string (the unset state), and ~10 fetchers add the key with a bare
ifPresent. So every keyless request carried an empty key param/header.

Fix it at the source: getApiKey now treats a blank key as absent, so all
callers get the clean keyless behaviour without per-call-site guards.
Reverts the two OpenAlex.java call-site filters added earlier in favour of
the source fix, and adds ImporterPreferencesTest for the contract.

OpenAlexFetcherTest's mocked key now mirrors the real getApiKey (blank ->
empty), keeping the offline URL-builder assertions valid.

* Trim getApiKey javadoc and OpenAlex mock comment

* Use CsvSource textBlock in ImporterPreferencesTest

subject: Add arxiv doi handling (#16033)
body:
* Add dedicated arXiv DOI cleanup

Split the arXiv-specific handling out of DoiCleanup into a new,
toggleable ArXivDoiCleanup job. For arXiv entries the version-stable
DOI (prefix 10.48550/arXiv.) is treated as canonical:

- eprint present, DOI empty -> create DOI from eprint
- arXiv DOI matching eprint -> drop redundant eprint fields
- otherwise -> keep both

Expose the new step as a checkbox in the cleanup dialog so users
can choose it.

* Add PR links

* Make ArXivDoiCleanup order-independent of EprintCleanup

ArXivDoiCleanup read the eprint/doi fields directly and relied on
EprintCleanup having already moved arXiv identifiers from
url/journal/note/etc. into eprint. Cleanup job execution order is not
deterministic (activeJobs is a HashSet), so consolidation was applied
inconsistently.

Make the job self-contained: try to consolidate from the current
fields; if nothing applies, probe on a copy whether running
EprintCleanup first would enable a consolidation, and only then apply
the eprint move plus consolidation to the real entry. Entries without
arXiv data are left untouched, regardless of whether EprintCleanup runs
separately or at all.

* Repair invalid DOI in ArXivDoiCleanup rule 1

Rule 1 inferred an arXiv DOI only when the doi field was absent. Now it
treats the field as missing when DOI.parse rejects its value, so an
entry whose doi holds garbage but whose eprint holds a valid arXiv ID
gets repaired. Valid non-arXiv publisher DOIs still parse and are
preserved (rule 3), matching the "valid DOI exists" concept already used
by DoiCleanup.

subject: Enable use of liberica jdk full (#16031)
body:
* First build to use LibericaJDK

* Extract flag

* Fix dependency resolution under -PuseLibericaJdkFull

Replacing moduleNameToGA via get()/filterKeys/set() snapshotted the map
before the java-module-dependencies plugin finished contributing the
project's module-name -> GA mappings, discarding entries such as
'unirest.modules.gson'. That dropped the transitive version provider for
gson (and xz) -- the only deps not explicitly pinned in :versions --
causing "Could not find com.google.code.gson:gson:." with an empty
version.

Exclude org.openjfx from every configuration instead: applied lazily at
resolution time, it keeps JavaFX off the Maven classpath without touching
moduleNameToGA. Verified gson resolves to 2.13.2 and org.openjfx is
absent from the runtime classpath under the flag.

* Make -PuseLibericaJdkFull actually compile against JDK-bundled JavaFX

JabRef's GUI references internal com.sun.javafx.* packages. With Maven
JavaFX these are opened by the extra-java-module-info metadata patches;
with JavaFX consumed from the JDK those patches are inert, so javac could
not see the packages (e.g. com.sun.javafx.scene.NodeHelper,
com.sun.javafx.scene.control.ContextMenuContent).

Add the compile-time --add-exports counterpart of the runtime JVM args,
and stop passing --release on the Liberica path (javac forbids
--add-exports for system modules together with --release). The toolchain
is pinned to JDK 25, so it sets the target release.

Verified :jabgui:compileJava succeeds with -PuseLibericaJdkFull against a
locally installed BellSoft Liberica Full JDK 25.

* Parse -PuseLibericaJdkFull strictly

Previously any value except the exact lowercase "false" enabled the
mode, so gradle.properties values like "False", "0", or "no" silently
turned it on. Parse the property explicitly: blank (bare flag) and
"true" enable it, "false" disables it, anything else errors.

* Fail fast when Liberica JDK lacks bundled JavaFX

-PuseLibericaJdkFull selects vendor BELLSOFT, but Gradle's toolchain
query cannot distinguish Liberica "Full" (ships JavaFX) from Liberica
"Standard" (does not). If Standard is picked, compilation fails later
with a cryptic "module javafx.* not found" because the Maven JavaFX was
already excluded.

Resolve the toolchain and verify jmods/javafx.controls.jmod exists
before compiling; otherwise fail with an actionable message pointing at
Liberica Full and org.gradle.java.installations.paths.

PreToolUse hook commands used a relative path (python .claude/hooks/X.py).
The Bash tool's cwd persists, so from a subdirectory or worktree the path
resolved against that cwd and python exited 2, blocking the command before
it ran.

Use ${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR} (expanded by Git Bash on Windows) for an
absolute, cwd-independent path. Also resolve CHECKLIST.md from
CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR in checklist-done-guard.py, which otherwise silently
skipped the guard when run from a subdirectory.

* Default CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR to . in hook commands

If CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR is unset or empty, "${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR}/..."
expands to an absolute /.claude/hooks/... path that does not exist, so the
hook fails to execute. Use "${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR:-.}" so it falls back to
the current directory, matching the fallback already used in
checklist-done-guard.py.

locally then do not need to set both properties.

subject: Fix reflected XSS in HTTP server HTML entry preview (#15937)
body:
* Fix reflected XSS in HTTP server HTML entry preview

The text/html entry preview endpoint escaped the entry fields in the
success body but reflected the unknown citation key and library id
unescaped into the NotFoundException error message, which is served
with the same text/html content type. A crafted citation key or
library id in the URL could therefore inject markup into the error
page (reflected XSS).

Escape both path parameters with Guava's HtmlEscapers before building
the message. Also add a checklist rule to catch this class of issue.

* Update CHANGELOG.md

* Make escaped 404 message reach client and test it

The HTML entry-preview 404 escaped the citation key and library id in the
NotFoundException message, but GlobalExceptionMapper forwards
WebApplicationException.getResponse() verbatim and NotFoundException(String)
builds a response with no entity, so the message was never sent to the client.
The escaping had no observable effect.

Attach the escaped message as a text/html entity so it survives the mapper,
and add EntryResourceTest.htmlRepresentationEscapesCitationKeyInNotFoundMessage
asserting the 404 body reflects the citation key HTML-escaped, not raw.

* Remove CHANGELOG entry for HTTP server XSS

Before this branch there was no client-visible body: NotFoundException(String)
produced no entity and GlobalExceptionMapper forwarded it verbatim, so the
unescaped citation key was never reflected to the client. There was no
user-facing vulnerability to announce.

* Add HTML 404 example to rest-api.http; fix stray request body

Add an Error-cases entry hitting the HTML entry-preview 404 with a markup
citation key, documenting that the message is HTML-escaped.

The prose line under "## Creation" had no comment prefix, so IntelliJ's HTTP
Client parsed it as the request body of the preceding GET /libraries/notfound.
Prefix it with // so it is treated as a comment.

subject: Add POST /libraries/query and import endpoints (#15790)
body:
* Add POST /libraries/query endpoint for cross-library DOI and URL lookup

Introduces three DTOs (LibraryQueryRequest, LibraryQueryMatch,
LibraryQueryResponse), a POST /libraries/query endpoint on
LibrariesResource that searches all open libraries by DOI (with
normalisation) and URL, and five tests with OpenFastTrace tracing.
Extracts openLibraryIds() helper to eliminate duplication with get().

* Add test for DOI lookup against Chocolate.bib

Covers the real-library case using Corti_2009 (10.1161/circulationaha.108.827022).

* Add CHANGELOG entry for POST /libraries/query

* Add PR link

* add chocolate bib

* Fix tests

* Remove obsolete file

* WIP: Introduce InMemoryLibrarySearcher

* Make keyword seperator configurable

* Refactor: move IndexManager + indexing/retrieval into sqlbased subpackage

Groups all SQL/Postgres + Lucene-backed search infrastructure under
org.jabref.logic.search.sqlbased so the in-memory alternative can sit
as a peer subpackage. Mechanical move only — no behavior change.

Moved:
- IndexManager, LuceneIndexer, PostgreServer (search/ -> search/sqlbased/)
- indexing/* (BibFieldsIndexer, DefaultLinkedFilesIndexer, DocumentReader,
  ReadOnlyLinkedFilesIndexer) -> sqlbased/indexing/
- retrieval/* (BibFieldsSearcher, LinkedFilesSearcher) -> sqlbased/retrieval/
- Corresponding tests follow the same pattern.

Updated module-info exports + all importers across jablib, jabgui, jabsrv.

* Add usePostgresSearch preference + General tab checkbox

Adds a boolean preference (default false) for choosing whether the
GUI's search should be backed by Postgres+Lucene or by the in-memory
search implementation. This commit only wires the plumbing — the
actual branching of the GUI search code path lands in a follow-up.

- New SEARCH_USE_POSTGRES key in JabRefCliPreferences (default false).
- New usePostgresSearch BooleanProperty on SearchPreferences, written
  back to storage via EasyBind listener.
- New checkbox in General preferences tab, bound bidirectionally to
  the property in GeneralTabViewModel.
- i18n string in JabRef_en.properties.

* Introduce SearchContext (Bridge GoF) + SearchBackend Implementor

Decouples the GUI's view of search from the concrete search engine
using the Bridge pattern (Gamma et al., 1994, pp. 151-161).

- SearchBackend: the Implementor interface with search, isEntryMatched,
  and indexing-lifecycle methods (addToIndex, removeFromIndex,
  updateEntry, close).
- SearchContext: the Abstraction holding a SearchBackend reference and
  forwarding all calls. Subscribes to SearchPreferences#usePostgresSearchProperty
  and swaps the backend live (closes old, builds new via supplier) when
  the user toggles the preference.
- SqlSearchBackend (sqlbased): wraps the existing IndexManager
  (Postgres metadata + Lucene fulltext).
- InMemorySearchBackend (inmemory): wraps InMemoryLibrarySearcher;
  adapts List<BibEntry> matches into SearchResults; lifecycle methods
  are no-ops (no index to maintain). No fulltext support.

This commit only adds the new types — wiring them into LibraryTab and
the GUI call sites lands in the next commit.

* Wire SearchContext into LibraryTab + GUI search call sites (live swap)

Replaces IndexManager with SearchContext (the Bridge abstraction) throughout
the GUI and srv state-manager layer. Toggling the "Use Postgres-backed search"
preference now swaps the backing SearchBackend live — no JabRef restart needed.

API renames (StateManager + SrvStateManager):
- setIndexManager / getIndexManager -> setSearchContext / getSearchContext

LibraryTab:
- createIndexManager / getIndexManager / closeIndexManger ->
  createSearchContext / getSearchContext / closeSearchContext
- createSearchContext() now builds a SearchContext with two suppliers:
  - SqlSearchBackend wrapping a freshly-built IndexManager
  - InMemorySearchBackend wrapping InMemoryLibrarySearcher
  The context picks one based on the current usePostgresSearch preference
  and rebuilds on change.
- The 3 index-update event listeners (EntriesAddedEvent, EntriesRemovedEvent,
  FieldChangedEvent) now route through searchContext.{addToIndex,
  removeFromIndex, updateEntry}; in-memory backend treats these as no-ops.

GUI search call sites updated to use SearchContext:
- MainTableDataModel (3 indexManager.search calls)
- GroupNodeViewModel (3 stateManager.getIndexManager calls)
- GroupDialogViewModel (1)
- SearchResultsTableDataModel (1)
- RebuildFulltextSearchIndexAction (1)
- SaveDatabaseAction (close/recreate lifecycle calls)

Added rebuildFullTextIndex() to SearchBackend so the GUI's "rebuild
fulltext index" action can stay backend-agnostic; in-memory implements
it as a no-op.

Also updated ServerTest's mock CliPreferences to expose
getBibEntryPreferences() — InMemoryLibrarySearcher needs the keyword
separator from there.

* Reorder usePostgresSearch to sit next to fulltext in preferences

Move SEARCH_USE_POSTGRES constant directly after SEARCH_FULLTEXT (and the
corresponding default + SearchPreferences constructor parameter + field).
The two settings are conceptually related — Postgres-backed search is
what enables fulltext content matching in linked files — so keeping them
adjacent makes the preferences easier to scan.

* Drop local MatchType enum in favor of SearchFlags

BibEntryMatchVisitor had a private enum {INEXACT, EXACT, REGEX} that
duplicated three values already present on org.jabref.model.search.SearchFlags
(INEXACT_MATCH, EXACT_MATCH, REGULAR_EXPRESSION). Use the canonical
SearchFlags vocabulary so the visitor speaks the same language as the
rest of the search subsystem (e.g. SearchToSqlVisitor).

* Resolve CAYW search TODO: use InMemoryLibrarySearcher for the dialog filter

CAYWResource.openSearchGui previously had a TODO to wire the dialog
filter through a LibrarySearcher so the popup understood the Search.g4
grammar instead of doing a plain substring match on a few label fields.

Now:
- openSearchGui takes the BibDatabaseContext as a parameter and builds an
  InMemoryLibrarySearcher once per dialog open.
- The dialog's filter callback parses each keystroke as a SearchQuery; if
  the expression is valid (Search.g4), it filters via the searcher.
- If the user is mid-typing (e.g. "author=") and the expression is invalid,
  fall back to the legacy substring match across label/shortLabel/description
  so the list stays responsive instead of going empty.

Added InMemoryLibrarySearcher#matches(BibEntry, SearchQuery) so the
dialog can test a single entry without iterating the whole library on
every keystroke.

* CAYWResource: use jspecify @NullMarked, drop redundant null check

The class declared one @Nullable return (getChocolateBibAsStream)
but otherwise relied on implicit non-null semantics + an explicit
searchText == null check.

Switch to @NullMarked at the class level so non-null is the default,
and drop the searchText == null check in filterEntries. The JavaFX
TextField text the dialog feeds in is never null — defaults to empty
string — so the null branch was dead in practice.

* Fix submodules

* Reformat code

* Move POST /libraries/query CHANGELOG entry to Unreleased

* Fix CHANGELOG blank line after merge

* Rename Postgres search checkbox to "Experimental search (Postgres)"

Move the checkbox out of the Saving section to directly below the
"User interface" section in the General preferences tab.

* Fix submodules

* Add new sources to JabSrvLauncher jbang script

The new jabsrv DTOs (LibraryQueryMatch/Request/Response),
LibraryQueryExpressionBuilder service, and the jablib SearchContext +
in-memory search backend classes do not exist in the 6.0-SNAPSHOT
jablib artifact yet, so jbang compilation fails without them.

* Fix CAYW: force JavaFX 26 and harden Platform.startup error path

afterburner.fx 2.0.0's POM pins javafx-* to version 20. Gradle's
consistent-resolution upgraded most artifacts to 26.0.1, but the
JBang launcher (which resolves purely via Maven) ended up with
javafx.graphics:20 alongside javafx.base:26. Platform.startup then
threw NoClassDefFoundError: javafx/util/FXPermission (removed in
javafx 25), which surfaced as an opaque 500 on /better-bibtex/cayw.

- Strip and re-declare afterburner.fx's javafx-* deps in the Gradle
  dependency-rules so nothing requests javafx 20 transitively.
- Pin javafx-{base,graphics,controls,fxml}:26.0.1 in the JBang
  jabsrv launcher to override afterburner's transitive 20.
- Catch Throwable/IllegalStateException around Platform.startup in
  CAYWResource and translate to a clear 503 response; set the
  `initialized` flag outside the FX lambda so a synchronous startup
  failure no longer risks a hung latch.

* Fix format

* Fix submodules

* Use strongly-typed LibraryQueryRequest/Response in /libraries/query

Register a Gson-backed MessageBodyReader and MessageBodyWriter so JAX-RS
resources can declare POJO parameters and return values for
application/json instead of manually parsing String request bodies and
calling gson.toJson on responses.

The query endpoint now reads LibraryQueryRequest directly and returns a
LibraryQueryResponse. Open org.jabref.http.dto to the HK2 utilities
module so injection into the new providers works.

* Refine AGENTS.md

* Add initial CHECKLIST.md

* Use _

* Add reformatting hints

* Route LibrariesResource through SrvStateManager.getSearchContext

Make the stand-alone JabRefSrvStateManager build an in-memory SearchContext
on demand so the GUI orchestrator and the stand-alone server can share the
same SearchContext-based code path. Resources no longer instantiate
InMemoryLibrarySearcher directly.

Also extend POST /libraries/query with an optional free-text `query` field
carrying a Search.g4 expression. When present, it takes precedence over the
`dois` / `urls` convenience lists and matches are reported without
doi/url attribution via the new LibraryQueryMatch.forEntry factory.

* Fix formatting

* Rename freeText -> hasSearchQuery in query route

The `query` field carries a Search.g4 expression, not arbitrary free text;
align the variable and test names with that grammar.

* Make SrvStateManager.getSearchContext return SearchContext directly

The lifecycle (LibraryTab on database open, JabRefSrvStateManager on
demand) guarantees a SearchContext exists by the time callers ask for
one, so the Optional wrapper added clutter without value at every call
site (`ifPresent`, `orElseThrow`, `.get()`).

If the invariant is violated, log an error and fall back to a new
NoOpSearchBackend-backed SearchContext that returns empty SearchResults
so the application keeps running instead of crashing. An `assert`
surfaces the bug for developers running with -ea.

* Refine AGENTS.md and add CHECKLIST.md

* Fix typo

* Fix typos and clarify guidance in AGENTS.md

Correct spelling errors, switch lint command fences and the docker formatter command to valid bash, reword the reformatting rule, use straight quotes, and align the standard header block phrasing. Add the missing verb to the StringUtil.isBlank checklist item.

* Expand CHECKLIST.md into a final quality gate

Restructure CHECKLIST.md into code rules, verification commands, and documentation sections so it serves as the post-work quality check. Clarify in AGENTS.md that it is development-time guidance while CHECKLIST.md is the final check.

* Fix submodules

* feat(jabsrv): groups endpoint, multi-query, import-to-group

- POST /libraries/query now takes an ordered list of Search.g4
  queries; the doi/url lists are removed
- GET /libraries/{id}/groups lists a library's groups as a flat
  breadcrumb list
- POST /libraries/{id}/entries accepts an optional ?group= query
  param; imported entries are assigned to it, group created if missing

* Fix GroupTreeViewModelTest

* Fix formatting in GroupChange.java

* Remove "query" sub resource

* Fix JBang launcher

* Remove obosolete requirements

* Introduce constants for the "field" query part

* Fix checkstyle

* Address Qodo review comments

- InMemorySearchBackend: isEntryMatched uses per-entry searcher.matches
  instead of a full-library scan; search now sets query.setSearchResults
  so getSearchResults() is not stale after a backend switch
- GsonMessageBodyReader: isReadable declines String/byte[]/InputStream/
  Reader so raw-JSON resources keep using the container readers
- JabRefSrvStateManager: wire the in-memory backend into both backend
  slots instead of a supplier that throws UnsupportedOperationException

* Revert "Remove obosolete requirements"

This reverts commit 9ad44938beb5afd837b4826a1be8210e6130d4f1.

* Revert "Fix JBang launcher"

This reverts commit ecff003ac26d2688484dd364816fe1c722c5bcb0.

* Revert "Remove "query" sub resource"

This reverts commit 4df2e6e19e3fc615dffc0e0ece828038ea25a747.

* Fix checkstyle

* Rewrite Optional use

* Make exception more explicit but use Optional pattern

* Fix checkstyle

* Cache compiled regexes in BibEntryMatchVisitor

matchRegex compiled a fresh Pattern on every match attempt; a visitor is
created per BibEntry, so scanning a library recompiled the same pattern
once per entry. Reuse compiled patterns via a Guava Cache keyed by
pattern + case mode, with a 15-minute write/access expiry.

Also rewrite Optional handling to .filter()/.ifPresent():
- BibEntryWriter.writeField uses Unchecked.consumer, unwrapping a
  wrapped IOException back into the declared throws clause
- BibEntryMatchVisitor.matchNamedField/matchAnyField use filter().isPresent()

* Use Caffeine instead of Guava cache for compiled regexes

Switch BibEntryMatchVisitor's COMPILED_PATTERNS cache from Guava to
Caffeine, the caching library already used elsewhere in jablib
(CitationStyleCache, FileAnnotationCache). Behavior is unchanged: keyed
by pattern + case mode, 15-minute write/access expiry.

Add an ArchUnit rule (doNotUseGuavaCache) forbidding any dependency on
com.google.common.cache so Caffeine stays the single caching library.

* Fix OpenRewrite

* Reword CHANGELOG.md without techspeak

* Share SearchContext registry between GUI and server state managers

Extract AbstractSrvStateManager holding the per-database SearchContext
map plus get/setSearchContext. Both JabRefGuiStateManager and
JabRefSrvStateManager now extend it instead of each keeping their own
registry and lookup.

JabRefSrvStateManager parses every served library once at startup and
builds an in-memory SearchContext for each in its constructor, so
getSearchContext only ever returns pre-built contexts. The constructor
now takes BibEntryPreferences plus the parsed databases instead of
CliPreferences. getOpenDatabases() returns the held libraries.

* Add plain-citation HTTP endpoint and refine parsing

- jabsrv: new POST /libraries/{id}/entries accepting text/plain that
  parses a reference via the user's configured plain-citation parser
  (including LLM) and appends it to the current library.
- PlainCitationParserFactory: split into two methods so the LLM branch
  takes a non-null AiService; the other branch needs no AiService at
  all. Removes the @Nullable parameter and the runtime null check.
- RuleBasedPlainCitationParser: extract DOI before URL matching so a
  doi.org link is recognised as a DOI rather than swallowed as a URL.
- DOI: add replaceInText helper that reuses the existing matchers so
  callers can strip a DOI (including any URL / "doi:" prefix) without
  re-deriving the regex.

* Remove null targetGroup from AppendBibTeXToCurrentLibrary callers

Make the record canonical signature use Optional<String> and add
convenience constructors taking either just the bibtex or a non-null
target-group string. Callers no longer pass `null`:

- ArgumentProcessor uses the single-argument constructor.
- EntriesResource branches on the @Nullable query param to pick the
  appropriate constructor.
- JabRefFrameViewModel exposes two distinct overloads of
  importBibtexStringAndOpen / directImportEntries and dispatches via
  Optional.ifPresentOrElse, so the no-group path no longer carries a
  nullable parameter through.

* Consolidate CHANGELOG entry for HTTP server additions

* Fix TODO marker

* Address review comments (and apply formatting)

* Fix formatting

* Remove "filesToServe"

* Add mtime modifications

* Merge importBibtexStringAndOpen overloads with @Nullable targetGroup

Collapse the two `importBibtexStringAndOpen` and `directImportEntries`
overloads into one each, accepting a `@Nullable String targetGroup`.
The caller passes `targetGroup().orElse(null)`.

* Move group-lookup logic to GroupTreeNode.findOrCreateExplicitGroup

Pulls the iterate/find-or-create-subgroup snippet out of the GUI layer
and into the model, where it belongs. JabRefFrameViewModel.assignToGroup
now only handles the metadata root fallback.

* Refactor parser ternary to if/else in NewEntryViewModel

The ternary spanning the LLM and non-LLM factory calls was too long to
read at a glance; split into an explicit if/else.

* Use StringUtil.isNotBlank for targetGroup check

Replaces the explicit null-and-blank check with the shared helper.

* Add Javadoc to RuleBasedPlainCitationParser.findDoi

Documents the side effect on the doi field and the reason the method
runs before findUrls. The previous inline comment is folded into the
Javadoc to avoid duplication.

* Fix checkstyle

* Use StringUtil.isBlank for citationText check

* Switch refreshStaleLibraries to ListIterator

Drops the manual index in favor of a ListIterator so the loop reads
like an enhanced for-each while still being able to replace the
current element via it.set().

* trigger ci

* Fix checkstyle

* Fix test

* Fix method reference

* Link addBibtex to req~jabsrv.import.group~1

* Try to fix module-info from JabSrv

* Strip DOI instead of placeholder in RuleBasedPlainCitationParser

DOI_TAG contained no digits, skewing findParts' non-digit segment count
that infers title, journalOrPublisher, and isArticle. The DOI is already
stored in the doi field, so dropping it from the residual string is
sufficient and keeps the heuristic accurate.

* Fix setAvailableLibraries clobbering filesToServe

setUp() resets filesToServe to GENERAL_SERVER_TEST as its per-test default.
setAvailableLibraries called setUp() after assigning filesToServe, so the
assignment was overwritten and the new JabRefSrvStateManager loaded the
wrong library — causing 404s in GroupsResourceTest#listsGroupsAsBreadcrumbs.
Call super.setUp() to skip the override.

* Pick earliest match in DOI.findInTextInternal

The previous loop overwrote 'result' for each pattern, so the returned match
was whichever pattern was tried last, not the first DOI in the text.
replaceInText relied on this being the first occurrence and could otherwise
strip the wrong span.

* Use named regex group 'doi' in DOI patterns

Replaces unnamed group \1 with (?<doi>...) across all DOI patterns and a
DOI_GROUP constant. Callers read matcher.group(DOI_GROUP) instead of group(1).
The shortcut form prepends "10/" so the DOI constructor parses it via
EXACT_SHORT_DOI_PATT instead of re-deriving the doi.org/ URL form.

* Fix depdency scope

* Fix test - again

* Document jabsrv mtime reload as ADR 0061

Add ADR 0061 documenting the decision to keep mtime polling for
library reload in jabsrv instead of moving DefaultFileUpdateMonitor
to jablib or duplicating it. Mark `refreshStaleLibraries` with
`@ADR(61)`.

Also fix a SearchContext leak when a library is re-parsed: the old
context's entry stayed in the registry under a uid no caller held.
Add `AbstractSrvStateManager#removeSearchContext` and call it from
`refreshStaleLibraries` before replacing the context.

* Return snapshot from JabRefSrvStateManager#getOpenDatabases

Grizzly/Jersey serves requests concurrently and several resources call
`srvStateManager.getOpenDatabases().stream()`. Returning the live
`openDatabases` ObservableList let a caller iterate it while another
thread entered `refreshStaleLibraries` and structurally modified the
same list via `ListIterator#set`.

Take the snapshot under the existing monitor and return an unmodifiable
observable wrapper so iteration after the call is race-free. Also mark
`getAllDatabasePaths` synchronized so its stream over `openDatabases`
runs under the same monitor.

Add scripts/check-http-server.py: a stdlib-only (urllib) smoke check that
verifies the JabRef REST server responds on the root page and /libraries,
mirroring the basic commands in jabsrv/src/test/rest-api.http without
requiring IntelliJ HTTP Client.

* Fix Markdown ad MapResource

* Add duplicate check to addFromCache citation endpoint

When SumatraPDF (or any other client) re-issues an add against a cached
citation that the user has since accepted, refuse the second copy: run
DuplicateCheck and return 200 with {"status":"already-exists","entryId"}
instead of appending another entry to the library.

Refactor the success path to a small Optional chain so the lookup ->
either-already-exists-or-append branches are an Optional.map / orElseGet
pair rather than an isPresent / get pattern.

* Move batch query to libraries:query (Google AIP-136 colon notation)

POST /libraries/query lost JAX-RS path-specificity arbitration against
the per-library route @Path("libraries/{id}"): the {id}=query match
beats the sibling on literal-character count, so the request reached
LibraryResource (which has no POST handler) and returned 405.

Switch the URL to libraries:query, following Google's API Improvement
Proposal 136 for custom (non-CRUD) methods on a collection — the colon
sits between the collection name and the verb with no separating
slash, eliminating the path-segment collision entirely.

JAX-RS cannot produce libraries:query via @Path("libraries") +
@Path(":query") because the spec inserts a single separating slash
between class and method paths. The endpoint therefore moves to a new
dedicated resource class LibrariesQueryResource(@Path("libraries:query")).

- Rename test URLs to /libraries:query; switch the test's local

Class-level Javadoc on LibrariesQueryResource cites and quotes AIP-136
and explains the JAX-RS specificity rationale.

part.matches(".*\d.*") fed user-provided text into a backtracking
regex flagged by static analysis. Replace with a linear codePoints scan.

* Serve bundled Chocolate.bib as demo library in jabsrv CLI

The CLI demo path pointed at a non-existent http-server-demo.bib via a cwd-relative filesystem path, which failed unless launched from the jabsrv module root.

Serve the bundled Chocolate.bib instead: it sits at the resources root of jablib (a jabsrv dependency), so it is reachable on the classpath. Since JabRefSrvStateManager needs a filesystem Path, the classpath resource is copied to a temp file (deleted on exit). body:
* Fix formatter annotation script and dedupe CI formatting checks

- format-diff-annotations.sh: stop the line 74 comment apostrophes from closing the bash single-quoted awk program (which silently dropped all matching rules); use singular 'line N' for single-line annotations.

- Extract the repeated check/diff/upload steps in tests-code.yml into the reusable .github/actions/check-formatting composite action, which also uploads the diff as a patch artifact for local 'git apply'.

* Fix inaccurate range-format comment in format-diff-annotations.sh

The output now uses "line N" for single-line hunks and "lines N-M" for
ranges, but the header comment still described only the "lines X-Y"
form. Update the comment to match.

* Detect staged and untracked changes in check-formatting

format-diff-annotations.sh used plain `git diff`, which only sees
unstaged modifications. Staged changes and untracked files could remain
while CI reported the tree clean, contradicting the action's "uncommitted
changes" contract.

Mark untracked files intent-to-add, then diff against HEAD so the check
covers unstaged, staged, and untracked changes. Update the action
description and the failure-path diff dump to match.

through HeadlessExecutorService.executeAll with a hard 10 second cap.
Fetchers that need to bounce through an institutional sign-in (e.g.
SeamlessAccess / SAML IdP redirect chain) or that wait on a slow
publisher CDN cannot complete in 10 s and silently lose to faster but
empty results. 60 s gives those flows enough headroom without making
the overall fetch noticeably slower on the happy path — losing
fetchers are still cancelled as soon as a winning result arrives.

* Link CHANGELOG entry to PR

* Raise per-fetcher fulltext timeout to 120 seconds

60 s was tight for fetchers that wait on a SAML IdP redirect chain
plus a slow publisher download. 120 s leaves headroom while still
letting the user reasonably cancel; losing fetchers are still
cancelled as soon as a winning result arrives.

subject: Annotate wrongly formatted lines in CI (#15871)
body:
* Annotate wrongly formatted lines in CI

The format, format-javadoc, and openrewrite jobs previously failed via `git diff --exit-code` without telling reviewers which lines were wrong.

Add .github/format-diff-annotations.sh, which parses the post-format `git diff` and emits a GitHub Actions `::error` annotation with a line range (file/line/endLine) for each diff hunk, then exits non-zero so the job still fails. Wire all three jobs to call it.

* Percent-encode file path in CI annotations

The `::error` workflow command did not escape the `file` property, so
paths containing `:` or `,` (e.g. Windows paths) could be mis-parsed or
ignored by GitHub Actions. Add an AWK `escape_property` function that
mirrors org.jabref.logic.util.GitHubActionsEscape#property (escape %,
CR, LF, then : and ,) and apply it to the file path.

* Anchor pure-addition hunks on the new line range

A hunk with oldCount==0 (new file / pure addition) has oldStart==0, so
annotating the old range produced `line=0,endLine=0`, which points at no
real line. Parse the new range ($3) too and, when there are no old lines,
anchor on newStart..newStart+newCount-1. Clamp start>=1 and end>=start.

* Make annotation title and message configurable

The script is reused by the openrewrite job, where a remaining diff means
`:rewriteRun` output was not committed rather than a formatting problem,
yet it always emitted title=Formatting and a 'run the formatter' message.

Add ANNOTATION_TITLE and ANNOTATION_MESSAGE_PREFIX env vars (defaulting to
the existing formatting wording, escaped via the data/property rules) and
set OpenRewrite-specific text in the openrewrite job.

body:
* Fix truncation check in getValidFileName to account for extension length
When a BibTeX entry has a very long title, renaming the linked file
via pattern failed with a misleading error message. The root cause
was that getValidFileName() checked only the name length without
the extension against the 255-char OS limit.

For example, a name of 252 chars + '.pdf' = 256 total would pass
the old check (252 > 255 = false) and return a 256-char filename,
causing Files.move() to fail on Windows.

Fix: check the full filename length (name + extension) against
MAXIMUM_FILE_NAME_LENGTH before deciding whether to truncate.

subject: Fix duplicate finder progress counter incrementing on empty queue polls (#15781)
Refine JabKit CLI: positional input argument and check command group (#15759)
body:
* Fix description

* Fix typos

* Refine JabKit CLI: positional input + check command group

Group the consistency and integrity checks under a new `check` parent
command (`jabkit check consistency`, `jabkit check integrity`) and default
`check integrity` to the txt output format.

Accept the input file as a positional argument on every input-taking
subcommand via a shared InputOption mixin; `--input` is kept as an alias.
This supersedes ADR-0045 (ADR-0057) for increased convenience while
preserving cross-command consistency.

* Add errorformat output to the consistency check

Add a BibliographyConsistencyCheckResultErrorFormatWriter producing
line-oriented `file:line:column: message` output, mirroring the integrity
check's errorformat writer. One line is emitted per deviating field of a
reported entry.

Make `errorformat` the default output format for both `jabkit check`
subcommands.

* Move JabKit CLI changelog entries to "Added" and link PR #15759

* Run both checks when jabkit check given a file without a subcommand

jabkit check <file> now runs the consistency and integrity checks together.
The shared check logic is extracted into static execute() methods so the
parent check command and the consistency/integrity subcommands reuse it.

* Extract jabkit check output-format constants

Replace the "errorformat"/"txt"/"csv" string literals in the `check`
commands with `FORMAT_*` constants on `Check`.

* Fix ternary indentation in InputOption

Align the `?`/`:` operators under the first operand to match the JabRef
code style.

* Add mavenlocal

* Refine JBang checks

* Pin JBang scripts to Java 25

* Refine check worfklow

* Use citationKey:field segments in check errorformat output

Emit findings as `file:line:column:citationKey[:field]: message` in both
the integrity and consistency error-format writers. Entry-level findings
carry only the citation key; field-level findings add the field name.

Document the format as req~jabkit.cli.check-errorformat-output~1 and link
it from the writers.

* Factor out file import/validation in the check commands

Extract the duplicated import-and-validate block from CheckConsistency
and CheckIntegrity into JabKit.importBibtexLibrary, which returns an
ImportOutcome record. Callers no longer unwrap an Optional.

* Drop the integrity check txt writer, alias txt to errorformat

Remove IntegrityCheckResultTxtWriter. The integrity check's `txt` output
format is now an alias for `errorformat`; `csv` is unchanged. The
consistency check keeps its tabular `txt` output.

* Format switch case labels in CheckIntegrity

* Split launcher --help checks into separate steps

One step per launcher in the jbang-check action, so a failure points
precisely at the offending launcher.

* Localize the jabkit subcommand messages

Wrap the "Specify a subcommand ..." and PDF format-option messages in
Localization.lang and add the keys to JabRef_en.properties.

* Make pdf update fail with a non-zero exit on a bad --format

Print the --format validation error to System.err and convert PdfUpdate
to Callable<Integer> so usage and import errors exit with code 2.

* Send CLI errors to System.err with non-zero exit codes

Route user-facing error and usage messages in the jabkit commands to
System.err, and convert the remaining Runnable commands to
Callable<Integer> so failures exit with code 2 instead of 0.

* Fix consistency errorformat writer test assertions

Update the expected lines to the file:line:column:citationKey:field
format the writer now produces.

* Add JBang setup for jbang check

* More powerful runner for :jabkit:runJabKitPortableSmokeTest

* Fix NPE

* Fix handling of "null"

* Signal integrity findings with a non-zero exit code

CheckIntegrity.execute() always returned 0, so `jabkit check integrity`
and `jabkit check FILE` could not report integrity findings via exit
status, letting CI pass with integrity problems.

Return 1 when findings exist (0 = none, 1 = findings, 2/3 = error),
matching CheckConsistency. The parent `check` command propagates the
worst code via Math.max.

subject: Add InMemorySearch (#15599)
body:
* Add POST /libraries/query endpoint for cross-library DOI and URL lookup

Introduces three DTOs (LibraryQueryRequest, LibraryQueryMatch,
LibraryQueryResponse), a POST /libraries/query endpoint on
LibrariesResource that searches all open libraries by DOI (with
normalisation) and URL, and five tests with OpenFastTrace tracing.
Extracts openLibraryIds() helper to eliminate duplication with get().

* Add test for DOI lookup against Chocolate.bib

Covers the real-library case using Corti_2009 (10.1161/circulationaha.108.827022).

* Add CHANGELOG entry for POST /libraries/query

* Add PR link

* add chocolate bib

* Fix tests

* Remove obsolete file

* WIP: Introduce InMemoryLibrarySearcher

* Make keyword seperator configurable

* Refactor: move IndexManager + indexing/retrieval into sqlbased subpackage

Groups all SQL/Postgres + Lucene-backed search infrastructure under
org.jabref.logic.search.sqlbased so the in-memory alternative can sit
as a peer subpackage. Mechanical move only — no behavior change.

Moved:
- IndexManager, LuceneIndexer, PostgreServer (search/ -> search/sqlbased/)
- indexing/* (BibFieldsIndexer, DefaultLinkedFilesIndexer, DocumentReader,
  ReadOnlyLinkedFilesIndexer) -> sqlbased/indexing/
- retrieval/* (BibFieldsSearcher, LinkedFilesSearcher) -> sqlbased/retrieval/
- Corresponding tests follow the same pattern.

Updated module-info exports + all importers across jablib, jabgui, jabsrv.

* Add usePostgresSearch preference + General tab checkbox

Adds a boolean preference (default false) for choosing whether the
GUI's search should be backed by Postgres+Lucene or by the in-memory
search implementation. This commit only wires the plumbing — the
actual branching of the GUI search code path lands in a follow-up.

- New SEARCH_USE_POSTGRES key in JabRefCliPreferences (default false).
- New usePostgresSearch BooleanProperty on SearchPreferences, written
  back to storage via EasyBind listener.
- New checkbox in General preferences tab, bound bidirectionally to
  the property in GeneralTabViewModel.
- i18n string in JabRef_en.properties.

* Introduce SearchContext (Bridge GoF) + SearchBackend Implementor

Decouples the GUI's view of search from the concrete search engine
using the Bridge pattern (Gamma et al., 1994, pp. 151-161).

- SearchBackend: the Implementor interface with search, isEntryMatched,
  and indexing-lifecycle methods (addToIndex, removeFromIndex,
  updateEntry, close).
- SearchContext: the Abstraction holding a SearchBackend reference and
  forwarding all calls. Subscribes to SearchPreferences#usePostgresSearchProperty
  and swaps the backend live (closes old, builds new via supplier) when
  the user toggles the preference.
- SqlSearchBackend (sqlbased): wraps the existing IndexManager
  (Postgres metadata + Lucene fulltext).
- InMemorySearchBackend (inmemory): wraps InMemoryLibrarySearcher;
  adapts List<BibEntry> matches into SearchResults; lifecycle methods
  are no-ops (no index to maintain). No fulltext support.

This commit only adds the new types — wiring them into LibraryTab and
the GUI call sites lands in the next commit.

* Wire SearchContext into LibraryTab + GUI search call sites (live swap)

Replaces IndexManager with SearchContext (the Bridge abstraction) throughout
the GUI and srv state-manager layer. Toggling the "Use Postgres-backed search"
preference now swaps the backing SearchBackend live — no JabRef restart needed.

API renames (StateManager + SrvStateManager):
- setIndexManager / getIndexManager -> setSearchContext / getSearchContext

LibraryTab:
- createIndexManager / getIndexManager / closeIndexManger ->
  createSearchContext / getSearchContext / closeSearchContext
- createSearchContext() now builds a SearchContext with two suppliers:
  - SqlSearchBackend wrapping a freshly-built IndexManager
  - InMemorySearchBackend wrapping InMemoryLibrarySearcher
  The context picks one based on the current usePostgresSearch preference
  and rebuilds on change.
- The 3 index-update event listeners (EntriesAddedEvent, EntriesRemovedEvent,
  FieldChangedEvent) now route through searchContext.{addToIndex,
  removeFromIndex, updateEntry}; in-memory backend treats these as no-ops.

GUI search call sites updated to use SearchContext:
- MainTableDataModel (3 indexManager.search calls)
- GroupNodeViewModel (3 stateManager.getIndexManager calls)
- GroupDialogViewModel (1)
- SearchResultsTableDataModel (1)
- RebuildFulltextSearchIndexAction (1)
- SaveDatabaseAction (close/recreate lifecycle calls)

Added rebuildFullTextIndex() to SearchBackend so the GUI's "rebuild
fulltext index" action can stay backend-agnostic; in-memory implements
it as a no-op.

Also updated ServerTest's mock CliPreferences to expose
getBibEntryPreferences() — InMemoryLibrarySearcher needs the keyword
separator from there.

* Reorder usePostgresSearch to sit next to fulltext in preferences

Move SEARCH_USE_POSTGRES constant directly after SEARCH_FULLTEXT (and the
corresponding default + SearchPreferences constructor parameter + field).
The two settings are conceptually related — Postgres-backed search is
what enables fulltext content matching in linked files — so keeping them
adjacent makes the preferences easier to scan.

* Drop local MatchType enum in favor of SearchFlags

BibEntryMatchVisitor had a private enum {INEXACT, EXACT, REGEX} that
duplicated three values already present on org.jabref.model.search.SearchFlags
(INEXACT_MATCH, EXACT_MATCH, REGULAR_EXPRESSION). Use the canonical
SearchFlags vocabulary so the visitor speaks the same language as the
rest of the search subsystem (e.g. SearchToSqlVisitor).

* Resolve CAYW search TODO: use InMemoryLibrarySearcher for the dialog filter

CAYWResource.openSearchGui previously had a TODO to wire the dialog
filter through a LibrarySearcher so the popup understood the Search.g4
grammar instead of doing a plain substring match on a few label fields.

Now:
- openSearchGui takes the BibDatabaseContext as a parameter and builds an
  InMemoryLibrarySearcher once per dialog open.
- The dialog's filter callback parses each keystroke as a SearchQuery; if
  the expression is valid (Search.g4), it filters via the searcher.
- If the user is mid-typing (e.g. "author=") and the expression is invalid,
  fall back to the legacy substring match across label/shortLabel/description
  so the list stays responsive instead of going empty.

Added InMemoryLibrarySearcher#matches(BibEntry, SearchQuery) so the
dialog can test a single entry without iterating the whole library on
every keystroke.

* CAYWResource: use jspecify @NullMarked, drop redundant null check

The class declared one @Nullable return (getChocolateBibAsStream)
but otherwise relied on implicit non-null semantics + an explicit
searchText == null check.

Switch to @NullMarked at the class level so non-null is the default,
and drop the searchText == null check in filterEntries. The JavaFX
TextField text the dialog feeds in is never null — defaults to empty
string — so the null branch was dead in practice.

* Fix submodules

* Reformat code

* Move POST /libraries/query CHANGELOG entry to Unreleased

* Fix CHANGELOG blank line after merge

* Rename Postgres search checkbox to "Experimental search (Postgres)"

Move the checkbox out of the Saving section to directly below the
"User interface" section in the General preferences tab.

* Fix submodules

* Add new sources to JabSrvLauncher jbang script

The new jabsrv DTOs (LibraryQueryMatch/Request/Response),
LibraryQueryExpressionBuilder service, and the jablib SearchContext +
in-memory search backend classes do not exist in the 6.0-SNAPSHOT
jablib artifact yet, so jbang compilation fails without them.

* Fix CAYW: force JavaFX 26 and harden Platform.startup error path

afterburner.fx 2.0.0's POM pins javafx-* to version 20. Gradle's
consistent-resolution upgraded most artifacts to 26.0.1, but the
JBang launcher (which resolves purely via Maven) ended up with
javafx.graphics:20 alongside javafx.base:26. Platform.startup then
threw NoClassDefFoundError: javafx/util/FXPermission (removed in
javafx 25), which surfaced as an opaque 500 on /better-bibtex/cayw.

- Strip and re-declare afterburner.fx's javafx-* deps in the Gradle
  dependency-rules so nothing requests javafx 20 transitively.
- Pin javafx-{base,graphics,controls,fxml}:26.0.1 in the JBang
  jabsrv launcher to override afterburner's transitive 20.
- Catch Throwable/IllegalStateException around Platform.startup in
  CAYWResource and translate to a clear 503 response; set the
  `initialized` flag outside the FX lambda so a synchronous startup
  failure no longer risks a hung latch.

* Fix format

* Fix submodules

* Use strongly-typed LibraryQueryRequest/Response in /libraries/query

Register a Gson-backed MessageBodyReader and MessageBodyWriter so JAX-RS
resources can declare POJO parameters and return values for
application/json instead of manually parsing String request bodies and
calling gson.toJson on responses.

The query endpoint now reads LibraryQueryRequest directly and returns a
LibraryQueryResponse. Open org.jabref.http.dto to the HK2 utilities
module so injection into the new providers works.

* Refine AGENTS.md

* Add initial CHECKLIST.md

* Use _

* Add reformatting hints

* Route LibrariesResource through SrvStateManager.getSearchContext

Make the stand-alone JabRefSrvStateManager build an in-memory SearchContext
on demand so the GUI orchestrator and the stand-alone server can share the
same SearchContext-based code path. Resources no longer instantiate
InMemoryLibrarySearcher directly.

Also extend POST /libraries/query with an optional free-text `query` field
carrying a Search.g4 expression. When present, it takes precedence over the
`dois` / `urls` convenience lists and matches are reported without
doi/url attribution via the new LibraryQueryMatch.forEntry factory.

* Fix formatting

* Rename freeText -> hasSearchQuery in query route

The `query` field carries a Search.g4 expression, not arbitrary free text;
align the variable and test names with that grammar.

* Make SrvStateManager.getSearchContext return SearchContext directly

The lifecycle (LibraryTab on database open, JabRefSrvStateManager on
demand) guarantees a SearchContext exists by the time callers ask for
one, so the Optional wrapper added clutter without value at every call
site (`ifPresent`, `orElseThrow`, `.get()`).

If the invariant is violated, log an error and fall back to a new
NoOpSearchBackend-backed SearchContext that returns empty SearchResults
so the application keeps running instead of crashing. An `assert`
surfaces the bug for developers running with -ea.

* Refine AGENTS.md and add CHECKLIST.md

* Fix typo

* Fix typos and clarify guidance in AGENTS.md

Correct spelling errors, switch lint command fences and the docker formatter command to valid bash, reword the reformatting rule, use straight quotes, and align the standard header block phrasing. Add the missing verb to the StringUtil.isBlank checklist item.

* Expand CHECKLIST.md into a final quality gate

Restructure CHECKLIST.md into code rules, verification commands, and documentation sections so it serves as the post-work quality check. Clarify in AGENTS.md that it is development-time guidance while CHECKLIST.md is the final check.

* Fix submodules

* Fix GroupTreeViewModelTest

* Fix formatting in GroupChange.java

* Remove "query" sub resource

* Fix JBang launcher

* Remove obosolete requirements

* Introduce constants for the "field" query part

* Fix checkstyle

* Address Qodo review comments

- InMemorySearchBackend: isEntryMatched uses per-entry searcher.matches
  instead of a full-library scan; search now sets query.setSearchResults
  so getSearchResults() is not stale after a backend switch
- GsonMessageBodyReader: isReadable declines String/byte[]/InputStream/
  Reader so raw-JSON resources keep using the container readers
- JabRefSrvStateManager: wire the in-memory backend into both backend
  slots instead of a supplier that throws UnsupportedOperationException

* Fix checkstyle

* Rewrite Optional use

* Make exception more explicit but use Optional pattern

* Fix checkstyle

* Cache compiled regexes in BibEntryMatchVisitor

matchRegex compiled a fresh Pattern on every match attempt; a visitor is
created per BibEntry, so scanning a library recompiled the same pattern
once per entry. Reuse compiled patterns via a Guava Cache keyed by
pattern + case mode, with a 15-minute write/access expiry.

Also rewrite Optional handling to .filter()/.ifPresent():
- BibEntryWriter.writeField uses Unchecked.consumer, unwrapping a
  wrapped IOException back into the declared throws clause
- BibEntryMatchVisitor.matchNamedField/matchAnyField use filter().isPresent()

* Use Caffeine instead of Guava cache for compiled regexes

Switch BibEntryMatchVisitor's COMPILED_PATTERNS cache from Guava to
Caffeine, the caching library already used elsewhere in jablib
(CitationStyleCache, FileAnnotationCache). Behavior is unchanged: keyed
by pattern + case mode, 15-minute write/access expiry.

Add an ArchUnit rule (doNotUseGuavaCache) forbidding any dependency on
com.google.common.cache so Caffeine stays the single caching library.

* Fix OpenRewrite

* Reword CHANGELOG.md without techspeak

* Share SearchContext registry between GUI and server state managers

Extract AbstractSrvStateManager holding the per-database SearchContext
map plus get/setSearchContext. Both JabRefGuiStateManager and
JabRefSrvStateManager now extend it instead of each keeping their own
registry and lookup.

JabRefSrvStateManager parses every served library once at startup and
builds an in-memory SearchContext for each in its constructor, so
getSearchContext only ever returns pre-built contexts. The constructor
now takes BibEntryPreferences plus the parsed databases instead of
CliPreferences. getOpenDatabases() returns the held libraries.

subject: Fix CAYW endpoint failing with JavaFX version mismatch (#15736)
body:
* Fix CAYW: force JavaFX 26 and harden Platform.startup error path

afterburner.fx 2.0.0's POM pins javafx-* to version 20. Gradle's
consistent-resolution upgraded most artifacts to 26.0.1, but the
JBang launcher (which resolves purely via Maven) ended up with
javafx.graphics:20 alongside javafx.base:26. Platform.startup then
threw NoClassDefFoundError: javafx/util/FXPermission (removed in
javafx 25), which surfaced as an opaque 500 on /better-bibtex/cayw.

- Strip and re-declare afterburner.fx's javafx-* deps in the Gradle
  dependency-rules so nothing requests javafx 20 transitively.
- Pin javafx-{base,graphics,controls,fxml}:26.0.1 in the JBang
  jabsrv launcher to override afterburner's transitive 20.
- Catch Throwable/IllegalStateException around Platform.startup in
  CAYWResource and translate to a clear 503 response; set the
  `initialized` flag outside the FX lambda so a synchronous startup
  failure no longer risks a hung latch.

* Fix format

body:
* including SearchRxiv integration for SLR and enhancements to citation fetching and PDF downloads.

* Add share functionality for SearchRxiv

* introduce buildStudy method for creating Study instances and enhance share functionality for SearchRxiv

* adding a button for exporting search queries to SearchRxiv and improving layout for validation messages.

* Implement SearchRxivExporter for exporting study search queries in JSON format, adhering to the search-query library's specifications.

* adding export options for search queries in JSON format

* Add unit tests for SearchRxivExporter, verifying file creation and JSON structure for study exports

* Revert unrelated changes, keep only SearchRxiv integration files

* Sync remaining unrelated files with upstream main

* Fix localization

* Fix localization: match tooltip key with FXML

* Fix localization: add missing key and match tooltip with FXML

* Fix CHANGELOG, restore some missing

* Extract noCatalogEnabled to ActionHelper

* Address review comment

* Use FileUtil.getValidFileName for SearchRxiv export filenames

Replace ad-hoc regex-based filename cleaning and arbitrary 20-char
truncation with the existing FileUtil.getValidFileName helper, so the
SearchRxiv exporter follows the same illegal-character handling and
filesystem length limit as the rest of JabRef.

* Clean filename components and add parameterized test

FileUtil.getValidFileName only cleans illegal characters when it also
truncates (length > 255), so short filenames like "IEEE-a/b:c*d-0.json"
slipped through unchanged and broke Path.resolve. Apply
FileNameCleaner.cleanFileName per component, then keep
FileUtil.getValidFileName as a length safeguard. Add a parameterized
test covering illegal chars, blank query fallback, and a regular query.

* Compare exported JSON as a tree in a single assertion

Replace the field-by-field assertions with a single JsonNode tree
equality check against an inline expected document. Tree equality is
order- and whitespace-independent, and any unexpected extra field
(such as "title") fails naturally.

* Use Markdown link in buildJson Javadoc description

Convert the inline HTML link in the buildJson description to Markdown
syntax. The @see tags are kept as HTML since the codebase uniformly
uses HTML there and JEP 467 only guarantees reference-link form for
@see, not inline links.

* Link to SearchRxiv in CHANGELOG entry

* Use @CsvSource textBlock for filename parameterized test

Replace the @MethodSource Stream<Arguments> with @CsvSource using a
text block. Single-quoted values preserve whitespace and special
characters; surrounding spaces are trimmed by the CSV parser, so the
columns can be padded for visual alignment.

* Drop redundant BooleanExpression wrap in noCatalogEnabled

Bindings.createBooleanBinding already returns a BooleanBinding (which
extends BooleanExpression), so wrapping it in BooleanExpression.booleanExpression
is a no-op.

subject: Fix #12271: Integrity checker for year, location, and page numbers in booktitle (#15465)
body:
* Fix #12271: Detect year, country, and page numbers in booktitle

Enhance BooktitleChecker to flag booktitle values that contain:
- A 4-digit year (e.g. 2015)
- A country name (e.g. Norway, Austria, Singapore)
- Explicit page-number patterns (e.g. "pp. 1–10", "pages 3-7")

Add Countries.java with a hard-coded set of all UN-recognised country
names used for the country-presence check.  The set is built as a single
pre-compiled regex alternation so the pattern is compiled only once.

Update BooktitleCheckerTest with parameterised tests covering all three
new integrity rules and the blank-value / valid-value edge cases.

Closes #12271

* Fix Countries.java javadoc to use /// style

* Add missing localization keys for booktitle integrity checks

* Address code review: split BooktitleChecker into focused checkers

- Extract year, country, and page-number checks into separate
  ValueChecker classes (BooktitleContainsYearChecker,
  BooktitleContainsCountryChecker, BooktitleContainsPagesChecker)
  so all three issues in one booktitle are reported independently
- Fix word-boundary regex in country checker: replace [a-z]
  lookarounds with \p{Alnum} so tokens like USA2015 are not
  mis-flagged as locations
- Register all three new checkers in FieldCheckers for BOOKTITLE
- Strengthen tests: use assertEquals with exact expected message
  instead of assertNotEquals(Optional.empty()); add regression
  test for alphanumeric token false-positive

* Fix Checkstyle: use Pattern instead of Predicate<String> for compiled regexes

* Fix Checkstyle: put Pattern.compile on same line as static final declaration

* Retrigger CI

* refactor: use Locale API for country names, add region markers to tests

- Replace hard-coded country list in Countries.java with
  Locale.getISOCountries() + getDisplayCountry() so no manual
  maintenance is needed
- Use //region and //endregion in BooktitleCheckerTest for
  better test organization

* fix: align stream chain to match IntelliJ formatter style

* fix: add space after // in region comments for Checkstyle

* refactor: inline country names into checker, remove Countries class

- Remove separate Countries.java utility class; inline the
  Locale-derived country set directly into
  BooktitleContainsCountryChecker
- Use Locale.of() instead of Locale.Builder (matches existing
  JabRef convention in Language.java)
- Remove javadoc from new checkers to match existing checker
  style (BracketChecker, TitleChecker, YearChecker have none)

* chore: retrigger CI after rebase

* chore: retrigger CI

* fix: use alphanumeric boundary for booktitle year regex

Previously the year regex used digit-only lookarounds, so tokens like
ICML2015 matched the 2015 and triggered a false positive. Switching the
boundary to \p{Alnum} mirrors the country checker and prevents matching
years that are embedded inside larger alphanumeric tokens.

Also adds a regression test and a CHANGELOG entry under [Unreleased].

subject: Fix group filter to use OR semantics for space separated terms (#15350)
body:
* Fix group filter to use OR semantics for space-separated terms

When filtering groups in the side pane, typing multiple space-separated
words (e.g. 'machine learning') now shows groups containing ANY of the
words instead of requiring ALL words to be present.

Implemented by reusing the existing Search.g4 ANTLR grammar. A new
GroupNameFilterVisitor evaluates the parse tree against the group name
string directly, without Lucene. The key change is using anyMatch (OR)
instead of allMatch (AND) for implicit space-separated bare terms.
Complex expressions with parentheses and NOT continue to use AND
between top-level parts.

Explicit AND, OR, NOT and parentheses continue to work as expected.

Closes #12721

This reverts those changes. Only the new code we added should be formatted if needed.

Fixes issue where URLs with fragments (e.g., https://arxiv.org/html/2503.08641v1#bib.bib5)
were not being detected. The cleanIdentifierText() method now strips fragments
and query parameters before identifier parsing.

* Fix CHANGELOG entry format to match origin/main style

and converted to proper JavaDoc comment format.

subject: [Junie]: Filter specific ClassCastException warnings in JavaFX logs (#14666)
body:
* Filter specific ClassCastException warnings in JavaFX logs
 ### What I changed
- Implemented a precise filter for the noisy JavaFX CSS warnings that appear when opening the entry editor.
- Added a JUL filter that drops only those warnings which come from stylesheet processing (JavaFX’s Modena theme or JabRef’s Base.css) and match “Could not resolve …” or “while converting value …” patterns.
- Wired the filter into JabRef’s startup before the SLF4J ↔ tinylog bridge is installed, so the messages never reach tinylog, the console, or the GUI event log.
- Added a small unit test to ensure the filter blocks the targeted messages and allows unrelated warnings through.

### Technical details
- New class: `org.jabref.gui.logging.JavaFxCssLogFilter` (implements `java.util.logging.Filter`).
  - Filters only `Level.WARNING` records whose message both:
    - Mentions stylesheet processing and is tied to either `modena.bss` (JavaFX) or `/org/jabref/gui/Base.css` (JabRef), and
    - Contains either “Could not resolve '…' while resolving lookups …” or “while converting value for '…' …”.
  - Also suppresses attached `ClassCastException`/`IllegalArgumentException` thrown during stylesheet parsing for those sources.
- Hookup: In `Launcher.initLogging()`, before `SLF4JBridgeHandler.install()`:
  - `Logger.getLogger("").setFilter(new JavaFxCssLogFilter());`
- Tests: `JavaFxCssLogFilterTest` validates that CSS conversion/lookup warnings (examples from the issue) are filtered and unrelated warnings pass.

### Why this approach
- The issue arises from JavaFX CSS (cf. JDK-8268657). Filtering at the JUL source avoids over-filtering by class name alone and keeps other `sun.util.*` logs intact.
- It keeps tinylog configuration untouched and avoids writer-specific duplication: both console output and file/event logs are silenced for these specific warnings.
- The match is conservative (requires references to Modena or Base.css and specific message phrases), reducing the risk of hiding useful logs.

### Validation
- `:jabgui:test --tests org.jabref.gui.logging.JavaFxCssLogFilterTest` passes locally.
- The new filter is isolated to GUI startup and does not affect other modules.

### Follow-ups
- If JavaFX fixes the root cause, this filter can remain harmlessly (it matches nothing) or be removed.
- If more CSS warning variants appear, extend the pattern checks in `JavaFxCssLogFilter` accordingly.

* Add export buttons for AI summary and chat

Why:
Quite often, JabRef users would like to share a conversation with AI, or store it in some text file that would be read later without opening JabRef.
However, currently we don't have an option of saving the conversation or summary to some external file.

How:
- Add `MenuButton` with export options to `SummaryShowingComponent.fxml`
  and `AiChatComponent.fxml`.
- Implement `exportMarkdown` method to construct Markdown content
  including the BibTeX source code.
- Implement `exportJson` method using Jackson to generate JSON output
  that adheres to the OpenAI conversation format.
- Add necessary localization keys to `JabRef_en.properties`.
- Update `CHANGELOG.md` to reflect the new feature.

Tags:
ai, export, json, markdown

subject: Fixes #13274: Allow cygwin-paths on Windows (#13297)
body:
* feat: add method to convert Cygwin-style paths to Windows format

Created the method convertCygwinPathToWindows in the FileUtil class. It transforms a file path from Cygwin-style to Windows-style only if the operating system is Windows.

The method follows this logic:
1. If the filePath is null or the OS is not Windows, return it unchanged.
2. If the path starts with /cygdrive/{drive} or /{drive}, replace it with {driveLetterUpperCase}:\ and convert forward slashes to backslashes.

Based on research, the two common Cygwin-style formats are:
- /cygdrive/{drive}/some/path
- /c/some/path

If none of theses patters match, or if the OS is not Windows, the original path is returned.

Additionally, unit tests for this method were added to FileUtilTest class
